Some of the pictures on the walls his hands had handled, and in her strong fancy his lithe form seemed moving the ladder to take them down again, while she, with heart and mind at rest, looked with growing curiosity and interest on her humble helper.

What changes had occurred within a short half-year! She shuddered at the thought that one who was then so instinct with life and happiness could now be dust and nothingness, and she the cause.

Association and conscience were again too powerful. She was becoming nervous and full of a strange unrest, so she concluded to finish her sketch at another time. As she was gathering up her materials she heard someone enter the room.

===Chinese===
卢多尔夫先生去了自己的办公室，克里斯蒂娜目不斜视，径直走上楼上的展厅，立刻试图调动全副心神，来画父亲提议的那幅临摹速写。既然按她所信的，丹尼斯既已不在人世，亦不在别处，她便想把生活重新拾起来，回到他尚未出现之前的样子，权当世上从来没有过这个人。

徒劳之举！在这处熟悉的所在——当年他们正是从这里开始重新布置画店的——万物都在诉说着他的存在。她仿佛看见他泛着红润光采的双颊；他那双深邃热切的眼睛又一次追随着她的一举一动，甚至在她开口之前便领会了她的心意。墙上有几幅画，曾经过他的双手；在她强烈的臆想中，他那矫健敏捷的身影似乎又在挪动梯子，准备把画摘下来，而她自己则心神安宁地站在旁侧，带着日益浓厚的好奇与兴致，打量着这位谦卑的助手。

短短半年之间，竟发生了何等沧桑巨变！一想到昔日那样生机勃勃、满怀喜悦的一个人，如今竟化作尘土与虚无，而祸根偏偏正是自己，她不禁浑身战栗。

触景生情与良心谴责再度排山倒海般袭来。她渐渐心神不宁，涌起一阵莫名的烦乱，于是决定这张速写改天再画完。她正收拾着画具，忽然听见有人走进了屋里。

===Original===
She was in such a morbid, unstrung state that the least thing startled her. But imagine if you can her wonder and terror as she saw Dennis Fleet﻿—the dead and buried, as she fully believed﻿—enter, carrying a picture as of old, and looking as of old, save that he was paler and thinner. Was it an apparition? or, as she had read, had she dwelt so long on this trouble that her mind and imagination were becoming disordered and able to place their wild creations before her as realities?

Her sketching materials fell clattering to the floor, and after one sharp exclamation of alarm she stood as if transfixed, with parted lips and dilated eyes, panting like a frightened bird.

If a sculptor had wished to portray the form and attitude of one startled by the supernatural, never could he have found a more fitting model than Christine at this moment.

As she had been seated a little on one side Dennis had not seen her at first; but, on recognizing her so unexpectedly, he was scarcely less startled than she, and the valuable picture he was carrying nearly met sudden destruction. But he had no such reason as Christine for the continuance of his surprise, and, at once recovering himself, he set the picture against the wall.

This made the illusion still more strange and terrible to Christine. There was the dead before her, doing just as she had been imagining﻿—just what he had done at her bidding months before.

===Chinese===
她本就处在病态而又心弦紧绷的状态，一丁点风吹草动都能惊着她。可试想一下，当她看见丹尼斯·弗利特——那个在她深信不疑的认知里早已死去下葬的人——迈步走了进来，像从前一样捧着一幅画，模样也一如从前，只是脸色更苍白、身形更清癯时，她心中该是何等的惊骇与恐惧！莫非这是一个幽灵？还是像她在书里读到过的那样，因为她长久深陷于这桩心病之中，神智与想象力已经紊乱，竟能把狂乱虚妄的臆造之物化作活生生的实景，呈现在她眼前？

她手中的画具哗啦一声跌落在地，发出一声尖锐的惊呼后，她整个人宛如被钉在原地一般，双唇微张，瞳孔大睁，像一只受惊的飞鸟般急促喘息着。

倘若哪位雕塑家想要刻画一个被超自然幽灵吓呆之人的身姿与神态，世上再也找不出比此刻的克里斯蒂娜更传神的模特了。

由于她坐得略微偏在一侧，丹尼斯起初并未看见她；然而待猝不及防地认出她时，他所受的惊吓几乎并不亚于她，手里捧着的那幅珍贵画作险些当场摔毁。不过，他可不像克里斯蒂娜那样有理由惊魂未定，于是他立刻定下神来，将画作靠墙放好。

这一举动在克里斯蒂娜眼中，更让眼前这幻象显得诡异而可怖。那个死去的人就站在她面前，做着她方才一直幻想的动作——一如几个月前他听从她的吩咐所做过的那样。

===Original===
Dennis was greatly puzzled by her look of alarm and distress. Then he thought that perhaps she feared he would break out in bitter and angry invectives again, and he advanced toward her to assure her of the contrary.

Slowly and instinctively she retreated and put up her hands with a deprecatory gesture.

“She cannot endure the sight of me,” thought he, but at once he said, with dignified courtesy: “Miss Ludolph, you have nothing to fear from me, that you should regard me in that manner. You need not shrink as if from contagion. We can treat each other as courteous strangers, at least.”

“I﻿—I﻿—I﻿—thought you were dead!” she gasped, in a loud whisper.

Dennis’s cheek grew paler than it had been in all his sickness, and then as suddenly became dark with anger. His eyes were terrible in their indignation as he advanced a few paces almost fiercely. She trembled violently and shrunk further away.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯见她神色惊惶惨痛，心中大感不解。继而他转念一想，莫非她是怕自己又要像上回那样劈头盖脸地痛斥她一顿，于是便朝她走近几步，好打消她的顾虑。

她本能地缓缓后退，举起双手，做出恳求他别再靠近的姿态。

“她竟连看我一眼都忍受不了。”他心想，随即却仍保持着不卑不亢的礼数说道：“卢多尔夫小姐，您不必对我心存戒惧，用这样的眼光看着我。您大可不必像躲避瘟疫一般往后缩。我们至少还能像素昧平生、彼此客气的陌生人那样相待。”

“我——我——我——以为你已经死了！”她用一声响亮而急促的气音喘息道。

丹尼斯的脸颊霎时变得比他在整场大病期间还要苍白，旋即又猛地涨得铁青。他眼中燃起骇人的怒火，几乎带着一股凛冽之势朝前逼近了几步。她剧烈地颤抖起来，身子往后缩得更远了。

===Original===
“You thought I was dead?” he asked, sternly.

“Ye‑e‑s,” in the same unnatural whisper.

“What!” he exclaimed, in short and bitter emphasis, “do you mean to say that you never cared even to ask whether I lived or died in my long, weary illness?﻿—that you were so supremely indifferent to my fate that you could not articulate one sentence of inquiry? Surely this is the very sublimity of heartlessness; this is to be callous beyond one’s power of imagination. It seems to me that I would feel as much interest as that in any human being I had once known. If even a dog had licked my hand in goodwill, and afterward I had seen it, wounded or sick, creep off into covert, the next time I passed that way I would step aside to see whether the poor creature had lived or died. But after all the wealth of affection that I lavished upon you, after toiling and almost dying in my vain effort to touch your marble heart, you have not even the humanity to ask if I am above ground!”

The illusion had now passed from Christine’s mind, and with it her alarm. The true state of the case was rapidly dawning upon her, and she was about to speak eagerly; but in his strong indignation he continued, impetuously: “You thought I was dead! The wish probably was father to the thought. My presumption deserved no better fate. But permit me to tell you, though all unbidden, I did not die. With God’s blessing I expect to live to a good old age, and intend that but few years shall pass before my name is as well known and honored as the ancient one of Ludolph;” and he turned on his heel and strode from the room.

===Chinese===
“你以为我死了？”他厉声问道。

“是——的，”她仍旧用那种极不自然的气音答道。

“什么！”他短促而痛切地喝道，“难道你是说，在我那般漫长煎熬的病痛期间，你竟连问一句我是死是活的心思都未曾动过吗？——你对我的生死竟漠不关心到如此地步，连一句打听的话都开不了口？这真是冷酷无情到了极点；这种铁石心肠，简直超出常人所能想象的极限！换作是我，但凡是我曾经相识的人，我也会有这点关切的。哪怕是一条狗，只要曾善意地舔过我的手，后来我见它带着伤病爬进树丛里躲起来，下回再打那儿经过时，我总也会绕过去瞧一眼那可怜的畜生究竟是活下来了还是死了。可我对你倾注了那般深厚无比的爱意，为了打动你那颗大理石般冰冷的心，我辛劳奔命、几近丧命，到头来一切化为泡影，而你竟连问一声我还活没活在人世间这点起码的人性都没有！”

此刻，克里斯蒂娜脑中的幻觉已经消散，惊恐也随之退去。事情的真相正迅速在她心头豁然明朗，她正要急切地开口辩白；然而丹尼斯正值怒火中烧，根本不容她插嘴，激愤地接着说道：“你以为我死了！多半是你心底先盼着如此，才生出这样的念头吧。谁叫我妄自尊大，原也不配有什么好下场。不过请允许我不请自来地告诉你一声：我并没有死。蒙上帝护佑，我还要长命百岁、颐养天年呢，而且用不了几年，我定要让我的名字变得同古老显赫的卢多尔夫家族姓氏一样家喻户晓、受人敬重！”说罢，他猛一转身，大步流星地走出了展厅。

## XLII Baron Ludolph Learns the Truth / 第四十二章 卢多尔夫男爵得知真相

===Original===
With eyes ablaze with excitement, Dennis plunged into the region just before the main line of fire, knowing that there the danger would be greatest. None realized the rapidity of its advance. At the door of a tenement-house he found a pale, thin, half-clad woman tugging at a sewing-machine.

“Madam,” cried Dennis, “you have no time to waste over that burden if you wish to escape.”

“What is the use of escaping without it?” she answered, sullenly. “It is the only way I have of making a living.”

“Give it to me then, and follow as fast as you can.” Shouldering what meant to the poor creature shelter, clothing, and bread, he led the way to the southeast, out of the line of fire. It was a long, hard struggle, but they got through safely.

“How can I ever pay you?” cried the grateful woman.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯双眸因激动而闪闪发光，径直扎进了主火线正前方那片险境——他深知那里的危险最为深重。谁也没有料到火势蔓延得竟如此迅猛。在一幢廉租公寓的门口，他撞见一个面色苍白、身形瘦削、衣衫单薄的妇人，正使劲拖拽着一台缝纫机。

“夫人，”丹尼斯高声喊道，“您若是想逃命，眼下可没工夫顾着这沉东西了！”

“没有它，逃出去又有什么用？”她闷声答道，“这是我糊口度日的唯一指望了。”

“那就把它交给我，您只管尽全力跟紧我！”他将这台对那可怜妇人而言意味着遮风避雨之所、身上衣衫与口中食粮的机器扛上肩头，领着她朝东南方向突围，逃出火线的笼罩。这一路漫长而艰难，但两人总算有惊无险地冲出了重围。

“叫我拿什么报答您才好哇？”妇人感激涕零地喊道。

===Original===
But he did not stay to answer, and now determined to make his way to the west and windward of the fire, as he could then judge better of the chances of its spreading. He thought it safer to go around and back of the flames, as they now seemed much wider, and nearer the south branch of the Chicago River.

He found that he could cross the burned district a little to the southwest, for the small wooden houses were swept so utterly away that there were no heated, blazing ruins to contend with. He also saw that he could do better by making quite a wide circuit, as he thus avoided streets choked by fugitives. Beaching a point near the river on the west side of the fire, he climbed a high pile of lumber, and then discovered to his horror that the fire had caught in several places on the south side, and that the nearest bridges were burning.

To those not familiar with the topography of the city, it should be stated that it is separated by the Chicago River, a slow, narrow stream, into three main divisions, known as the south, the north, and the west side.

By a triumph of engineering, the former mouth of this river at the lake is now its source, the main stream being turned back upon itself, and dividing into two branches at a point a little over half a mile from the lake, one flowing to the southwest into the Illinois, and the other from the northwest into the main stream.

The south division includes all the territory bounded on the east by the lake, on the north by the main river and on the west by the south branch. The north division includes the area bounded on the east by the lake, on the south by the main river, and on the west by the north branch, while the west division embraces all that part of the city west of the two branches. The fire originated in De Koven Street, the southeastern part of the west side, and it was carried steadily to the north and east by an increasing gale. The south side, with all its magnificent buildings, was soon directly in the line of the fire.

===Chinese===
可他顾不上驻足回话，当即决意绕到火场的西侧与上风向去，如此方能更准确地判断火势蔓延的趋向。他思忖，绕到火势后方更稳妥些，因为此时火头已骤然变宽，正逼近芝加哥河（Chicago River）的南支流。

他发现自己可以略向西南斜穿已经烧过的地段——那些低矮的木屋早被扫荡得干干净净，竟连灼热冒烟的残垣断壁也没剩多少，省去了不少阻碍。他还看出，兜个大圈子反而走得更快，因为这样能避开挤满逃难人群的街道。待他在火场西侧靠近河岸的地方站定，爬上一座高高的木料堆放垛时，他骇然发现，南区已有好几处起了火，而距离最近的几座桥梁也正熊熊燃烧。

对于不熟悉芝加哥地形的读者，有必要先交代几句：这座城市被水流平缓而狭窄的芝加哥河分割成三大片区，人称南区、北区与西区。

凭借一项工程壮举，这条河原先在湖畔的入湖口如今已变成它的源头——主干河道被人为倒转流向，在距湖半英里多一点儿的地方分作两道支流，一道向西南流入伊利诺伊河（the Illinois），另一道则自西北汇入主干。

南区囊括东临大湖、北界主干河道、西抵南支流的全部地界；北区涵盖东临大湖、南界主干河道、西抵北支流的区域；而西区则包揽两条支流以西的整片城区。这场大火起于西区东南角的德科文街（De Koven Street），在越刮越猛的大风助长下，一路稳稳向北、向东席卷而来。南区连同其间所有宏伟壮丽的建筑，很快便正正落在了火势吞噬的路径之上。

===Original===
When Dennis saw that the flames had crossed the south branch, and were burning furiously beyond, he knew that the best part of the city was threatened with destruction. He hastened to the Washington Street tunnel, where he found a vast throng, carrying all sorts of burdens, rushing either way. He plunged in with the rest, and soon found himself hustled hither and thither by a surging mass of humanity. A little piping voice that seemed under his feet cried: “O mamma! mamma! Where are you? I’m gettin’ lost.”

“Here I am, my child,” answered a voice some steps in advance and Dennis saw a lady carrying another child; but the rushing tide would not let her wait﻿—all, in the place where they were wedged, being carried right along. Stooping down, he put the little girl on his shoulder where she could see her mother, and so they pressed on. Suddenly, in the very midst of the tunnel, the gas ceased, by reason of the destruction of the works, and utter darkness filled the place.

There was a loud cry of consternation, and then a momentary and dreadful silence, which would have been the preface of a fatal panic, had not Dennis cried out, in a ringing voice, “All keep to the right!”

This cry was taken up and repeated on every hand, and side by side, to right and left, the two living streams of humanity, with steady *tramp! tramp!* rushed past each other.

When they emerged into the glare of the south side Dennis gave the child to its mother and said, “Madam, your only chance is to escape in that direction,” pointing northwest.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯见烈焰已越过南支流，在对岸猛烈燃烧起来，便明白这座城市最繁华的地段已危在旦夕。他急忙赶往华盛顿街（Washington Street）隧道，只见那里人潮汹涌，男男女女扛着各式各样的包袱家什，朝两头奔突。他随众人一道挤了进去，很快便被翻滚的人浪推来搡去、身不由己。脚下仿佛有个细声细气的童音哭喊道：“哦，妈妈！妈妈！你在哪儿呀？我要走丢啦！”

“我在这儿呢，我的孩子！”前头隔着几步远传回一个声音，丹尼斯望见一位女士正抱着另一个孩子；可奔涌的人流根本不容她停步等待——挤在那一段的人全都被裹挟着向前涌动。丹尼斯弯下腰，把小女孩扛上肩头，好让她能看见母亲，就这样簇拥着往前挪动。谁知行至隧道正中，因煤气厂已遭大火毁坏，照明煤气骤然断绝，整条隧道顿时陷入伸手不见五指的漆黑之中。

人群发出一声惊骇的呼喊，紧接着是一阵短暂而骇人的死寂——眼看就要酿成一场致命的踩踏惨祸，幸而丹尼斯用洪亮的声音厉声喝道：“大家全都靠右走！”

这声呼喊立刻被四面八方的人接过去齐声复诵；于是，左右两股活生生的人流并肩而行，伴着整齐沉稳的“咚！咚！”脚步声，彼此擦肩急奔而过。

待众人冲出隧道、重见南区漫天火光之际，丹尼斯将小女孩交还给母亲，指着西北方向说道：“夫人，您眼下唯一的生路就是朝那个方向逃。”

===Original===
He then tried to make his way to the hotel where Professor and Mrs. Leonard were staying, but it was in the midst of an unapproachable sea of fire. If they had not escaped some little time before, they had already perished. He then tried to make his way to the windward toward his own room. His two thousand dollars and all his possessions were there, and the instinct of self-preservation caused him to think it was time to look after his own. But progress was now very difficult. The streets were choked by drays, carriages, furniture, trunks, and every degree and condition of humanity. Besides, his steps were often stayed by thrilling scenes and the need of a helping hand. In order to make his way faster he took a street nearer the fire, from which the people had mostly been driven. As he was hurrying along with his hat drawn over his eyes to avoid the sparks that were driven about like fiery hail, he suddenly heard a piercing shriek. Looking up he saw the figure of a woman at the third story window of a fine mansion that was already burning, though not so rapidly as those in the direct line of the fire. He with a number of others stopped at the sound.

“Who will volunteer with me to save that woman?” cried he.

“Wal, stranger, you can reckon on this old stager for one,” answered a familiar voice.

Dennis turned and recognized his old friend, the Good Samaritan.

“Why, Cronk,” he cried, “don’t you know me? Don’t you remember the young man you saved from starving by suggesting the snow-shovel business?”

“Hello! my young colt. How are you? give us yer hand. But come, don’t let’s stop to talk about snow in this hell of a place with that young filly whinnying up there.”

===Chinese===
随后，他设法赶往伦纳德教授夫妇（Professor and Mrs. Leonard）下榻的旅馆，可那里早已沦为一片无法靠近的火海。倘若他们没在早些时候逃离，此刻怕是已遭不测。接着他又转向迎风方向，试图奔回自己的住处。他那两千美元积蓄和全部家当都留在那里，求生的本能驱使他觉得该去顾全自己的财物了。可眼下行路已举步维艰。街道上挤满了运货平板马车、四轮马车、家具、大皮箱，以及三教九流、各色人等。况且，一路上动人心魄的险景屡屡牵住他的脚步，四处都需要有人搭把手相救。为了加快脚程，他拐进了一条更贴近火场、人群大多已经撤离的街道。他把帽檐压低遮住眼睛，好抵挡如火雹般四下飞溅的火星，正急步赶路时，忽听一声撕心裂肺的尖叫。他抬头望去，只见一幢气派府邸的三楼窗口立着一个女子的身影；那宅子虽不像正对着主火线的房屋那样烧得飞快，却也已燃起大火。他和附近好几个人听见呼救，都停下了脚步。

“谁愿同我一道去救那位女子？”他高声问道。

“成啊，这位老兄，算我这老把式一个！”一个熟悉的嗓音应声答道。

丹尼斯转过身，认出了自己的老朋友——那位“好撒玛利亚人”。

“呀，克朗克，”他叫了起来，“您不认得我了吗？您不记得那个曾险些饿死、多亏您指点去干铲雪营生的年轻人了吗？”

“嗨呀！我的小马驹！你可好啊？快把手伸过来！不过走吧，别在这鬼地方站着唠叨下雪的事儿啦，上头还有匹小母马正嘶鸣求救呢！”

===Original===
“Right!” cried Dennis. “Let us find a ladder and rope; quick﻿—”

At a paint-shop around the corner a ladder was found that reached to the second story, and someone procured a rope.

“A thousand dollars,” cried another familiar voice, “to the man who saves that woman!”

Looking round, Dennis saw the burly form of Mr. Brown, the brewer, his features distorted by agony and fear; then glancing up he discovered in the red glare upon her face that the woman was no other than his daughter. She had come to spend the night with a friend, and, being a sound sleeper, had not escaped with the family.

“Who wants yer thousand dollars?” replied Bill Cronk’s gruff voice. “D’ye s’pose we’d hang out here over the bottomless pit for any such trifle as that? We want to save the gal.”

===Chinese===
“说得对！”丹尼斯喊道，“咱们赶紧找副梯子和一根绳子，快——”

拐角一家油漆铺里找着了一副能够搭上二楼的梯子，又有人寻来了一根绳索。

“一千美元！”另一个熟悉的声音大喊起来，“谁救下那个女人，就给他一千美元！”

丹尼斯回身一看，只见啤酒商布朗先生（Mr. Brown）那敦实粗壮的身影，一张脸因剧痛与惊恐而扭曲变形；再抬头借着映在她脸上的赤红火光一瞧，他这才认出楼上那女子不是别人，正是布朗小姐（Miss Brown）。她原本是来朋友家过夜的，因为睡得太沉，没能跟着这一家人一齐逃出。

“谁稀罕你那一千美元？”比尔·克朗克粗声粗气地顶了回去，“你当俺们悬在这无底深渊上头，是为了图那点儿小钱吗？俺们是要救那姑娘！”

===Original===
Before Cronk had ended his characteristic speech, Dennis was halfway up the ladder. He entered the second story, only to be driven back by fire and smoke.

“A pole of some kind!” he cried.

The thills of a broken-down buggy supplied this, but the flames had already reached Miss Brown. Being a girl of a good deal of nerve and physical courage, however, she tore off her outer clothing with her own hands. Dennis now passed her the rope on the end of the buggy-thill and told her to fasten it to something in the room that would support her weight, and lower herself to the second story. She fastened it, but did not seem to know how to lower herself. Dennis tried the rope, found it would sustain his weight; then, bringing into use an art learned in his college gymnasium, he overhanded rapidly till he stood at Miss Brown’s side. Drawing up the rope he fastened her to it and lowered her to the ladder, where Bill Cronk caught her, and in a moment more she was in her father’s arms, who at once shielded her from exposure with his overcoat. Dennis followed the rope down, and had hardly got away before the building fell in.

===Chinese===
克朗克这番极合他脾性的话还没说完，丹尼斯已爬到了梯子半腰。他翻进二楼，却立刻被烈焰与浓烟逼了回来。

“给我找根长杆子！”他大喊道。

街边一辆散架轻便马车的车辕正好派上了用场，可此时火舌已经舔到了布朗小姐身上。所幸她是个颇有胆识与气力的姑娘，竟亲手撕下了着火的外衣。丹尼斯随即把系在车辕顶端的绳索递到她手边，叮嘱她将绳子拴在屋里某个能承住体重的物件上，再顺着绳子滑降到二楼来。她把绳子系好了，却似乎不知该如何攀绳而下。丹尼斯用力扯了扯绳索，试出能承受自己的分量，便施展出当年在大学体操房练就的身手，双手交替抓绳，飞快地攀了上去，稳稳立在布朗小姐身旁。他把绳索拉上来，替她系牢腰身，缓缓将她缒到梯子上；比尔·克朗克伸手接住，转眼间便把她送进了父亲怀里——布朗先生立刻脱下大衣裹住女儿，替她遮风蔽体。丹尼斯随后顺着绳索滑落地面，脚刚离地没几步，整座楼宇便轰然倒塌。

===Original===
“Is not this Mr. Fleet?” asked Miss Brown.

“Yes.”

“How can we ever repay you?”

“By learning to respect honest men, even though they are not rich, Miss Brown.”

“Did you know who it was when you saved me?”

===Chinese===
“这不是弗利特先生吗？”布朗小姐开口问道。

“正是。”

“我们拿什么报答您才好呢？”

“只要学会敬重诚实正派的人——哪怕他们并不富裕——就够了，布朗小姐。”

“您救我的时候，知道是我吗？”

===Original===
“Yes.”

“Mr. Fleet, I sincerely ask your pardon.”

But before Dennis could reply they were compelled to fly for their lives.

Mr. Brown shouted as he ran, “Call at the house or place of business of Thomas Brown, and the money will be ready.”

But Thomas Brown would have found it hard work to rake a thousand dollars out of the ashes of either place the following day. The riches in which he trusted had taken wings.

===Chinese===
“知道。”

“弗利特先生，我诚恳地向您赔罪。”

丹尼斯还来不及回答，众人便已被迫拔脚奔逃保命。

布朗先生一边狂奔一边高声喊道：“去托马斯·布朗（Thomas Brown）的宅邸或商号走一趟，赏金早已备好！”

然而到了第二天，托马斯·布朗恐怕很难从这两处地方的灰烬里扒出一千美元来。他平日所倚仗的财富，早已长了翅膀飞逝无踪。

===Original===
Cronk and Dennis kept together for a short distance, and the latter saw that his friend had been drinking. Their steps led them near a large liquor-store which a party of men and boys were sacking. One of these, half intoxicated, handed Bill a bottle of whiskey, but as the drover was lifting it to his lips Dennis struck it to the ground. Cronk was in a rage instantly.

“What the —﻿—﻿— did you do that for?” he growled.

“I would do that and more too to save your life. If you get drunk tonight you are a lost man,” answered Dennis, earnestly.

“Who’s a-goin’ ter get drunk, I’d like ter know? You feel yer oats too much tonight. No man or horse can kick over the traces with me;” and he went off in the unreasoning anger of a half-drunken man. But he carried all his generous impulses with him, for a few minutes after, seeing a man lying in a most dangerous position, he ran up and shook him, crying, “I say, stranger, get up, or yer ribs will soon be roasted.”

===Chinese===
克朗克与丹尼斯并肩同行了一小段路，丹尼斯看出这位朋友刚才喝过酒。两人走近一家大酒铺，一群男子和半大孩子正在里头趁火打劫。其中一个半醉的家伙递给比尔一瓶威士忌，可这位牲口贩刚把酒瓶举到嘴边，丹尼斯一抬手便将瓶子打落在地。克朗克登时勃然大怒。

“你他——的干嘛这么做？”他低吼道。

“为了救你的命，别说打掉酒瓶，更狠的事我也做得出来。今夜你要是喝醉了，就彻底没命了！”丹尼斯诚恳地答道。

“我倒要问问，谁要喝醉了？你今晚也太拿自个儿当回事了！甭管是人是马，谁也别想在我这儿尥蹶子耍脾气！”说罢，他便怀着半醉之人那股毫无来由的怒气甩手走了。不过他那副慷慨热心肠依然带在身上——没走几分钟，他瞧见有个人躺在极其危险的地方，便飞奔过去摇晃那人，大喊道：“喂，老兄，快爬起来，不然你的排骨转眼就要烤熟啦！”

===Original===
“Lemme ’lone,” was the maudlin answer. “I’ve had drink ’nuff. ’Tain’t mornin’ yet.”

“Hi, there!” cried a warning voice, and Cronk started back just in time to escape a blazing wall that fell across the street. The stupefied man he had sought to arouse was hopelessly buried. Cronk, having got out of danger, stood and scratched his head, his favorite way of assisting reflection.

“That’s just what that young critter Fleet meant. What a cussed ole mule I was to kick up so! Ten chances to one but it will happen to me afore mornin’. Look here, Bill Cronk, you jist p’int out of this fiery furnace. You know yer failin’, and there’s too long and black a score agin you in t’other world for you to go tonight;” and Bill made a bee line for the west side.

===Chinese===
“别管……我，”那人含糊不清地醉呓道，“我喝够了……还没到天亮呢。”

“嗨，当心！”一声警呼响起，克朗克猛地往后一跃，这才堪堪躲过一面横倒在街心的燃烧高墙。那个被他极力唤醒的醉汉，已然毫无指望地被埋在了火堆之下。克朗克逃出险境后站定身子，挠了挠头——那是他帮助自己动脑筋时最爱做的动作。

“弗利特那小子刚才说的正是这个理儿。我真是个该死的老骡子，竟然那样乱发脾气！十有八九，不等天亮我也得遭这个劫。听着，比尔·克朗克，你赶紧撒丫子逃出这片烈火洪炉吧。你清楚自己的毛病，你在另一个世界里记下的黑账可太长太深了，今晚绝不能就这么去报到！”说罢，比尔便朝西区抄直线狂奔而去。

===Original===
Struggling off to windward through the choked streets for a little distance, Dennis ascended the side stairs of a tall building, in order to get more accurately the bearings of the fire. He now for the first time realized its magnitude, and was appalled. It appeared as if the whole south side must go. At certain points the very heavens seemed on fire. The sparks filled the air like flakes of fiery snow, and great blazing fragments of roofs, and boards from lumber yards, sailed over his head, with the ill-omened glare of meteors. The rush and roar of the wind and flames were like the thunder of Niagara, and to this awful monotone accompaniment was added a Babel of sounds﻿—shrieks, and shouts of human voices, the sharp crash of falling buildings, and ever and anon heavy detonations, as the fire reached explosive material. As he looked down into the white upturned faces in the thronged streets, it seemed to him as if the people might be gathering for the last great day. Above all the uproar, the courthouse bell could be heard, with its heavy, solemn clangor, no longer ringing alarm, but the city’s knell.

But he saw that if he reached his own little room in time to save anything he must hasten. His course lay near the Art Building, the place so thronged with associations to him. An irresistible impulse drew him to it. It was evident that it must soon go, for an immense building to the southwest, on the same block, was burning, and the walls were already swaying.

Suddenly a man rushed past him, and Mr. Ludolph put his pass key in the side door.

“Mr. Ludolph, it is not safe to enter,” said Dennis.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯顶着风向，穿过拥堵的街道挣扎着走了一小段，随后攀上一座高楼的外侧楼梯，好更准确地辨明火势的方位。直到此刻，他才头一回真切意识到这场大火的规模何等骇人，不由得惊骇万状。看样子，整个南区都保不住了。在某些方向，仿佛连苍穹本身也燃起了熊熊烈火。漫天火星宛如炽热的雪片飘落，木料场吹来的大片燃烧屋顶残片与木板从他头顶呼啸飞掠，带着凶兆般的流星火光。狂风与烈焰的奔涌咆哮，犹如尼亚加拉大瀑布的轰雷；在这骇人的低沉轰鸣伴奏之上，又叠起一片宛如巴别塔般的嘈杂声浪——人的尖叫与呐喊、楼宇坍塌的刺耳轰响，以及火焰触及易爆物时接连不断的沉闷爆裂声。他俯瞰拥挤街道上仰望火光的一张张惨白面孔，只觉眼前这群人仿佛正在聚集，迎接末日大审判的那一天。压过这一切喧嚣的，是法院大楼的钟声；它沉重而肃穆地当当作响，敲响的已不再是火警的警报，而是整座城市的丧钟。

但他明白，若想赶在一切化为乌有之前回到自己的小屋抢救些东西，就必须加快脚步。他所经之路正挨着艺术大厦（Art Building）——那个令他心头涌起无数回忆的地方。一股难以抗拒的冲动牵引着他走了过去。明眼人一看便知，这幢楼很快也撑不住了，因为同一街区西南角的一座巨大建筑正在猛烈燃烧，墙壁已经开始摇晃倾斜。

突然，一个人影从他身旁飞奔而过，紧接着卢多尔夫先生（Mr. Ludolph）将一把万能钥匙插进了侧门锁孔。

“卢多尔夫先生，现在进去太危险了！”丹尼斯喊道。

===Original===
“What are you doing here with your ill-omened face?” retorted his old employer, turning toward him a countenance terrible in its expression. As we have seen, anything that threatened Mr. Ludolph’s interests, even that which most men bow before, as sickness and disaster, only awakened his anger; and his face was black with passion and distorted with rage.

The door yielded, and he passed in.

“Come back, quick, Mr. Ludolph, or you are lost!” cried Dennis at the door.

“I will get certain papers, though the heavens fall!” yelled back the infuriated man, with an oath.

Dennis heard an awful rushing sound in the air. He drew his hat over his face as he ran, crouching. Hot bricks rained around him, but fortunately he escaped.

When he turned to look, the Art Building was a crushed and blazing ruin. Sweet girlish faces that had smiled upon him from the walls, beautiful classical faces that had inspired his artist soul, stern Roman faces, that had made the past seem real, the human faces of gods and goddesses that made mythology seem not wholly a myth, and the white marble faces of the statuary, that ever reminded him of Christine, were now all blackened and defaced forever. But not of these he thought, as he shudderingly covered his eyes with his hands to shut out the vision; but of that terrible face that in the darkness had yelled defiance to Heaven.

===Chinese===
“你顶着一张晦气脸在这里干什么？”他的老东家厉声反唇相讥，转过脸来朝他投去一眼，神情凶狠可怖。正如我们先前所见，凡是威胁到卢多尔夫先生利益之事——哪怕是病痛、灾祸这类大多数人也只能低头顺受的变故——只会激起他的怒火；此刻他整张脸因狂怒而发黑，因暴恚而扭曲。

门应声而开，他一头冲了进去。

“快回来，卢多尔夫先生，不然您就没命了！”丹尼斯在门口急切地大喊。

“就算天塌下来，我也要把几份要紧文件拿到手！”暴怒至极的男人咒骂着吼了回来。

丹尼斯忽听半空传来一阵骇人的呼啸巨响。他猫着腰拔腿狂奔，压低帽子护住面庞。滚烫的砖石如雨点般砸落在他四周，好在他侥幸逃过一劫。

待他回身望去，艺术大厦已化作一片坍塌燃烧的废墟。曾从墙上对他微笑的甜美少女面庞，曾激励他艺术灵魂的秀美古典面容，曾让往昔历历在目的冷峻罗马人面孔，曾让神话显得不尽虚幻的诸神面庞，还有总令他想起克里斯蒂娜（Christine）的雪白大理石雕像面容——此刻尽皆焦黑损毁，万劫不复。然而，当他战栗着以双手掩面、试图遮去眼前这一幕时，心头浮现的却并非这些，而是黑暗中那张向天狂吼、桀骜抗命的恐怖面孔。

## XXXI Beguiled / 第三十一章 魅惑

===Original===
Dennis returned to his room greatly perplexed. There was something in Christine’s actions which he could not understand. From the time of their first conversation at Miss Winthrop’s, she had evidently felt and acted differently. If her heart remained cold and untouched, if as yet neither faith nor love had any existence therein, what was the inspiring motive? Why should deep discouragement change suddenly to assured hope?

Then again her manner was equally inexplicable. From that same evening she gave him more encouragement than he had even hoped to receive for months, but yet he made no progress. She seemed to enjoy meeting him, and constantly found opportunity to do so. Her eyes were continually seeking his face, but there was something in her manner in this respect that puzzled him more than anything else. She often seemed looking at his face, rather than at *him*. At first Christine had been furtive and careful in her observations, but as the habit grew upon her, and her interest increased, she would sometimes gaze so steadily that poor Dennis was deeply embarrassed. Becoming conscious of this, she would herself color slightly, and be more careful for a time.

In her eagerness for success, Christine did not realize how dangerous an experiment she was trying. She could not look upon such a face as Dennis Fleet’s, eloquent with that which should never fail to touch a woman’s heart with sympathy, and then forget it when she chose. Moreover, though she knew it not, in addition to her interest in him as an art study, his strong, positive nature affected her cool, negative one most pleasantly. His earnest manifested feeling fell like sunlight on a heart benumbed with cold.

Thus, under the stimulus of his presence, she found that she could paint or sketch to much better purpose than when alone. This knowledge made her rejoice in secret over the opportunity she could now have, as Dennis again assisted her in hanging pictures, and affixing to the walls ornaments of various kinds.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯回到自己房间时，心中困惑极了。克里斯蒂娜的举止中透着一股令他百思不得其解的意味。打从他们在温思罗普小姐府上头一回深谈之后，她的心思和言行便明显判若两人。倘若她的心依旧冰冷而毫无触动，倘若她心中至今既无信仰，也无爱意，那究竟是什么念头在驱使着她？为何深沉的沮丧会骤然化作笃定的希望？

不仅如此，她的态度也同样教人捉摸不透。从那个晚上起，她给予他的鼓励便远胜过他原本指望在几个月里能得到的，可他却依旧寸步未进。她似乎很乐意与他相见，还时常寻由头同他见面。她的目光总是不停地追寻着他的脸庞，然而她看人时的那份神态，却比别的一切都更令他费解。她往往像是在端详他的面容，而非注视着他本人。起初，克里斯蒂娜的观察还颇为隐蔽小心；可随着这习惯日渐养成、兴致愈发浓厚，她有时竟会目不转睛地盯着他瞧，弄得可怜的丹尼斯窘迫不已。待她自己察觉过来，脸颊反倒会微微泛红，往后一阵子便会收敛些许。

急于求成的克里斯蒂娜并未意识到，自己正在尝试一场何等危险的试验。丹尼斯·弗利特生就那样一张面庞，眉宇间洋溢着任哪个女子的心弦都会为之动容的深情，她既看在了眼里，便再也无法随心所欲地将它抹去。况且，连她自己也不曾察觉的是，除了将他视为艺术习作的对象之外，他那刚毅而热忱的性情，也正极其惬意地感染着她那冷淡而消极的心境。他毫不掩饰的真挚情意，犹如一束暖阳，照进了一颗早已被寒霜冻僵的心。

于是，在他身旁那股气息的激发下，她发现自己作画或写生时远比独处时得心应手。这个发现令她暗自窃喜，欣然珍惜起眼前又能同他相处的机会——因为眼下丹尼斯又一次协助她悬挂画作，并在墙上安放各色饰物。

===Original===
Coming to him one morning in the store, she said, “I am going to ask a favor of you again.”

Dennis looked as if she were conferring the greatest of favors. His face always lighted up when she spoke to him.

“It is very kind of you to ask so pleasantly for what you can command,” he said.

“To something of the same effect you answered before, and the result was the disagreeable experience at Miss Brown’s.”

Dennis’s brow contracted a little, but he said, heroically, “I will go to Miss Brown’s again if you wish it.”

===Chinese===
一天早晨，她来到店里走到他跟前，说道：“我又要请你帮个忙了。”

丹尼斯的神情，活像她正赐予自己天大的恩典一般。只要她一开口同他说话，他整张脸总会立刻焕发出光彩。

“您本可以只管吩咐一声，却还这样和颜悦色地相请，真是太厚待我了。”他说道。

“上回你也是这般答复我的，结果却是在布朗小姐家受了那番窝囊气。”

丹尼斯的眉头微微一蹙，随即便慷慨凛然地说道：“只要您愿意，我就是再去一趟布朗小姐家也无妨。”

===Original===
“How self-sacrificing you are!” she replied, with a half-mischievous smile.

“Not as much so as you imagine,” he answered, flushing slightly.

“Well, set your mind at rest on that score. Though not very merciful, as you know, I would put no poor soul through that ordeal again. In this case you will only have to encounter one of the tormentors you met on that occasion, and I will try to vouch for her better behavior.” Then she added, seriously: “I hope you will not think the task beneath you. You do not seem to have much of the foolish pride that stands in the way of so many Americans, and then”﻿—looking at him with a pleading face﻿—“I have so set my heart upon it, and it would be such a disappointment if you were unwilling!”

“You need waste no more ammunition on one ready to surrender at discretion,” he said.

===Chinese===
“你可真是舍己为人啊！”她说着，嘴角噙着一抹略带顽皮的笑意。

“倒也没有您想象的那么高尚。”他答道，脸微微一红。

“好啦，这桩事你尽管放宽心。你也知道，我虽算不上多么仁慈，却也不忍叫哪位可怜人再遭一回那样的折磨。这回你只需应付那次折腾过你的其中一位，而我也会尽量担保她这回安分些。”接着她正色补了一句：“我希望你别觉得这差事委屈了你。你身上似乎并没有许多美国人常犯的那种愚蠢傲气，再者说——”她用一副恳求的神情望着他，“我实在太指望这件事了，你要是不肯，教我该有多失望啊！”

“您不必再对着一个甘愿无条件投降的人耗费弹药了。”他说道。

===Original===
“Very well; then I shall treat you with all the rigors of a prisoner of war. I shall carry you away captive to my new castle on the north side and put you at your old menial task of hanging pictures and decorating in various ways. As eastern sovereigns built their palaces and adorned their cities by the labors of those whom the fortunes of war threw into their hands, so your skill and taste shall be useful to me; and I, your head taskmistress,” she added, with her insinuating smile, “will be ever present to see that there is no idling, nothing but monotonous toil. Had you not better have stood longer in the defensive?”

Dennis held out his hands in mock humility and said: “I am ready for my chains. You shall see with what fortitude I endure my captivity.”

“It is well that you should show it somewhere, for you have not done so in your resistance. But I parole you on your honor, to report at such times as I shall indicate and papa can spare you;” and with a smile and a lingering look that seemed, as before, directed to his face rather than himself, she passed out.

That peculiar look often puzzled him, and at times he would go to a glass and see if there was anything wrong or unusual in his appearance. But now his hopes rose higher than ever. She had been very gracious, certainly, and invited intimate companionship. Dennis felt that she must have read his feelings in his face and manner, and, to his ingenuous nature, any encouragement seemed to promise all he hoped.

===Chinese===
“好极了；既如此，我便要按战俘的严规来处置你了。我要把你押解到我在城北的新城堡里，仍旧派你去做挂画、四处布置装饰的贱役。正如昔日东方君王役使沙场俘获的战败者来修筑宫殿、装点城池一样，你的手艺与品味也正好为我所用；而我这位总监工，”她挂着那抹撩人心弦的微笑接道，“自会时刻守在一旁督阵，绝不许偷懒，只管叫你埋头做这单调无尽的苦工。你先前难道不该多坚守阵地一会儿么？”

丹尼斯佯作谦卑地伸出双手，说道：“我已经准备好戴上锁链了。您且看我以何等坚毅忍受这番囚禁吧。”

“你总算在别处显出几分骨气了，先前抵抗时倒是一点没瞧见。不过，我姑且凭你的荣誉准你假释，待我指定时日、爸爸又能抽调出你的时候，再来听候差遣。”说罢，她嫣然一笑，投下一道绵长的目光——那目光一如既往，仿佛落在他的脸庞上，而非他本人身上——随即转身走了出去。

那道奇特的目光常常令他困惑不已，他时不时会走到镜子前照一照，看看自己仪表上是不是出了什么岔子或怪异之处。可如今，他的希望却比以往任何时候都升得更高。她无疑对他格外垂青，还主动邀他亲密相伴。丹尼斯只觉她必定已从自己的神色与举止中读懂了他的心意；而在他这般纯真坦荡的性情看来，哪怕一星半点的鼓励，也仿佛是在应允他所企盼的一切。

===Original===
For a week after this he scarcely saw her, for she was very busy making preliminary arrangements for the occupation of her new home. But one afternoon she suddenly appeared, and said, with affected severity, “Report tomorrow at nine a.m.”

Dennis bowed humbly. She gave him a pleasant smile over her shoulder, and passed away as quickly as she had come. It seemed like a vision to him, and only a trace of her favorite perfume (which indeed ever seemed more an atmosphere than a perfume) remained as evidence that she had been there.

At five minutes before the time on the following day he appeared at the new Ludolph mansion. From an open window Christine beckoned him to enter, and welcomed him with characteristic words﻿—“In view of your foolish surrender to my power, remember that you have no rights that I am bound to respect.”

“I throw myself on your mercy.”

“I have already told you that I do not possess that trait; so prepare for the worst.”

===Chinese===
这之后一连一个星期，他几乎没见过她的面，因为她正忙着为入住新居打点前期事宜。然而有一天下午，她却突然现身，故意板起面孔说道：“明天上午九点前来报到。”

丹尼斯恭顺地欠身行礼。她回过头朝他惬意一笑，转身离去得同来时一样迅疾。在丹尼斯看来，她方才宛若一场幻影，唯有空气里残存的一缕她最喜爱的幽香（说来那倒更像是一团萦绕不散的气韵，而不单是香水味），证明着她方才确实来过。

次日不到九点差五分，他便出现在了卢多尔夫家的新宅邸门前。克里斯蒂娜从一扇敞开的窗子里朝他招手示意他进来，随后便用她那特有的口吻迎上前去：“既然你糊里糊涂地向我的威权投了降，那就记住，你可没有任何叫我非尊重不可的权利。”

“我只求您大发慈悲。”

“我早就告诉过你，我可没有那份心肠；做好最坏的打算吧。”

===Original===
She was dressed in some light summer fabric, and her rounded arms and neck were partially bare. She looked so white and cool, so self-possessed, and, with all her smiles, so devoid of warm human feeling, that Dennis felt a sudden chill at heart. The ancient fable of the sirens occurred to him. Might she not be luring him on to his own destruction? At times he almost hoped that she loved him; again, something in her manner caused him to doubt everything. But there were not, as in the case of Ulysses and his crew, friendly hands to bind and restrain, or to put wax in his ears, and soon the music of her voice, the strong enchantment of the love she had inspired, banished all thought of prudence. His passion was now becoming a species of intoxication, a continued and feverish excitement, and its influence was unhappy on mind and body. There was no rest, peace, or assurance in it, and the uncertainty, the tantalizing inability to obtain a definite satisfying word, and yet the apparent nearness of the prize, wore upon him. Sometimes, when late at night he sat brooding over his last interview, weighing with the nice scale of a lover’s anxiety her every look and even accent, his own haggard face would startle him.

Then again her influence was not morally good, and his interest declined in everything save what was connected with her.

Conscience at times told him that he was more bent on gaining her love for himself than in winning it for God. He satisfied himself by trying to reason that when he had won her affection his power for good would be greater, and thus, while he ever sought to look and suggest his own love in nameless little ways, he made less and less effort to remind her of a better love than even his. Moreover, she never encouraged any approach to sacred themes, sometimes repelling it decidedly, and so, though he would scarcely acknowledge it, the traitorous fear sprung up, that in speaking of God’s love he might mar his chances of speaking of his own.

In the retirement of his own room, his reveries grew longer, and his prayers shorter and less inspired by faith and earnestness. At the mission school, Susie Winthrop noticed with regret that the lesson was often given in a listless, preoccupied manner; and even the little boys themselves missed something in the teacher once so interesting and animated. From witnessing his manner when with Christine, Miss Winthrop had more than suspected his secret for some time, and she felt at first a genuine sympathy for him, believing his love to be hopeless. From the first she had found Dennis very fascinating, but when she read his secret in his ardent glances toward Christine, she became conscious that her interest was rather greater than passing acquaintance warranted, and, like the good, sensible girl that she was, fought to the death the incipient fancy. At first she felt that he ought to know that Christine was pledged to a future that would render his love vain. But her own feelings made her so exceedingly sensitive that it was impossible to attempt so difficult and delicate a task. Then, as Christine seemed to smile upon him, she said to herself: “After all, what is their plan, but a plan, and to me a very chimerical one? Perhaps Mr. Fleet can give Christine a far better chance of happiness than her father’s ambition. And, after all, these are matters in which no third person can interfere.” So, while remaining as cordial as ever, she prudently managed to see very little of Dennis.

===Chinese===
她身上穿着一袭轻薄的夏衣，圆润的双臂与脖颈半露在外。她看上去是那样洁白、清冷、镇定自若，纵然满面春风，却又透着一股毫无温情的漠然，教丹尼斯心头猛地泛起一阵寒意。古老的塞壬海妖（sirens）寓言蓦地浮上他的心头。她莫非是在将他一步步诱向自己的毁灭？有时他几乎要奢望她是爱自己的；可转眼之间，她神态里的某种东西又令他怀疑起一切。只是，这回不像尤利西斯（Ulysses）与他的船员那样，有友人的双手将他捆绑约束，或往他耳中塞进蜂蜡；转瞬之间，她悦耳的嗓音与她所唤起的强烈爱恋魔力，便将一切审慎之念驱散殆尽。他的一腔痴情如今已化作某种迷醉，成了一场接连不断、发烧般的亢奋，对他身心的影响颇为不佳。这份感情里没有安宁，没有平静，也没有笃定；那悬而未决的煎熬、那近在咫尺却偏偏求而不得一句痛快定论的折磨，日复一日地消耗着他。有时深夜里，他枯坐着反复回味上一次会面，怀着情人特有的焦虑，用精细的天平掂量着她的每一个眼神乃至每一声语调，冷不防瞥见自己那张憔悴的面容，连他自己都会吓上一跳。

不仅如此，她对他的影响在道德上也难言有益；除了与她相干的一切之外，他对世间万事的兴致都在日渐消退。

良心时常警醒他：他一心只想为自己赢得她的芳心，倒胜过为上帝赢得她的归依。他便试着自我宽解，心想等赢得了她的爱慕，自己感化她向善的力量岂不更大；于是，他一面费尽心思在数不清的细微之处流露并暗示着自己的情意，一面却越来越少设法向她提起那份甚至比他的爱更为崇高的爱。更何况，她向来不鼓励谈及任何神圣的字眼，有时甚至会断然拒斥；因此，尽管他几乎不愿承认，心底却还是悄然滋生出一种背信般的怯意——生怕谈起上帝之爱，反倒会断送自己倾诉爱意的机会。

在自己房间的静谧之中，他的出神遐思越来越长，祷告却越来越短，也越来越缺乏虔诚与热忱。在布道学校里，苏茜·温思罗普（Susie Winthrop）惋惜地察觉到，他讲课常常显得心不在焉、敷衍了事；就连那些小男孩们，也觉出这位往日里风趣生动的老师似乎失了点什么。从前亲眼见到丹尼斯与克里斯蒂娜相处时的模样，温思罗普小姐早已揣测出了他的秘密；起初，她打心底里同情他，认定他这份单恋绝无指望。打从初识起，她便觉得丹尼斯颇具魅力，可当她从他望向克里斯蒂娜的炽热目光中读出那桩心事时，才猛然发觉自己对他的关注已远远超出了泛泛之交的分寸；于是，像她这样善良而明理的姑娘会做的那样，她拼死掐灭了心头那缕刚刚萌动的情愫。一开始，她曾觉得应当告诉丹尼斯，克里斯蒂娜早已许下了另一番前程，那前程注定会令他的一片痴心落空。然而，她自己的心绪却令她格外敏感避嫌，实在无法启齿去担承这般艰难又微妙的差事。后来，见克里斯蒂娜似乎也对他笑脸相迎，她便暗自思忖道：“说到底，他们父女的谋划也不过是一纸空谈，在我看来更是荒诞不经得很。也许弗利特先生能给克里斯蒂娜的幸福机会，远胜过她父亲的野心。再者，这本就是旁人无从插手的私事。”于是，她在保持一如既往的热忱之余，又审慎地设法极少与丹尼斯见面。

===Original===
As we have seen, under Christine’s merry and half-bantering words (a style of conversation often assumed with him), even the thought of caution vanished. She led him over the moderately large and partially furnished house. There were women cleaning, and mechanics at work on some of the rooms. As they passed along she explained the nature of the decorations she wished. They consisted largely of rich carvings in wood, and unique frames.

“I wish you to help me design these, and see that they are properly put up, and to superintend the fresco-painters and mechanics in general. Indeed, I think you are more truly my prime-minister than my captive.”

“Not less your captive,” said Dennis, with a flush.

She gave him a bewildering smile, and then studied its effect upon him. He was in Elysium, and his eyes glowed with delight at her presence and the prospect before him. At last she led him into two large apartments on the second floor that opened into each other, and said, “These are my rooms; that yonder is my studio,” as was evident from the large easel with canvas prepared upon it.

They at once had to Dennis all the sacredness of a shrine.

“I intend to make these rooms like two beautiful pictures,” said Christine, “and here shall be the chief display of your taste.”

===Chinese===
正如我们方才所见，在克里斯蒂娜欢快而又半带打趣的言辞（她与他交谈时常常用这种腔调）之下，就连一丝戒心也烟消云散了。她领着他走过这座规模适中、陈设尚未齐全的宅邸。屋里有些妇人在打扫，还有工匠们在几间屋子里施工。他们一路走着，她一路向他说明自己想要的装潢样式。那些装饰多半由精致的木雕与别具一格的画框组成。

“我希望你帮我设计这些式样，盯着工匠们安放妥当，还得替我照管着壁画师和一干手艺人。说真的，与其说你是我的俘虏，倒不如说更像是我的首席大臣。”

“依然是您的俘虏。”丹尼斯涨红了脸说道。

她朝他递去一个令人神魂颠倒的微笑，随即便端详起这笑在他身上激起的反响。他仿佛置身极乐仙境（Elysium），一双眼眸因她的陪伴和眼前的光景而闪耀着狂喜的光芒。最后，她领他走进二楼两间彼此相通的宽敞房间，说道：“这便是我的屋子；那边那间是我的画室。”果不其然，那里正支着一张大画架，上面绷好了待画的画布。

这两间屋子在丹尼斯眼中，顿时有了圣殿般的神圣意味。

“我打算把这两间屋子布置得宛如两幅美妙的画卷，”克里斯蒂娜说道，“而这里，就将是你大展品味的舞台。”

===Original===
Dennis could scarcely believe his ears, or realize that the cold, beautiful girl who a few short months ago did not notice him now voluntarily gave him such opportunities to urge his suit. The success that a man most covets seemed assured, and his soul was intoxicated with delight. He said, “You intimated that my tasks might be menial, but I feel as I imagine a Greek artist must have done, when asked to decorate the temple of a goddess.”

“I think I told you once before that your imagination overshadowed your other faculties.”

Her words recalled the painted girl whom she by a strange coincidence so strongly resembled. To his astonishment he saw the same striking likeness again. Christine was looking at him with the laughing, scornful expression that the German lady bent upon the awkward lover who kneeled at her feet. His face darkened in an instant.

“Have I offended you?” she asked, gently; “I remember now you did not admire that picture.”

“I liked everything about it save the expression of the girl’s face. I think you will also remember that I said that such a face should be put to nobler uses.”

Christine flushed slightly, and for a moment was positively afraid of him. She saw that she must be more careful, for she was dealing with one of quick eye and mind. At the same time her conscience reproached her again. The more she saw of him the more she realized how sincere and earnest he was; how different from ordinary society-men, to whom an unsuccessful suit to a fair lady is a mere annoyance. But she was not one to give up a purpose readily for the sake of conscience or anything else, and certainly not now, when seemingly on the point of success. So she said, with a slight laugh, “Do not compare me to any of those old pagan myths again;” and having thus given a slight reason, or excuse, for her unfortunate expression, she proceeded to beguile him more thoroughly than ever by the subtle witchery of smiles, glances, and words, that might mean everything or nothing.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯简直不敢相信自己的耳朵，也难以置信几个月前还对自己视而不见的那位冷若冰霜的美人，如今竟会主动赐予自己这般一吐衷肠的良机。男子最梦寐以求的圆满似乎已唾手可得，他的灵魂彻底沉醉在狂喜之中。他说道：“您先前暗示说交给我的或许是贱役，可我倒觉得自己宛如一名古希腊艺术家，有幸受邀去装点女神的神庙。”

“我想我以前就对你说过，你的想象力实在盖过了你别的本事。”

她的话令他猛然记起了画中那个与她巧合得惊人相似的少女。令他大吃一惊的是，他此刻竟然又见到了那副酷似的神态。克里斯蒂娜正用那位德国贵族小姐向跪倒在自己脚边的笨拙求爱者投去的那种含笑而轻蔑的神情望着他。他的脸色瞬间阴沉了下来。

“我惹你不快了吗？”她柔声问道，“我倒想起来了，你那时就不太喜欢那幅画。”

“那幅画的其余一切我都喜欢，唯独不喜欢那姑娘脸上的神情。我想您也还记得，我曾说过那样一张脸庞本该用来成就更高尚的意境。”

克里斯蒂娜微微一红，有那么一瞬间，她真真切切地有些怕他了。她看得出往后自己必须更加小心，因为她此刻打交道的，是一个眼光犀利、心思敏锐之人。与此同时，她的良心又一次谴责起她来。越是与他朝夕相处，她便越发意识到他是何等的真诚而笃实；他和寻常交际场中的男子截然不同——对那些人而言，向一位美人求爱不遂不过是桩扫兴的小事罢了。然而，她素来不是个会为了良心或其他什么缘故就轻易放弃既定目的的人，如今眼看大功将成，自然更不会罢手。于是，她轻笑了一声，说道：“别再拿我跟那些古老的异教神话比来比去了；”她就这般轻描淡写地为自己那副不合时宜的神态找了个由头（或者说托辞），随即又凭着微笑、眼波与言语中那股若有似无的魅惑魔力——那些话既仿佛蕴含万千深意，又好似全无所指——更加彻底地将他迷了进去。

===Original===
“You seem to have a study on your easel there,” said Dennis, as they stood together in the studio. “May I see it?”

“No,” said she; “you are to see nothing till you see a triumph in the portrayal of feeling and lifelike earnestness that even your critical eye cannot condemn.”

She justly feared that, should he see her work, he might discover her plan; for, however she might disguise it, something suggesting himself entered into all her studies.

“I hope you will succeed, but doubt it.”

“Why?” she asked, quickly.

“Because we cannot portray what we cannot feel. The stream cannot rise higher than its fountain.” Then he added, with heightened color and some hesitation, “I fear﻿—your heart is still sleeping;” and he watched with deep anxiety how she would take the questioning remark.

===Chinese===
“您那边的画架上似乎放着一幅习作，”他们并肩站在画室里时，丹尼斯说道，“我可以看看吗？”

“不行，”她说，“在拿出一幅无论情感表达还是栩栩如生的真挚神韵都足以令你那双挑剔的眼睛也无可非议的杰作之前，你什么也不准看。”

她担心的不无道理：倘若叫他瞧见了自己的画作，他多半会识破她的计谋；因为不管她如何百般掩饰，她所有习作的笔触之中，都透着几分他的影子。

“我祝愿您能成功，却又不敢确信。”

“为什么？”她急切地追问。

“因为我们无法描摹自己体会不到的情感。溪流岂能高过它的源头。”接着，他脸色涨红，略带迟疑地补了一句：“我只怕——您的心至今仍在沉睡；”他怀着深切的焦虑，紧盯着她会如何回应这句试探之言。

===Original===
At first she flushed almost angrily; but, recovering self-possession in a moment, she threw upon him an arch smile, suggesting all that a lover could wish, and said: “Be careful, Mr. Fleet; you are seeking to penetrate mysteries that we most jealously guard. You know that in the ancient temple there was an inner sanctuary which none might enter.”

“Yes, *one* might,” said Dennis, significantly.

With her long lashes she veiled the dark blue eyes that expressed anything but tender feeling, and yet, so shaded, they appeared as a lover would wish, and in a low tone she answered, “Well, he could not enter when he would, only when permitted.”

She raised her eyes quickly to see the effect; and she did see an effect that she would have given thousands to be able to transfer to canvas.

His face, above all she had ever seen, seemed designed to express feeling, passion; and his wearing life had made it so thin, and his eyes were so large and lustrous, that the spiritual greatly predominated, and she felt as if she could almost see the throbs of the strong, passionate heart.

Apart from her artistic purposes, contact with such warm, intense life had for Christine a growing fascination. She had not realized that in kindling and fanning this flame of honest love to sevenfold power and heat, she might be kindled herself. When, therefore, she saw the face of Dennis Fleet eloquent with the deepest, strongest feeling that human features can portray, another chord than the artistic one was touched, and there was a low, faint thrill of that music which often becomes the sweetest harmony of life.

===Chinese===
起初，她气得脸颊几乎飞起红晕；但转瞬之间她便恢复了镇定，朝他抛去一抹狡黠娇俏的微笑——那笑意里藏着一个情人所能期盼的一切——说道：“小心些，弗利特先生；你这是在试图窥探我们最严加守卫的秘辛呢。你可知道，在古代的神庙里，有一座任何人都不得擅入的内殿圣所。”

“是的，唯有*一人*可以踏入。”丹尼斯意味深长地答道。

她垂下长长的睫毛，遮住那双深蓝色的眼眸——那双眼睛里流露出的绝非温情，可经这睫影一掩，在情人眼中却偏生显得柔情万种——随后她低声答道：“可他也不是想进就能进的，只有得了恩准才行。”

她飞快地抬起眼帘，想看看这番话收效如何；而她确实看到了某种神情——她情愿付出千金，也想能将这番神态描摹到画布上。

他那张面庞，比她平生所见过的任何一张脸都更仿佛是为传达深情与热忱而生的；加之辛劳煎熬的生活使他清瘦至此，一双眸子显得愈发大而澄澈，使得他整个人身上的灵性气息大占上风，她几乎觉得自己连那颗炽热而坚毅的心脏的搏动都能一眼看穿。

抛开她艺术创作的目的不谈，与这样一腔炽热而浓郁的生命气息朝夕相触，对克里斯蒂娜也渐渐生出一种难以言喻的吸引力。她未曾料到，在将这团诚挚爱恋的火焰点燃并扇旺到七倍的炽烈威势之时，她自己也可能会被点燃。因此，当她看见丹尼斯·弗利特的脸庞上焕发出人类容颜所能描摹的最深沉、最强烈的情感时，除了艺术的心弦之外，另一根心弦也被拨动了，隐隐震颤出一缕低微而轻柔的清音——那往往正是人生中最甜美的和弦。

===Original===
“And at some time in the future may I hope to enter?” he asked, tremulously.

She threw him another smile over her shoulder as she turned to her easel﻿—a smile that from a true woman would mean, You may, but which from many would mean nothing, and said, vaguely, “What is life without hope?” and then, as matters were going too fast and far, decisively changed the subject.

Seated at her easel she painted eagerly and rapidly, while he measured the space over and around the fireplace with a view to its ornamentation. She kept the conversation on the general subject of art, and, though Dennis knew it not, every glance at his face was that of a portrait-painter.

===Chinese===
“那么在将来的某一天，我可否盼望踏入其中？”他声音微颤地问道。

她转回画架前，回眸朝他递去又一抹微笑——那抹微笑若出自一位真心女子之口，便是应允“你可以”；可若出自许多女子之口，却什么也不算数——她含糊地说道：“人生若无希望，又还有什么滋味？”随即，见话头进展得太快太远，她便果断岔开了话题。

她坐在画架前，热切而飞快地挥笔画了起来，而他则忙着丈量壁炉上方和四周的尺寸，以便筹划装饰。她始终把谈话维持在艺术这个笼统的话题上；而丹尼斯浑然不觉的是，她每朝他脸上投去的一瞥，都是一位肖像画家的审视目光。

## XLIX Bill Cronk’s Toast / 第四十九章 比尔·克朗克的祝酒词

===Original===
After all, it was a long day to Christine. Tears would start from her eyes at the thought of her father, but she realized that the only thing for her to do was to shroud his memory in a great, forgiving pity, and put it away forever. She could only turn from the mystery of his life and death﻿—the mystery of evil﻿—to Him who taketh away the sin of the world. There was no darkness in that direction. She busied herself with Mrs. Leonard, and the distribution of food to others, till six o’clock, and then she stood near the door to watch till her true knight should appear in his shirtsleeves, with a shovel on his shoulder, and an old burned, tattered felt hat on his head, instead of jewelled crest and heron plume.

Dennis had gone to his work not very hopeful. He knew Christine would be his grateful friend while she lived, and would perhaps even regard him as a brother, but all this might be and still she be unable to respond to his deeper feelings. Moreover, he knew she was Baroness Ludolph, and might be heiress of such titles and estates in Germany as would require that she should go at once to secure them; and so she seemed clearly to pass beyond his sphere.

As he shovelled the hot bricks and cinders hour after hour among other laborers, the distance between himself and the Baroness Ludolph seemed to increase; and when, begrimed and weary, he sat down to eat his dinner of a single sandwich saved from breakfast (for as yet he had no money), the ruins around him were quite in keeping with his feelings. He thought most regretfully of his two thousand dollars and burned picture. The brave, resolute spirit of the morning had deserted him. He did not realize that few men have lived who could be brave and hopeful when weary and hungry, and fewer still, when, in addition, they doubted the favor of the lady of their love.

The work of the afternoon seemed desperately hard and long, but with dogged persistency Dennis held his own with the others till six, and in common with them received his two dollars. Whether Christine would accept the supper he brought or not, he determined to fulfil his promise and bring one. Wearily he trudged off to the west side, in order to find a store. No one who met him would have imagined that this plodding laborer was the artist who the week before had won the prize and title of genius.

===Chinese===
归根结底，这对克里斯蒂娜而言是漫长的一天。一想到父亲，泪水便会夺眶而出，但她心里明白，自己唯一能做的，便是将关于父亲的记忆包裹在深沉而宽宥的悲悯之中，从此尘封。面对他生与死背后的谜团——那罪恶的深渊——她唯有转过身去，仰望那位除去世人罪孽的主。那个方向上没有丝毫黑暗。她跟着伦纳德太太一道忙活，给众人分发食物，一直忙到六点钟，这才站在门旁张望，守候她那位忠诚的骑士归来——他头上戴的不是镶满宝石的盔冠与白鹭羽翎，而是一顶烧焦破烂的旧毡帽；身上只穿着衬衫，肩上扛着一把铁锹。

丹尼斯去上工时，心里并没抱多少指望。他深知克里斯蒂娜此生都会感念他的恩情、将他视作挚友，甚至或许会待他如同兄长，但即便如此，她仍可能无法回应他内心更深沉的情感。况且，他知道她本是卢多尔夫女男爵（Baroness Ludolph），说不定还是德国一笔爵位与庄园的继承人，眼下只怕正须立刻启程回去承继家业；这么一来，她显然便走出了他所身处的天地。

他混在别的苦力中间，一小时接一小时地铲着滚烫的砖石与煤渣，只觉得自己与卢多尔夫女男爵之间的距离越拉越远；待他满身煤灰、疲惫不堪地坐下来吃午饭——仅仅是从早饭里省下来的一块三明治（因为他身上还一分钱也没有）——四周的断壁残垣恰如其分地映照着他凄凉的心境。他十分痛惜那两千美元积蓄和烧毁的画作。清晨那股英勇坚毅的锐气早已抛下他而去。他并不明白，世上罕有人能在又累又饿之时依然勇敢乐观，更少有人在心头还疑心自己未必能得心上人垂青之际，仍能意气风发。

下午的活计显得格外沉重漫长，但丹尼斯凭着一股百折不挠的韧劲，咬牙同大伙儿一道撑到六点，跟众人一样领到了两美元工钱。无论克里斯蒂娜肯不肯收下他带去的晚饭，他都打定主意要信守诺言买回去。他迈着沉重的步子拖往西区，想去寻一家杂货铺。路上凡是与他擦肩而过的人，谁也料想不到，眼前这个步履蹒跚的苦力，竟是上周刚夺得大奖、赢得天才之誉的画家。

===Original===
If he had been purchasing a supper for himself, he would doubtless have been sensible about it; but one that the Baroness Ludolph might share was a different matter. He bought some very rich cake, a can of peaches, a box of sardines, some fruit, and then his money gave out! But, with these incongruous and indigestible articles made up into one large bundle, he started for the church. He had gone but a little way when someone rushed upon him, and little Ernst clasped him round the neck and fairly cried for joy. Sitting on the sidewalk near were the other little Bruders, looking as forlorn and dirty as three motherless children could. Dennis stopped and sat down beside them (for he was too tired to stand), while Ernst told his story﻿—how their mother had left them, and how she had been found so burned that she was recognized only by a ring (which he had) and a bit of the picture preserved under her body. They had been looking ever since to find him, and had slept where they could.

As Ernst sobbingly told his story the other children cried in doleful chorus, and Dennis’s tears fell fast too, as he realized how his humble friend had perished. He remembered her kindness to his mother and little sisters, and his heart acknowledged the claim of these poor little orphans. Prudence whispered, “You cannot afford to burden yourself with all these children,” and pride added, “What a figure you will make in presenting yourself before the Baroness Ludolph with all these children at your heels!” But he put such thoughts resolutely aside, and spoke like a brother; and when one of the children sobbed, “We so hungry!” out came the Baroness Ludolph’s fruit and cake, and nothing remained for Christine but the sardines and peaches, since these could not well be opened in the street. The little Bruders having devoured what seemed to them the ambrosia of the gods, he took the youngest in his arms, Ernst following with the others; and so they slowly made their way to the church where Christine was now anxiously waiting, with many surmises and forebodings at Dennis’s delay.

At last, in the dusk, the little group appeared at the church-door, and she exclaimed, “What has kept you so, Mr. Fleet?”

He determined to put the best face on the situation, and indulge in no heroics, so he said, “You could not expect such a body of infantry as this to march rapidly.”

“What!” she exclaimed, “have you brought all the lost children in the city back with you?”

===Chinese===
若只是给自己买晚饭，丹尼斯自然会精打细算、挑些实在东西；可想到这顿饭卢多尔夫女男爵也会一同分食，情形便大不相同了。他买了些极为甜腻丰厚的蛋糕、一罐桃子、一盒沙丁鱼，还有些水果，紧接着兜里的钱便花了个精光！不过，他还是把这几样彼此毫不相干、又极难消化的吃食打成一个大包袱，动身朝教堂走去。刚走出没多远，忽然有个人影朝他猛扑过来，小恩斯特一把抱住他的脖子，喜极而泣，哭得止都止不住。旁边人行道上坐着布鲁德家另外几个小孩，一个个灰头土脸、孤苦伶仃，恰如三个刚没了娘的孩童所能流露出的全部凄楚模样。丹尼斯停下脚步，在他们身旁坐下（他实在累得站不住了），听恩斯特讲述他们的遭遇——母亲如何离他们而去，后来人们如何寻到她，可她已被烧得面目全非，全靠一枚戒指（此刻正收在恩斯特身上）和压在她身底下幸存的一角画片才辨认出身份。打那以后，几个孩子就一直在四处寻访丹尼斯，走到哪儿睡到哪儿。

听着恩斯特抽噎着诉说经过，其余几个孩子也跟着凄凄惨惨地哭成一团，丹尼斯听明白了这位出身微寒的友人是如何罹难的，泪水也禁不住簌簌落下。他记起她生前对他母亲和小妹妹们的诸多照拂，心底里毫不犹豫地认下了这几个可怜小孤儿的托付。审慎的理智在耳边低语：“你自顾尚且不暇，担不起这满屋子孩子的重负。”骄傲也紧跟着添油加醋：“身后领着这么一长串孩子去见卢多尔夫女男爵，你像什么样子！”然而他毅然将这些念头抛诸脑后，用兄长般的口吻温言宽慰起他们；待其中一个孩子哽咽着喊出“我们好饿”时，原本打算献给卢多尔夫女男爵的水果和蛋糕立刻全拿了出来，留给克里斯蒂娜的便只剩那盒沙丁鱼和那罐桃子——只因这两样东西在大街上实在不好拆开。几个小布鲁德狼吞虎咽地吃完了这顿在他们眼中宛若天界神馔的美餐，丹尼斯便抱起最小的一个，恩斯特带着另外两个跟在后面；一行人就这样慢吞吞地赶往教堂。而此时的克里斯蒂娜正焦灼地守候在那里，见丹尼斯迟迟未归，心头早已生出无数猜疑与不祥的预感。

终于，在暮色苍茫之中，这一小队人影出现在教堂门口，克里斯蒂娜脱口喊道：“弗利特先生，是什么事把您耽搁成这样？”

丹尼斯打定主意要从容撑住场面，半句自诩英勇的话也不肯说，只答道：“您总不能指望这么一支步兵队伍能急行军吧。”

“什么！”她惊叫道，“难道您把全城走失的孩子都给带回来了不成？”

===Original===
“No, only those that fell properly to my care;” and in a few words he told their story.

“And do you, without a cent in the world, mean to assume the burden of these four children?” she asked, in accents of surprise.

He could not see her face, but his heart sank within him, for he thought that to her it would seem quixotic and become another barrier between them; but he answered, firmly: “Yes, till God, who has imposed the burden, removes it, and enables me to place them among friends in a good home. Mrs. Bruder, before she died, wrote to her family in Germany, telling her whole story. Relatives may take the children; if not, some way will be provided.”

“Mr. Fleet, I wonder at you,” was her answer. “Give me that child, and you bring the others.”

He wondered at her as he saw her take the child and imprint a kiss on the sleepy, dirty face; and Ernst, who had been eying her askance, crept timidly nearer when he saw the kiss, and whispered, “Perhaps her old outside heart has been burned away.”

===Chinese===
“没有，只带回了理当归我照管的这几个。”说着，他三言两语把孩子们的遭遇讲了一遍。

“您身无分文，难道还打算一个人扛起这四个孩子的重担吗？”她用惊讶的语气问道。

暮色里他看不清她的神情，心头却往下一沉，暗想在她眼里，这举动只怕显得像堂吉诃德般迂阔可笑，反倒要在两人之间横添一道屏障；可他依然语气坚定地答道：“是的，直到赐下这副重担的上帝亲自将它卸去，使我能把他们安顿到亲友中间，给他们寻个好归宿。布鲁德太太临终前曾给德国的娘家人写信，诉说了自己的全部遭遇。兴许亲戚们会收养这些孩子；若不成，上天总会另辟出路。”

“弗利特先生，您真教我惊叹不已。”她这样答道，“把这个孩子递给我，您领着另外几个进来。”

见她接过孩子，竟在孩子那张困倦而脏兮兮的小脸上轻轻印下一吻，这回轮到丹尼斯对她惊叹不已了；而原本一直斜着眼打量她的恩斯特，一看见这一吻，也怯生生地蹭近了些，压低嗓音嘀咕道：“兴许她外头那颗旧硬心肠已经给大火烧化啦。”

===Original===
They followed to a lobby of the lecture-room, and here she procured a damp towel and proceeded to remove the tear and dust stains from the round and wondering faces of the children. Having restored them to something of their original color, she took them away to supper, saying to Dennis, with a decided nod, “You stay here till I come for you.”

Something in her manner reminded him of the same little autocrat who had ordered him about when they arranged the store together. She soon returned with a basin of water and a towel, saying: “See what a luxury you secure by obeying orders. Now give an account of yourself, as every lady’s knight should on his return. How have you spent the day?”

He could not forbear laughing as he said: “My employment has been almost ludicrously incongruous with the title by which you honor me. I have been shovelling brick and mortar with other laborers.”

“All day?”

“All day.”

Her glance became so tender and wistful that he forgot to wash his hands in looking at her, and felt for the moment as if he could shovel rubbish forever, if such could be his reward.

===Chinese===
他们跟着她来到教堂讲堂外的一间前厅，她拿来一条湿毛巾，动手擦去孩子们那一张张圆嘟嘟、满是惊奇的小脸上的泪痕与尘污。待擦洗得大体恢复了本色，她便领着孩子们去吃晚饭，临走时朝丹尼斯果断地点了点头，吩咐道：“您先待在这儿，等我回来找您。”

她说话时那股神态，让丹尼斯猛然想起了当年两人一道布置画店时那个对他发号施令的小女皇。没过多久，她端着一盆水、拿着一条毛巾走了回来，说道：“瞧瞧，服从命令换来的是何等奢华的享受！现在快老实交代行踪吧，每位贵妇的骑士归来时都该如此。您这一整天是怎么过的？”

丹尼斯忍不住失笑起来，答道：“我今天干的营生，跟您谬赞的这个头衔简直滑稽得格格不入。我跟别的苦力一道，铲了一天碎砖烂泥。”

“一整天？”

“一整天。”

她的目光骤然变得那样温柔而怅惘，叫丹尼斯看得入了神，竟忘了伸手去洗脸，只觉得那一刻哪怕叫他一辈子铲瓦砾垃圾，只要能换得她这样一瞥的犒赏，他也心甘情愿。

===Original===
Seemingly by an effort, she regained her brusque manner, which he did not know was but the mask she was trying to wear, and said, quickly: “What is the matter? Why don’t you wash your face?”

“You told me to give an account of myself,” he retorted, at the same time showing rising color in his dust-begrimed face.

“Well, one of your ability can do two things at once. What have you got in that bundle?”

“You may have forgotten, but I promised to bring you home something that you chose to regard as charity.”

“If I was so ungracious, you ought to have rewarded me by bringing me a broken brick. Will you let me see what you brought?” but without waiting for permission she pounced upon the bundle and dragged out the peaches and sardines.

He, having washed and partially wiped his face, was now able to display more of his embarrassment, and added, apologetically: “That is not all I had. I also bought some cake and fruit, and then my money gave out.”

===Chinese===
她仿佛费了番气力，才勉强重新端起那副唐突利落的架势——丹尼斯并不知晓，那不过是她极力想要戴在脸上的面具——急忙说道：“怎么了？干嘛还不洗脸？”

“是您叫我先交代行踪的呀。”他回敬了一句，满是尘灰的脸膛上却不由自主地泛起一阵红晕。

“哼，像您这么能干的人，本该能一心二用才对。那个包袱里装的是什么？”

“您兴许早就忘了，可我答应过要给您带些东西回来——就是您先前偏要看作施舍的那份东西。”

“要是我真那么不识好歹，您本该赏我一块碎砖头才对。能让我瞧瞧您带了什么回来吗？”话音未落，她也不等他应允，便扑过去抓住包袱，从里头拽出了那罐桃子和那盒沙丁鱼。

丹尼斯此时已经洗了脸，正胡乱擦拭着半干的脸庞，羞赧之情更是藏不住了，只得赔着小心补充道：“原本不止这两样。我还买了些蛋糕和水果，后来手头的钱就花光了。”

===Original===
“And do you mean to say that you have no money left?”

“Not a penny,” he answered, desperately.

“But where are the cake and fruit?”

“Well,” he said, laughingly, “I found the little Bruders famishing on the sidewalk, and they got the best part of your supper.”

“What an escape I have had!” she exclaimed. “Do you think I should have survived the night if I had eaten those strangely assorted dainties, as in honor bound I would have done, since you brought them?” Then with a face of comical severity she turned upon him and said: “Mr. Fleet, you need someone to take care of you. What kind of economy do you call this, sir, especially on the part of one who has burdened himself with four helpless children?”

===Chinese===
“您的意思是说，您眼下身上半文钱也不剩了？”

“一分也没了。”他豁出去似的答道。

“可那蛋糕和水果上哪儿去了？”

“这个嘛，”他笑着说，“我在人行道上撞见小布鲁德一家正饿得发慌，于是您晚饭里最精贵的那部分，就全进他们的肚皮啦。”

“那我可真是逃过一劫！”她惊呼道，“既然是您买回来的，按情理我非吃不可；您当真以为我把那些搭配古怪的佳肴美点吃下肚，还能活过今夜吗？”随后她绷起脸，装出一副滑稽的严肃神情转过头对他说：“弗利特先生，您实在需要有个人来照管照管才行。先生，您这叫什么过日子的章法？更何况您自己肩上还背着四个无依无靠的孩子呢！”

===Original===
There was a mingling of sense and seriousness in her raillery, which he recognized, and he said, with a half-vexed laugh at himself: “Well, really, Miss Ludolph, I suppose that I have not wholly regained my wits since the fire. I throw myself on your mercy.” (The same expression he had used once before. She remembered it, and her face changed instantly.) Turning hastily away to hide her feelings, she said, in a rather husky voice, “When I was a wicked fool, I told you I had none; but I think I am a little changed now.” Then she added, sharply, “Please don’t stand there keeping our friends waiting;” and she led the way into the lecture-room, now filled with tables and hungry people.

Dennis was in a maze, and could scarcely understand her, she was so different from the pensive lady, shrinking from rude contact with the world, that he had expected to meet. He did not realize that there was not a particle of weak sentimentality about her, and that, since now pride was gone, her energetic spirit would make her as truly a leader in scenes like these as in those with which she had been familiar. Much less could he understand that she was hiding a heart brimming over with love to him.

He followed her, however, with much assumed humility. When in the middle of the room, who should meet him squarely but Bill Cronk?

“Hello!” he roared, giving Dennis a slap on his back that startled even the hungry, apathetic people at the tables.

===Chinese===
她这番打趣里夹杂着几分切实的关切与认真，丹尼斯听了出来，便带着几分自嘲又几分懊恼地笑道：“唉，说真的，卢多尔夫小姐，打从那场大火之后，我的神智大概还没完全清醒过来。我唯有仰仗您的慈悲宽宥了。”（这正是他从前曾说过的一句老话。她一眼认了出来，脸色顿时一变。）她慌忙转过身去掩饰心绪，用略带沙哑的嗓音说道：“从前我还是个骄横蠢笨的傻瓜时，曾对您说过我毫无慈悲可言；不过眼下，我想自己多少变了一些。”接着她又脆生生地补了一句：“请别老站在这儿让朋友们久等了。”说罢，她便引路走进了讲堂——此时里面摆满了长桌，挤满了饥肠辘辘的灾民。

丹尼斯如坠五里雾中，简直摸不透她的心思。她与他原以为会见到的那位忧郁沉思、怯于同世俗粗鄙接触的千金小姐，竟判若两人。他尚未悟出，她骨子里原没有半分柔弱伤感的酸气；如今傲慢既已褪尽，她那股蓬勃精干的锐气，便使她在眼下这般乱象之中，同样能像在她昔日熟悉的体面场合里一样，成为当之无愧的主心骨。他更无从知晓，她此刻正强自掩藏着一颗对他爱意满溢的芳心。

尽管如此，他还是装出一副恭顺谦卑的模样跟在她身后。刚走到大厅中央，迎面劈头撞上的不是别人，竟是比尔·克朗克！

“嗨哟！”他吼声如雷，一巴掌重重拍在丹尼斯背上，震得长桌旁那些饿得神情麻木的灾民都吓了一大跳。

===Original===
Dennis was now almost desperate. Glad as he was to see Cronk, he felt that he was gathering around him a company as incongruous as was the supper he had brought home. If Yahcob Bunk or even the red-nosed bartender had appeared, to claim him as brother, he would scarcely have been surprised. He naturally thought that the Baroness Ludolph might hesitate before entering such a circle of intimates. But he was not guilty of the meanness of cutting a humble friend, even though he saw the eyes of Christine resting on him. In his embarrassment, however, he held out the washbasin in his confused effort to shake hands, and said, heartily, “Why, Cronk, I am glad you came safely out of it.”

“Is this gentleman a friend of yours?” asked Christine, with inimitable grace.

“Yes!” said Dennis, firmly, though coloring somewhat. “He once rendered me a great kindness﻿—”

“Well, miss, you bet your money on the right hoss that time,” interrupted Bill. “If I hain’t a friend of his’n, I’d like to know where you’ll find one; though I did kick up like a cussed ole mule when he knocked the bottle out of my hand. Like enough if he hadn’t I wouldn’t be here.”

“Won’t you present me, Mr. Fleet?” said Christine, with an amused twinkle in her eye.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯此刻几乎走投无路了。虽说重逢克朗克令他满心欢喜，可他觉着自己身边凑起来的这帮人，简直跟他买回来的那顿晚饭一样荒唐不搭。这时候即便亚科布·邦克（Yahcob Bunk），甚至那个红鼻子酒保忽然冒出来跟他称兄道弟，他恐怕也不会有半点儿吃惊了。他理所当然地以为，卢多尔夫女男爵面对这样一群至交亲友，难免会有所迟疑却步。不过，尽管他看见克里斯蒂娜的目光正落在自己身上，他也绝干不出冷落寒微故友的卑劣行径。只是在慌乱窘迫之下，他本想伸手同人家相握，递过去的竟是手里端着的洗脸盆，嘴里还热忱地说道：“哟，克朗克，真高兴你平平安安逃出来了！”

“这位先生是您的朋友吗？”克里斯蒂娜问道，风度优雅得无人能及。

“是的！”丹尼斯坚定地答道，脸上虽微有赧色，“他从前曾对我施以大恩——”

“哎哟，小姐，您这回可真是把宝押对骏马了！”比尔抢着插嘴道，“要说我还不算他的朋友，那我倒真想瞧瞧这世上哪儿还能找着他的朋友！虽说当初他一把打掉我手里的酒瓶子时，我确实像头该死的倔骡子似的撒泼踢腾了一通。可多半若不是他那一下，我今儿个也没命站在这儿了。”

“弗利特先生，您不为我们引见一下吗？”克里斯蒂娜说着，眼里闪过一抹忍俊不禁的笑意。

===Original===
“Mr. Cronk,” said Dennis (who had now reached that state of mind when one becomes reckless), “this lady is Miss Ludolph, and, I hope I may venture to add, another friend of mine.”

She at once put out her hand, that seemed like a snowflake in the great horny paw of the drover, and said, “Indeed, Mr. Cronk, I will permit no one to claim stronger friendship to Mr. Fleet than mine.”

“I can take any friend of Mr. Fleet’s to my buzzom at once,” said Bill, speaking figuratively, but Christine instinctively shrank nearer Dennis. In talking with men, Bill used the offhand vernacular of his calling, but when addressing ladies, he evidently thought that a certain style of metaphor bordering on sentiment was the proper thing. But Christine said, “As a friend of Mr. Fleet’s you shall join our party at once;” and she led them to the further end of the room, where at a table sat Dr. Arten, Professor and Mrs. Leonard, Ernst, and the little Bruders, who at the prospect of more eating were wide awake again. After the most hearty greetings they were seated, and she took her place by the side of the little children in order to wait on them. Few more remarkable groups sat down together, even in that time of chaos and deprivation. Professor Leonard was without vest or collar, and sat with coat buttoned tight up to his chin to hide the defect. He had lost his scholarly gold-rimmed spectacles; and a wonderful pair of goggles bestrode his nose in their place. Mrs. Leonard was lost in the folds of an old delaine dress that was a mile too large, and her face looked as if she had assisted actively in an Irish wake. Dr. Arten did the honors at the head of the table in his dress coat and vest that had once been white, though he no longer figured around in red flannel drawers as he had done on the beach. The little round faces of the Bruders seemed as if protruding from animated rag babies, while nothing could dim the glory of Ernst’s great spiritual eyes, as they gratefully and wistfully followed Dennis’s every movement. Cronk was in a very dilapidated and famished state, and endured many and varied tortures in his efforts to be polite while he bolted sandwiches at a rate that threatened famine. Christine still wore the woollen dress she had so hastily donned with Dennis’s assistance on Sunday night, and the marks of the fire were all over it. Around her neck the sparks had burned a hole here and there, through which her white shoulders gleamed. While she was self-possessed and assiduous in her attention to the little children, there was a glow of excitement in her eyes which perhaps Mrs. Leonard understood better than anyone else, though the shrewd old doctor was anything but blind.

Dennis sat next to Christine in shirtsleeves once white, but now, through dust and smoke, of as many colors as Joseph’s coat. He was too weary to eat much, and there was a weight upon his spirits that he could not throw off﻿—the inevitable despondency that follows great fatigue when the mind is not at rest.

===Chinese===
“克朗克先生，”丹尼斯破罐破摔似的豁出去说道，“这位女士是卢多尔夫小姐，而且，我斗胆添上一句，也是我的另一位朋友。”

克里斯蒂娜立刻伸出手去；那只玉手落进牲口贩那双粗厚生茧的大巴掌里，宛如一片轻盈的雪花。她说道：“实在说，克朗克先生，论起同弗利特先生的交情深厚，我可不许旁人居我之先。”

“只要是弗利特先生的朋友，我这就一并拥进心窝子里！”比尔口头上不过是打个比方，克里斯蒂娜却本能地往丹尼斯身边缩了缩。平素同男人们打交道时，比尔开口满嘴都是赶牲口行当里随口甩出来的粗俗土话；可一旦面对淑女说话，他显然自以为必须端出一套近乎风雅抒情的比喻方显体统。克里斯蒂娜倒也大方，接着说道：“既然是弗利特先生的朋友，您这就立刻入我们的席吧。”说着便领着他们走向大厅尽头。那儿的一张桌旁正坐着阿滕医生、伦纳德教授夫妇、恩斯特，还有布鲁德家几个小孩——小家伙们一听说又有得吃，顿时又精神抖擞地醒了过来。一番热络诚挚的寒暄过后，众人纷纷落座，克里斯蒂娜则在几个孩子身旁坐下，好照料他们吃喝。哪怕在那般混乱匮乏的非常时期，也极少能见着比这更奇特的一桌人凑到一块儿。伦纳德教授既没穿马甲也没系硬领，上衣扣子一路紧紧扣到下巴颏，好遮住衣衫不整的窘态；他那副学者气十足的金丝边眼镜也丢了，鼻梁上如今架着一副稀奇古怪的护目镜。伦纳德太太整个人都淹没在一件肥大得没边儿的旧薄呢连衣裙褶皱里，一张脸憔悴得活像刚在一场爱尔兰守灵夜里卖力哭丧了一宿。阿滕医生坐在上首充当东道主，身上穿着他那件燕尾礼服和原先本是白色的马甲——好歹不再像在湖滩上时那样只穿着条红法兰绒衬裤四处走动了。布鲁德家几个孩子圆滚滚的小脸蛋，仿佛是从几个会动的破布娃娃领口里探出来的；唯有恩斯特那双大而富有灵气的眼睛，没有任何东西能遮掩它的光彩，此刻正满怀感激又依恋地追随着丹尼斯的每一个举动。克朗克则是衣衫褴褛、饿得前胸贴后背，他一边以几乎要闹出饥荒的速度狼吞虎咽地吞咽三明治，一边还要拼命挣扎着装出斯文礼貌的派头，直把自己折腾得受尽百般煎熬。克里斯蒂娜身上依然穿着星期日夜里在丹尼斯帮衬下仓促套上的那件羊毛连衣裙，裙子上遍布火烧的痕迹；颈项四周被飞溅的火星烧出好几个小洞，透过破洞隐约可见她雪白的肩头。她一边镇定自若、体贴周到地照应着几个孩子，眼底却闪耀着一团炽热兴奋的光芒——这光芒背后的深意，或许伦纳德太太比谁都心领神会，不过那位精明的老医生也绝非蒙在鼓里的糊涂人。

丹尼斯挨着克里斯蒂娜坐下，身上的衬衫袖子原先也是雪白的，如今经过烟熏尘染，倒变得像《圣经》里约瑟的彩衣一般五颜六色。他实在太累了，吃不下多少东西，心头还压着一块挥之不去的沉甸甸巨石——那是人在极度劳顿而心神又不得安宁之后，无可避免会涌上的意兴阑珊。

===Original===
Christine darted away and brought him a huge mug of hot coffee.

“Really, Miss Ludolph,” he remonstrated, “you should not wait on me in this style.”

“You may well feel honored, sir,” said Mrs. Leonard. “It is not every man that is waited on by a baroness.”

“The trouble with Christine is that she is too grateful,” put in the old doctor.

“Now I should say that was scarcely possible in view of﻿—” commenced the professor, innocently.

“I really hope Miss Ludolph will do nothing more from gratitude,” interrupted Dennis, in a low tone that showed decided annoyance.

===Chinese===
克里斯蒂娜轻快地起身走开，很快给他端来一大马克杯滚烫的咖啡。

“真的，卢多尔夫小姐，”他委婉推辞道，“您不该这样屈尊伺候我。”

“先生，您大可引以为荣啦，”伦纳德太太打趣道，“这世上可不是哪个男人都能有幸让一位女男爵亲自端茶递水的。”

“克里斯蒂娜的毛病呀，就是太懂得感恩图报了。”老医生在一旁插话道。

“照我看，鉴于——此事恐怕还远远谈不上什么‘过分’……”教授一本正经、天真憨直地刚开了个头。

“我倒真切盼望卢多尔夫小姐往后别再单单出于感激而做任何事了。”丹尼斯打断了他的话，嗓音压得很低，却透出显而易见的烦闷与恼意。

===Original===
The doctor and Mrs. Leonard were ready to burst with suppressed amusement, and Cronk, seeing something going on that he did not understand, looked curiously around with a sandwich halfway to his open mouth, while Ernst, believing from Dennis’s tone that he was wronged, turned his great eyes reproachfully from one to another. But Christine was equal to the occasion. Lifting her head and looking round with a free, clear glance she said, “And I say that men who meet this great disaster with courage and fortitude, and hopefully set about retrieving it, possess an inherent nobility such as no king or kaiser could bestow, and, were I twenty times a baroness, I should esteem it an honor to wait upon them.”

A round of applause followed this speech, in which Cronk joined vociferously, and Mrs. Leonard whispered: “Oh, Christine, how beautifully I learn from your face the difference between dignity and pride! That was your same old proud look, changed and glorified into something so much better.”

Dennis also saw her expression, and could not disguise his admiration, but every moment he increasingly felt how desperately hard it would be to give her up, now that she seemed to realize his very ideal of womanhood.

And Cronk, having satisfied the clamors of his appetite, began to be fascinated in his rough way with her grace and beauty. Nudging Dennis he asked in a loud whisper heard by all, which nearly caused Dr. Arten to choke, “The young filly is a German lady, ain’t she?”

Dennis, much embarrassed, nodded assent.

===Chinese===
老医生和伦纳德太太憋着笑，差点儿没当场乐出声来；克朗克瞧出大伙儿之间正暗流涌动着什么他摸不着头脑的玄机，把手里半截三明治停在张开的嘴边，好奇地东张西望；恩斯特却从丹尼斯的语调里以为他受了委屈，便把那双大眼睛满含责备地从一个人身上转到另一个人身上。然而克里斯蒂娜应付这种场面游刃有余。她昂起头，用坦荡明澈的目光环视众人，朗声说道：“依我说，凡是以勇气和坚毅迎战这场浩劫、并满怀希望地着手重整家园的男子，身上都自带一种与生俱来的高贵品格，那是世上任何国王或皇帝（kaiser）都封赏不来的；即便我顶着二十回女男爵的头衔，能服侍这样的男子，我也深以为荣。”

她话音刚落，席间便响起一阵掌声，克朗克拍得尤其震天响；伦纳德太太附在她耳边低声赞叹道：“哦，克里斯蒂娜，从你的神情里，我才何其美好地体悟出尊严与骄傲究竟有何区别！方才那还是你从前那副骄傲的眼神，如今却已脱胎换骨、熠熠生辉，化作一种高尚得多的气度了。”

丹尼斯同样看见了她的神态，钦慕之情溢于言表；然而眼见她此刻几乎完美印证了自己心中理想女性的模样，他每一瞬都愈发痛切地感到，要叫他放手放弃她，该是何等肝肠寸断的煎熬。

至于克朗克，既已安抚了腹中如雷的饥肠，便开始按他那粗豪的性子，为克里斯蒂娜的风姿与美貌所倾倒。他用胳膊肘捅了捅丹尼斯，压低嗓门——却响亮得叫满桌人都听得一清二楚，险些把阿滕医生呛着——问道：“这水灵的小马驹——我是说这位姑娘，是位德国小姐，对不？”

丹尼斯尴尬万分，只得硬着头皮点了点头。

===Original===
A happy thought struck Bill. Though impeded by the weight of an indefinite number of sandwiches, he slowly rose and looked solemnly round on the little group. Dennis trembled, for he feared some dreadful bull on the part of his rough, though well-meaning friend, but Dr. Arten, in a state of intense enjoyment, cried, “Mr. Cronk has the floor.”

Lifting a can of coffee containing about a quart, the drover said impressively, and with an attempt at great stateliness:

“Beautiful ladies and honorable gentlemen here assembled, I would respectfully ask you to drink to a toast in this harmless beverage: *The United States of Ameriky!* When the two great elemental races﻿—the sanguinary Yankee and the phlegmatic German﻿—become one, and, as represented in the blooded team before me” (waving his hand majestically over the heads of Dennis and Christine), “pull in the traces together, how will the ship of state go forward!” and his face disappeared behind his huge flagon of coffee in the deepest pledge. Bill thought he had uttered a very profound and elegant sentiment, but his speech fell like a bombshell in the little company.

“The very spirit of mischief is abroad today,” Dennis groaned. And Christine, with a face like a peony, snatched up the youngest little Bruder, saying, “It is time these sleepy children were in bed;” but the doctor and the Leonards went off again and again in uncontrollable fits of laughter, in which Dennis could not refrain from joining, though he wished the unlucky Cronk a thousand miles away. Bill put down his mug, stared around in a surprised and nonplussed manner, and then said, in a loud whisper, “I say, Fleet, was there any hitch in what I said?”

This set them off again, but Dennis answered good-naturedly, slapping his friend on the shoulder, “Cronk, you would make a man laugh in the face of fate.”

Bill took this as a compliment, and the strange party, thrown together by an event that mingled all classes in the community, broke up and went their several ways.

===Chinese===
一个绝妙的主意忽然涌上比尔的心头。尽管肚子里装了数不清多少个三明治、沉甸甸地坠得慌，他还是慢腾腾地站起身，一脸庄重肃穆地环视着这小桌众人。丹尼斯心里直打颤，生怕这位心地良善却粗鲁率直的朋友冷不丁闹出什么骇人的笑话；可阿滕医生却正瞧得兴味盎然、乐不可支，当即高喊一声：“现在请克朗克先生发言！”

牲口贩高高举起一只装了足有一夸脱（约合近一升）咖啡的铁皮大杯，竭力摆出一副庄严堂皇的架势，字正腔圆地说道：

“在座各位貌美如花的女士、德高望重的绅士，容我恭敬地恳请诸位，以这无伤大雅的佳酿，共同干了这杯祝酒词：*咱美利坚合众国嘞！* 当世间两大元气雄浑的种族——嗜血如狂的扬基佬（比尔误将‘血气热忱’说成了‘嗜血’）与沉静木讷的德意志人——合二为一，就如同我眼前这对血统纯正的良驹双驾一般”（说着，他朝丹尼斯和克里斯蒂娜头顶上威风凛凛地挥了挥大手），“套进同一副挽具里并驾齐驱，咱们的国家航船该当何等乘风破浪、一路向前啊！”说罢，他将一张脸整个埋进那只硕大无比的咖啡大壶后面，仰脖豪饮，以示最深挚的祝愿。比尔自以为刚刚吐露了一番极深邃又极高雅的肺腑高论，谁知他这番话竟宛如一颗炸弹，在小小的聚会中轰然炸响。

“今儿个怕是顽皮捣蛋的精怪满大街乱窜了。”丹尼斯苦笑呻吟道。克里斯蒂娜更是羞得满脸通红，活像一朵盛开的红芍药，一把抱起最小的布鲁德家孩子，急匆匆说道：“这些犯困的小家伙早该上床睡觉去了！”可老医生和伦纳德夫妇却一次又一次控制不住地放声大笑起来，笑得前仰后合，连丹尼斯也忍不住跟着大笑——尽管他心里恨不得把闯了祸的克朗克打发到一千里之外去。比尔放下咖啡杯，一脸愕然困惑地四下张望了一圈，随即便压低嗓门却又响亮地问道：“我说，弗利特，我刚才那话里头，是有哪儿卡壳露怯了吗？”

这一问又把大伙儿逗得哄堂大笑起来，不过丹尼斯还是好脾气地拍了拍朋友的肩膀，答道：“克朗克啊，哪怕命运当头压下来，你也有本事叫人笑出声来。”

比尔把这话当成了赞美；于是，这场因一场打破城中各阶层壁垒的大劫而偶然聚到一块儿的奇特聚会，便就此散席，众人各自道别离去。

## XXXII Bitter Disappointment / 第三十二章 苦涩的失望

===Original===
Dennis went back to the store in a maze of hopes and fears, but hope predominated. Christine could not be indifferent and treat him as she did, if she had a particle of sincerity, and with a lover’s faith he would not believe her false, though he knew her to be so faulty.

“At any rate,” he said to himself, “in this new arrangement I have all the opportunity a man could ask, and if I cannot develop her plainly manifested interest into something more decisive by such companionship, I may as well despair;” and he determined to avail himself of every advantage within his reach in making the most of what he deemed a rare stroke of fortune. His greatly increased salary enabled him to dress with that taste and even elegance so pleasing to a lady’s eye, and he had withal acquired that ease and grace of manner which familiarity with the best society bestows.

It is also well to tell the reader that after some hesitation Dennis had confided his feelings to his mother, and received from her the warmest sympathy. To Ethel Fleet’s unworldly nature, that he should fall in love with and marry his employer’s daughter seemed eminently fitting, with just a spice of beautiful romance. And it was her son’s happiness and Christine’s beauty that she thought of, not Mr. Ludolph’s money. In truth, such was her admiration for her son, she felt that with all her wealth the young lady would receive a greater honor than she conferred. Though Dennis wrote with the partiality of a lover, he could not so portray Christine’s character but that his mother felt the deepest anxiety, and often sighed in sad foreboding of serious trouble in the future.

From Mrs. Fleet’s knowledge of her son’s passion, Christine, though she knew it not, received another advantage of incalculable value. Dennis had painted an excellent little cabinet likeness of her, and sent it to his mother. In the quiet of the night she would sit down before that picture, and by her strong imagination summon her ideal of Christine, and then lead her directly to Christ, as parents brought their children of old. Could such prayers and faith be in vain? Faith is often sorely tried in this world, but never tried in vain.

Day after day Dennis went to Mr. Ludolph’s new home during the morning hours, and Christine’s spell worked with bewildering and increasing power. While she tortured him with many doubts and fears, his hope grew to be almost a certainty that he had at last made a place for himself in her heart. Sometimes the whole story of his love trembled on his lips, but she never permitted its utterance. That she determined should be reserved for the climax. He usually met her alone, but noticed that in the presence of others she was cool and undemonstrative. Mr. Ludolph rarely saw them together, and, when he did, there was nothing in his daughter’s manner to awaken suspicion. This perfectly acted indifference in the presence of others, and equally well acted regard when alone, often puzzled Dennis sorely. But at last he concluded: “She is wiser than I. She knows that I am in no condition now to make proposals for her hand; therefore it is better that there should be no recognized understanding between us;” and he resolved to be as prudent as she. Then again she would so awaken his jealousy and fears that he would feel that he must know his fate—that anything was better than such torturing uncertainty.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯回到店里时，心里交织着重重希望与忧惧，宛如坠入迷宫，但终究还是希望占了上风。只要克里斯蒂娜还有一丝诚意，她既对他如此相待，就不可能对他毫无情意；怀着一颗恋人的赤诚之心，哪怕明知她有诸多过失与瑕疵，他也不愿相信她虚情假意。

“不管怎样，”他暗自思忖，“在这番新安排下，男子所能奢求的一切机会我都已握在手中；倘若凭着这样的朝夕相伴，我还不能把她那显而易见的兴致培育成更笃定的情意，那我干脆趁早绝望算了。”于是，他下定决心要善用身边的一切有利条件，将这桩在他看来千载难逢的好运发挥到极致。大幅上涨的薪水使他得以衣着得体，甚至颇具几分令淑女赏心悦目的雅致风度；况且，常与上流社会周旋往来，也早已赋予他那份从容大方、优雅自然的举止神态。

这里还有必要向读者交代一番：经过几番踌躇之后，丹尼斯已将自己的心事向母亲吐露，并得到了她最热烈真挚的体恤与支持。在埃塞尔·弗利特那颗不染尘俗的心灵看来，儿子爱上雇主的千金并结为连理，实乃再合适不过的良缘，其中还平添了几分动人的浪漫情调。她心中惦念的只是儿子的幸福与克里斯蒂娜的貌美，绝非卢多尔夫先生的家财。说实在的，她是那般推崇自己的儿子，以致觉得那位小姐纵有万贯家资，嫁与丹尼斯也仍是她受荣多于赐荣。不过，丹尼斯写信时虽带着情人的偏爱，却仍无法把克里斯蒂娜的性情掩饰得天衣无缝，令母亲读后不由得深感忧虑，常常暗自叹息，隐隐预感到日后恐将生出大患。

弗利特太太知晓儿子的痴情后，克里斯蒂娜虽然浑然不觉，却由此获得了另一份价值不可估量的恩泽。丹尼斯曾为她画过一幅极传神的小型肖像画，寄给了母亲。每逢夜深人静，弗利特太太便会端坐在这幅画像前，凭着敏锐而深切的想象，在心底唤出她心目中理想的克里斯蒂娜，随后像古时候父母携儿女来到主前那样，将她径直领到基督（Christ）面前祈祷。这般虔诚的祷告与信心，难道会白白落空么？信心在世间固然常常备受严酷的试炼，却绝不会徒劳无功。

日复一日，丹尼斯趁着上午的时光前往卢多尔夫先生的新宅，而克里斯蒂娜的魔力也愈演愈烈，令他晕头转向、越陷越深。尽管她用种种疑虑与惊惧折磨着他，他心中的希望却渐渐长成了几近笃定的信念，以为自己终于在她芳心深处占得了一席之地。好几次，一腔深情的话语已颤巍巍地涌到了他的嘴边，她却总有办法不让他说出口。她打定主意，要把这一幕留待最后的顶点。两人相见时多半只有彼此在场，可他也留意到，一当有旁人在侧，她便显得冷淡而克制。卢多尔夫先生很少撞见他们同处一室，即便偶尔碰上，女儿的神态中也找不出一丝足以起疑的破绽。人前这般演得天衣无缝的漠然，与独处时那般同样演得逼真动人的关切，时常把丹尼斯搅得苦恼不堪。但到头来他还是自己想通了：“她比我更有远见。她知道我眼下尚无资格向她求婚，因此，我们之间眼下最好还是不要有任何公开的默契。”于是他也决心像她一样审慎行事。可没过多久，她又会撩拨起他强烈的嫉妒与惶恐，叫他觉得自己非得立刻探明命运的归宿不可——哪怕最坏的结局，也强过这般活受罪似的悬而未决。

===Original===
As for Christine, two processes were going on in her mind—one that she recognized, and one that she did not.

Her artistic aims were clear and definite. In the first place she meant perfectly to master the human face as it expressed emotions, especially such as were of a tender nature; and in the second place she intended to paint a picture that in itself would make her famous. She chose a most difficult and delicate subject—of the character she had ever failed in—a declaration of love.

When Dennis began to work again in her presence, the picture was well advanced.

In a grand old hall, whose sides were decorated with armor and weapons, a young man stood pleading his cause with a lady whose hand he held. The young girl’s face was so averted that only a beautiful profile was visible, but her form and attitude were grace itself. The lovers stood in an angle of the hall near an open window, through which was seen a fine landscape, a picture within a picture. But Christine meant to concentrate all her power and skill on the young knight’s face. This should be eloquent with all the feeling and passion that the human face could express, and she would insure its truthfulness to life by copying life itself—the reality. Dennis Fleet was the human victim that she was offering on the altar of her ambition.

Much of the picture was merely in outline, but she finished the form and features of the suppliant in all save the expression, and this she meant to paint from his face whenever she was in the right mood and could bring matters to a crisis.

===Chinese===
至于克里斯蒂娜，她的心底正同时经历着两重演变——一重她心知肚明，另一重她自己却浑然未觉。

她的艺术抱负清晰而明确。首先，她立志要彻底掌握人脸在流露情感时的神态变化，尤其是那些温柔缠绵的情愫；其次，她要画出一幅足以令自己一举成名的杰作。她挑选了一个极其棘手而又微妙的题材——恰恰是她向来屡屡挫败的那一类——倾诉爱意。

当丹尼斯重新开始在她眼皮底下干活时，这幅画的进度已相当可观。

画中是一座气派古雅的大厅，两侧墙壁陈列着盔甲与兵器，一位青年男子正握着一名贵妇的纤手，恳切地倾诉衷肠。那位少女将脸微偏过去，只露出一道秀美的侧面轮廓，然而她的身姿与仪态却尽显优雅风华。这对恋人立于大厅一隅一扇敞开的窗边，窗外映入一片秀丽的景致，宛若画中有画。然而克里斯蒂娜打算把全部心力与技艺都倾注在这位年轻骑士的面庞上。这张脸必须淋漓尽致地诉说出人类容颜所能传达的一切深情与炽烈，而她要通过直接临摹活生生的现实本身，来确保画面如实传神。丹尼斯·弗利特，便是她献在自己野心祭坛上的活祭品。

画作的大部分目前还仅具轮廓，但她已将那位苦苦恳求者的身形与五官描绘完成，唯独留下面部神情未画——她打算等自己兴致恰到好处、又能将事态推向紧要关头时，直接对着他的脸把这神情描摹下来。

===Original===
After he had been coming to the house two or three times a week for nearly a month she felt that she was ready for the final scene, and yet she dreaded it, she had staked so much hope upon it. It also provoked her to find that she was really afraid of him. His was such a strong, sincere nature, that she felt increasingly the wrong of trifling with it.
