“可我说你必须得说。你难道不知道我是卢多尔夫小姐吗？”

“不管你怎么惩罚我，我都不怕，”小家伙说着哭了起来，“我就是不说。”

“你为什么不肯说呢，好孩子？”克里斯蒂娜狡黠地换上一副软语诱哄的腔调说道。

惊惶失措、晕头转向的男孩还没反应过来，便已落入了圈套，抽噎着脱口而出：“因为弗利特先生不准我说，哪怕拼了性命，我也绝不违抗他的话。”

一阵惊讶的神色，继而一抹舒展的笑意，悄然爬上了年轻姑娘的脸庞——既是为了这礼物，也是为了这送信人，更是为了那位送礼之人。这实在是一段清新而出人意料的小插曲，打破了整日的沉闷——恰如一颗甜美多汁的草莓，令她干渴的唇齿倍感惬意。

“既然弗利特先生嘱咐过你别说，那你就不必告诉我啦。”她柔声安抚道。

===Original===
The boy saw the smile, and in a moment realized that he had been tricked out of the forbidden knowledge.

His little face glowed with honest indignation, and looking straight at Miss Ludolph, with his great eyes flashing through the tears, he said, “You stole that from me.”

Even she colored a little and bit her lip under the merited charge. But all this made him all the more interesting as an art study, and she was now sketching away rapidly. She coolly replied, however, “You don’t know the world very well yet, my little man.”

The boy said nothing, but stood regarding her with his unnaturally large eyes filled with anger, reproach, and wonder.

“Oh,” thought Christine, “if I could only paint that expression!”

“You seem a great friend of Mr. Fleet,” she said, studying and sketching him as if he had been an inanimate object.

===Chinese===
男孩看见她脸上的笑意，刹那间明白过来，自己守口如瓶的秘密竟被人用计套走了。

他那张小脸因坦荡的义愤而涨得通红，一双泪光闪闪的大眼睛直直盯着卢多尔夫小姐，说道：“这是你从我这儿偷走的。”

被他这样当面一斥，就连她也微微红了脸，下意识地咬了咬嘴唇。可这一幕反倒让他在画家的眼里愈发耐人寻味，她此刻正运笔如飞地勾勒着他的神态。不过嘴上，她还是故作镇定地回敬道：“小家伙，你还不太懂这世道呢。”

男孩没有搭腔，只是站在那里注视着她，他那双异乎寻常的大眼睛里，盛满了愤怒、责备与惊愕。

“哦，”克里斯蒂娜暗想，“要是能把这副神情画进画里该多好！”

“你似乎和弗利特先生很是交好啊，”她一边说，一边端详并描摹着他，仿佛他只是一件没有生命的静物模特。

===Original===
The boy made no answer.

“Perhaps you do not know that I am a friend﻿—friendly,” she added, correcting herself, “to Mr. Fleet also.”

“Mr. Fleet never likes to have his friends do wrong,” said the boy, doubtingly.

Again she colored a little, for Ernst’s pure and reproachful face made her feel that she had done a mean thing, but she laughed said: “You see I am not in his mission class, and have never had the instruction that you have. But, after all, why do you think Mr. Fleet better than other people?”

“By what he does.”

“That is a fair test; what has he done?”

===Chinese===
男孩依旧沉默不语。

“兴许你还不知道，我也是弗利特先生的朋友——呃，算得上是友善的熟人吧，”她随即改口补了一句。

“弗利特先生从不喜欢他的朋友们做错事，”男孩将信将疑地说道。

她的脸庞又微微泛起一抹红晕，因为恩斯特那张纯洁而又带着谴责意味的脸，令她觉得自己方才确实干了件卑劣的事；但她还是笑了一声，说道：“你看，我又没上过他的布道班，从未受过你所受的那番教导嘛。不过话说回来，你凭什么觉得弗利特先生比旁人都强呢？”

“凭他所做的事。”

“这倒是个公道的检验法子；那他究竟做过些什么？”

===Original===
“He saved us all from starving, and worse than starving.”

Then with feminine tact she drew from him his story, and it was told with deep feeling and the natural pathos of childhood, and his gratitude caused him to dwell with a simple eloquence on the part Dennis had taken, while his rich and loved German accent made it all the more interesting to Christine. She dropped her pencil, and, when he finished, her eyes, that were seldom moistened by the dew of sympathy, were wet.

“Goodbye, my child,” she said, in a voice so kind and sweet that it seemed as if another person had spoken. “You shall come again, and then I shall finish my sketch. When I get well I shall go to see your father’s picture. Do not be afraid; neither you nor Mr. Fleet will fare the worse for the strawberries, and you may tell him that they have done me much good.”

===Chinese===
“他救了我们全家，免得我们活活饿死，甚至免于落到比饿死更惨的地步。”

于是，她凭借女性特有的巧妙手腕，一步步套出了他的身世故事。男孩怀着深挚的情感讲述着，字字句句流露出孩童天然的凄恻与真挚；那份发自肺腑的感激，使他以质朴而动人的口才细细道出丹尼斯在其中所施的援手，而他那口醇厚又令她倍感亲切的德语口音，更让克里斯蒂娜听得入神。她放下了手中的画笔；待他讲完时，她那双极少被同情的露水润湿的眼眸，竟也微微湿润了。

“再见吧，孩子，”她说道，那嗓音如此温婉甜美，简直像是换了一个人在说话，“改天你还要再来一趟，到时我再把这幅素描画完。等我病好了，我就去看看你父亲画的那幅画。别害怕，无论你还是弗利特先生，都不会因为这篮草莓而受到半点苛责；你可以替我转告他，这草莓叫我受用极了。”

===Original===
When Dennis, wondering at Ernst’s long absence, heard from him his story, his mind was in a strange tumult, and yet the result of his effort seemed favorable. But he learned more fully than ever that Christine was not perfect, and that her faultless beauty and taste were but the fair mask of a deformed spirit. But he dwelt in hope on the feeling she had shown at Ernst’s story.

“She seemed to have two hearts,” said the boy﻿—“a good, kind one way inside the cold, hard outside one.”

“That is about the truth,” thought Dennis. “Good night, Ernst. I don’t blame you, my boy, for you did the best you could.”

He had done better than Dennis knew.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯原还纳闷恩斯特为何去了这许久，及至听完他带回来的经过，心头顿觉一阵奇异的翻涌，好在自己的一番心意似乎颇有成效。不过，他也比以往任何时候都更清楚地认识到，克里斯蒂娜并非十全十美，她那无懈可击的美貌与雅致品位，不过是一副掩盖着畸形灵魂的动人面具。然而，想到她在听完恩斯特的讲述后所流露出的那份真情，他又忍不住心怀希望。

“她倒像长了两颗心似的，”男孩说道——“在外面那颗冰冷坚硬的心里面，还藏着一颗善良温软的心呢。”

“这话说得八九不离十，”丹尼斯暗自思忖。“晚安，恩斯特。我不怪你，好孩子，你已经尽了最大的力气了。”

其实他所成就的，远比丹尼斯所知道的还要更好。

## XVIII Miss Ludolph Makes a Discovery / 第十八章 卢多尔夫小姐有所发现

===Original===
Several hours were measured off by the clock of a neighboring steeple before Dennis’s excited mind was sufficiently calm to permit sleep, and even then he often started up from some fantastic dream in which the Bruders and Mr. and Miss Ludolph acted strange parts. At last he seemed to hear exquisite music. As the song rose and fell, it thrilled him with delight. Suddenly it appeared to break into a thousand pieces, and fall scattering on the ground, like a broken string of pearls, and this musical trash, as it were, awoke him. The sun was shining brightly into the room, and all the air seemed vibrating with sweet sounds. He started up and realized that he had greatly overslept. Much vexed, he began to dress in haste, when he was startled by a brilliant prelude on the piano, and a voice of wonderful power and sweetness struck into an air that he had never heard before. Soon the whole building was resonant with music, and Dennis stood spellbound till the strange, rich sounds died away, as before, in a few instrumental notes that had seemed in his dream like the song breaking into glittering fragments.

“It must be Miss Ludolph,” thought Dennis. “And can she sing like that? What an angel true faith would make of her! Oh, how could I oversleep so!” And he dressed in breathless haste. In going down to the second floor, he found a piano open and new music upon it, which Miss Ludolph had evidently been trying; but she was not there. Yet a peculiar delicate perfume which the young lady always used pervaded the place, even as her song had seemed to pulsate through the air after it had ceased. She could not be far off. Stepping to a picture showroom over the front door, Dennis found her sitting quietly before a large painting, sketching one of the figures in it.

“I learned from my father that you were a very early riser,” she said, looking up for a moment, and then resuming her work. “I fear there is some mistake about it. If we are ever to get through rearranging the store you will have to curtail your morning naps.”

“I most sincerely beg your pardon. I never overslept so before. But I was out late last night, and passed through a most painful scene, that so disturbed me that I could not sleep till nearly morning, and I find to my great vexation that I have overslept. I promise you it shall not happen again.”

===Chinese===
附近教堂尖塔上的钟敲过了好几个钟点，丹尼斯兴奋纷乱的心绪才渐渐平复下来，得以入眠；即便睡着了，他也频频从一个个荒诞离奇的梦境中惊醒——梦里布鲁德一家与卢多尔夫父女正扮演着种种古怪的角色。到后来，他仿佛听见了绝妙的乐声。那歌声起落婉转，令他满心欢喜、激动不已。忽然之间，乐声似乎碎作千片万瓣，像一串断了线的珍珠般四散跌落地面，而这串仿佛碎落成珠玉残屑的乐声，竟将他惊醒了。阳光明晃晃地照进屋里，整个屋子的空气似乎仍在甜美的余韵中微微震颤。他猛地坐起身，这才发觉自己竟大大地睡过了头。他懊恼万分，正手忙脚乱地穿衣，忽被一阵绚丽夺目的钢琴前奏吓了一跳，紧接着，一个浑厚而又甜美得惊人的歌喉唱起了一支他从未听过的曲调。不一会儿，整座大楼都回荡着这片乐声，丹尼斯听得如痴如醉，直到那奇异丰润的嗓音像方才梦里一样，收束在几声晶莹零落、仿佛歌声碎裂成闪光碎片的琴音之中，这才袅袅散去。

“这一定是卢多尔夫小姐，”丹尼斯暗想，“她竟能唱得这样好？若是有了真信仰，她该会成为何等样的天使啊！哎呀，我怎么竟会睡过头到这步田地！”他屏息敛气，飞快穿戴妥当。下到二楼时，只见一架钢琴敞开着，琴谱架上放着新曲谱，显然正是卢多尔夫小姐方才试弹过的；但她人却不在这里。不过，这位年轻小姐惯用的那股清雅独特的幽香依然弥漫在空气中，恰似她的歌声虽已止歇，却仍在空气里久久搏动不散。她定然离得不远。丹尼斯迈步走向正门上方的画室展厅，果然见她正静静坐在一幅大画前，临摹画中一个人物的素描。

“我听家父说，您一向起得极早，”她抬眼望了他一下，随即便低下头继续画道，“只怕这话有些失实吧。咱们若还指望把店里的陈设重新理顺，您往后可就得把早上的回笼觉减一减了。”

“实在万分抱歉，请您原谅。我以前从没这样睡过头。只是昨晚我在外头待到很晚，经历了一桩极痛心的事，心里扰乱得厉害，直折腾到快天亮才合眼，结果竟睡过了头，我自己也懊恼得紧。我向您保证，绝不会再有下次了。”

===Original===
“I am not sure of that, if you are out late in Chicago, and passing through painful scenes. I should say that this city was a peculiarly bad place for a young man to be out late in.”

“It was an experience wholly unexpected to me, and I hope it may never occur again. It was a scene of trouble that I had no hand in making, but which even humanity would not permit me to leave at once.”

“Not a scene of measles or smallpox, I hope. I am told that your mission people are indulging in these things most of the time. You have not been exposed to any contagious disease?”

“I assure you I have not.”

“Very well; be ready to assist me tomorrow morning, for we have no slight task before us, and I wish to complete it as soon as possible. I shall be here at half-past six, and do not promise to sing you awake every morning. Were you not a little startled to hear such unwonted sounds echoing through the prosaic old store?”

===Chinese===
“那可未必，既然您在芝加哥深更半夜还在外头跑，又尽碰上些痛心的场面。依我看，年轻男子深更半夜在外头流连，这座城市可实在不是什么好去处。”

“那是我完全始料未及的遭遇，但愿再也别遇上了。那是旁人家里的一场灾祸，并非我惹出来的，可但凡有点人性，也绝不能丢下不管、一走了之。”

“但愿不是什么麻疹或天花的场面吧。我听说你们布道学校那些人，多半成天都在沾染这类病。您没接触什么传染病吧？”

“我向您担保，绝没有。”

“那好；明早请准备好帮我的忙，摆在咱们面前的可不是桩轻省活儿，我想尽快把它做完。我六点半准时到店，可不保证每天早上都唱歌把您唤醒。听见这样稀罕的乐声在这座枯燥乏味的老铺子里回响，您方才是不是吓了一跳？”

===Original===
“I was indeed. At first I could not believe that it was a human voice.”

“That is rather an equivocal compliment.”

“I did not mean to speak in compliment at all, but to say in all sincerity that I have seldom heard such heavenly music.”

“Perhaps you have never heard very much of any kind, or else your imagination overshadows your other faculties. In fact I think it does, for did you not at first regard me as a painted lady who had stepped from the canvas to the floor?”

“I confess that I was greatly confused and startled.”

“In what respect did you see such a close resemblance?”

===Chinese===
“确实吓了一跳。起初我简直不敢相信那是人的嗓音。”

“这话听起来，倒像句模棱两可的恭维。”

“我半点没有存心奉承的意思，只是掏心窝子说一句，这样天籁般的音乐，我生平极少听闻。”

“兴许您原本也没听过多少音乐，再不然就是您的想象力压过了其他感官。其实我看正是如此——当初您第一眼见到我，不也把我当成了一位从画布上踱步走下地来的画中女子吗？”

“我承认，当时我着实慌乱又吃惊。”

“您究竟看出我和那画有多相像，又像在何处呢？”

===Original===
Dennis hesitated.

“Are you not able to tell?” asked she.

“Yes,” said Dennis, with heightened color, “but I do not like to say.”

“But I wish you to say,” said she, with a slightly imperious tone.

“Well, then, since you wish me to speak frankly, it was your expression. As you stood by the picture you unconsciously assumed the look and manner of the painted girl. And all the evening and morning I had been troubling over the picture and wondering how an artist could paint so lovely a face, and make it express only scorn and pride. It seemed to me that such a face ought to have been put to nobler uses.”

===Chinese===
丹尼斯迟疑起来。

“怎么，说不出口吗？”她问道。

“说得出，”丹尼斯涨红了脸道，“只是我不太好意思讲。”

“可我偏要您讲，”她略带几分颐指气使的口吻说道。

“那好吧，既然您要我坦白直言，那就是您的神情。您站在那幅画旁时，不知不觉间流露出的神态和气度，简直与画中那位姑娘一模一样。昨儿一整个晚上加上今儿一早，我都在为这幅画苦恼，心里纳闷画家怎么能画出那样一张俏丽动人的脸庞，却只教它流露出轻蔑与傲慢。在我看来，那样一张脸庞，本该派上更高尚的用场才对。”

===Original===
Miss Ludolph bit her lip and looked a little annoyed, but turning to Dennis she said, with some curiosity: “You are not a bit like the man who preceded you. How did you come to take his place?”

“I am poor, and will gratefully do any honest work rather than beg or starve.”

“I wish all the poor were of the same mind, but, from the way they drag on us who have something to give, I think the rule is usually the other way. Very well, that will answer; since you have asked papa to let you continue to do Pat’s duties, you had better be about them, though it is not so late as you think;” and she turned to her sketching in such a way as to quietly dismiss him.

She evidently regarded him with some interest and curiosity, as a unique specimen of the genus *homo*, and, looking upon him as a humble dependant, was inclined to speak to him freely and draw him out for her amusement.

===Chinese===
卢多尔夫小姐咬了咬嘴唇，神色微现愠怒，但还是转头带着几分好奇对丹尼斯说道：“您和先前那人可一点儿也不一样。您怎么会来顶他的缺呢？”

“我家里穷，与其讨饭或饿死，只要是体面本分的活计，我都感恩戴德地乐意去干。”

“真盼望所有穷人都能像您这么想；不过瞧他们拖累起我们这些稍微有点积蓄可施舍的人那副架势，我看世上通例往往恰恰相反。好了，这就够了；既然您已经央求过家父，准您继续兼着帕特的差事，那您还是赶紧去办正事吧，虽说眼下倒也没您想的那么晚。”说着，她便转回身去继续描摹画稿，以这样一种不动声色的姿态把他打发了。

很明显，她对他颇有几分兴致和好奇，把他当作人类（genus *homo*）中一个稀罕标本，又只当他是个卑微的门下食客，因而乐得同他随口攀谈，逗他吐露心曲，权当消遣。

===Original===
On going downstairs he saw that Mr. Ludolph was writing in his office. He was an early riser, and sometimes, entering the side door by a pass key before the store was opened, would secure an extra hour for business. He shook his head at Dennis, but said nothing.

By movements wonderfully quick and dexterous Dennis went through his wonted tasks, and at eight o’clock, the usual hour, the store was ready for opening.

Mr. Ludolph often caught glimpses of him as he darted to and fro, his cheeks glowing, and every act suggesting superabundant life.

He sighed and said: “After all, that young fellow is to be envied. He is getting more out of existence than most of us. He enjoys everything, and does even hard work with a zest that makes it play. There will be no keeping him down, for he seems possessed by the concentrated vim of this driving Yankee nation. Then he has a world of delusions besides that seem grand realities. Well, it is a sad thing to grow old and wise.”

Indeed it is, in Mr. Ludolph’s style.

===Chinese===
下到楼下，他看见卢多尔夫先生正在办公室里伏案写字。卢多尔夫先生向来早起，有时会在店铺开门前用万能钥匙从侧门进来，好抢出额外一小时处理店务。他朝丹尼斯摇了摇头，却什么也没说。

丹尼斯手脚麻利得出奇，三下五除二便做完了日常那些杂务；到了八点整——店里照常开门的钟点——铺子已收拾得齐整妥帖，准备迎客。

卢多尔夫先生不时瞥见他穿梭来去的身影，只见他双颊泛红，一举一动都透着蓬勃盎然的朝气。

他叹了口气，自言自语道：“说到底，那小伙子倒真叫人羡慕。他从日子里尝到的滋味，比咱们大多数人都丰厚。他样样事都乐在其中，哪怕苦累的活计干起来也兴头十足，活像做游戏一般。这小子是压不住的，他浑身上下仿佛聚齐了这个拼命进取的美国佬国度的全部锐气。何况，他心底还揣着一整个虚妄的幻梦世界，而在他眼里，那些幻梦竟如同宏伟的实在之物。唉，人老了、精明了，可真是件扫兴的事啊。”

照卢多尔夫先生那一套做派，这倒确实如此。

===Original===
When Dennis opened the front door, there was Ernst cowering in the March winds, and fairly trembling in the flutter of his hopes and fears. Dennis gave him a hearty grasp of the hand and drew him in, saying, “Don’t be afraid; I’ll take care of you.”

The boy’s heart clung to him as the vine tendril clasps the oak, and, upheld by Dennis’s strength, he entered what was to him wonderland indeed.

Mr. Ludolph looked him over as he and his daughter passed out on their return to breakfast, and said, “He will answer if he is strong enough.”

He saw nothing in that child’s face to fear.

Dennis assured him with a significant glance, which Mr. Ludolph understood as referring to better fare, that “he would grow strong fast now.”

Miss Ludolph was at once interested in the boy’s pale face and large, spiritual eyes; and she resolved to sketch them before good living had destroyed the artistic effect.

===Chinese===
丹尼斯打开前门时，只见恩斯特正缩在三月的寒风里，满心盼望又满怀忐忑，浑身抖个不停。丹尼斯一把热切地攥住他的手，将他拉进门来，说道：“别害怕；有我照应你呢。”

这少年的心紧紧依附着他，恰如葡萄藤的卷须缠绕着橡树；在丹尼斯这股力量的搀扶下，他踏进了这片在他眼中宛如仙境的天地。

卢多尔夫先生和女儿出门回去吃早饭时，上下打量了恩斯特一番，说道：“只要他身子骨够结实，倒也顶得上用。”

他在那孩子脸上，看不出半点值得提防之处。

丹尼斯向他投去一个意味深长的眼神，担保说“他往后很快就会壮实起来的”——卢多尔夫先生会意地以为，这话指的是伙食会大有改善。

卢多尔夫小姐立刻被这少年苍白的面容与那双清澈灵秀的大眼睛吸引住了；她暗自打定主意，趁着好伙食还没把那份艺术韵味养没之前，先给他画张素描。

===Original===
Under kindly instruction, the boy took readily to his duties, and promised soon to become very helpful. At noon Dennis took him out to lunch, and the poor, half-starved lad feasted as he had not for many a long day.

The afternoon mail brought Dennis his mother’s letter, and he wondered that her prediction should be fulfilled even before it reached him, and thus again his faith was strengthened. He smiled and said to himself, “Mother lives so near the heavenly land that she seems to get the news thence before anyone else.”

During the day a lady who was talking to Mr. Ludolph turned and said to Dennis: “How prettily you have arranged this table! Let me see; I think I will take that little group of bronzes. They make a very nice effect together.”

Dennis, with his heart swelling that he had arrived at the dignity of salesman, with much politeness, which evidently pleased the lady, assured her that they would be sent promptly to her address.

Mr. Ludolph looked on as if all was a matter of course while she was present, but afterward said: “You are on the right track, Fleet. You now see the practical result of a little thought and grace in arrangement. In matters of art, people will pay almost as much for these as for the things themselves. The lady would not have bought those bronzes under Berder’s system. When things are grouped rightly, people see just what they want, and buy the *effect* as well as the articles;” and with this judicious praise Mr. Ludolph passed on, better pleased with himself even than with Dennis.

===Chinese===
在丹尼斯耐心和蔼的指点下，这孩子很快就摸熟了差事，眼见着不久便能成为得力帮手。中午时分，丹尼斯带他出去吃了顿午饭，这个向来食不果腹的可怜半大小子，美美地饱餐了一顿，那是他好长一段日子以来头一回吃得这样痛快。

下午的邮差送来了丹尼斯母亲的来信。令他惊奇的是，信还尚未送到他手里，母亲的预言竟已然应验，他的信心因此愈发坚定。他微微笑了笑，自言自语道：“母亲的心住得离天国那样近，仿佛总是比旁人更早收到那里的消息。”

白天里，一位正与卢多尔夫先生交谈的太太转过身来，对丹尼斯说道：“您把这张桌子摆得真雅致！让我瞧瞧——我想买下那组小铜像。它们摆在一起，效果真好看。”

丹尼斯一想到自己已跻身体面的售货员之列，心中不由涌起一阵自豪，便极其彬彬有礼地向她担保，货品定会按地址迅速送到府上——他那谦恭周到的态度，显然令那位太太十分受用。

当着客人的面，卢多尔夫先生神色泰然，仿佛一切本该如此；事后却对丹尼斯说道：“你走上正路了，弗利特。你如今亲眼看见，在陈设上花点巧思、讲求些美感，能带来多实在的收益。凡属艺术品行当，客人几乎愿意为这份巧思和格调付上与器物本身相当的价钱。若按贝尔德（Berder）那套章法，这位太太绝不会买下那几尊铜像。东西只要搭配归置得当，客人一眼就能看出自己想要什么，买下的既是物件，也是那份“效果”。”留下这番分寸恰当的嘉许，卢多尔夫先生便踱步走开了，他对自己眼光的满意，甚至更胜过对丹尼斯的赞赏。

===Original===
But, as old Bill Cronk had intimated, such a peck of oats was almost too much for Dennis, and he felt that he was in danger of becoming too highly elated.

After closing the store, he wrote a brief but graphic letter to his mother, describing his promotion, and expressing much sympathy for poor Berder. Regarding himself as on the crest of prosperity’s wave, he felt a strong commiseration for every degree and condition of troubled humanity, and even could sigh over unlucky Berder’s deserved tribulations.

About eight o’clock he started to see his new friends in De Koven Street, and take his lesson in drawing. They welcomed him warmly, for they evidently looked upon him as the one who might save them from the engulfing waves of misfortune and evil.

The children were very different from the clamorous little wolves of the night before. No longer hungry, they were happy in the corner, with some rude playthings, talking and cooing together like a flock of young birds. Ernst was washing the tea-things, while his mother cared for the baby, recalling to Dennis, with a rush of tender memories, his mother and his boyhood tasks. Mr. Bruder still sat in the dusky corner. The day had been a hard one for him. Having nothing to do in the present, he had lived the miserable past over and over again. At times his strength almost gave way, but his wife would say, “Be patient! your friend Mr. Fleet will be in soon.”

===Chinese===
然而，正如老比尔·克朗克从前点拨过的那样，一下子喂下这么一大斗燕麦，丹尼斯几乎有些消受不住了；他暗自察觉，自己正处在得意忘形的危险边缘。

打烊关店后，他给母亲写了封简短却绘声绘色的信，讲述自己升职的经过，并对可怜的贝尔德深表同情。此刻他自觉正站在顺境浪潮的波峰上，于是对世间一切身处困境、境遇各异的苦命人，都生出强烈的怜悯之心，甚至连倒霉的贝尔德那份咎由自取的磨难，也叫他不禁为之叹息。

大约八点钟，他动身去德科文街看望那几位新结识的朋友，顺便上一堂绘画课。一家人热情地迎候着他，显然把他当成了能将他们从不幸与罪恶的吞噬巨浪中拉上岸的救星。

几个孩子与昨夜那副嗷嗷叫的小狼崽模样判若两人。不再挨饿之后，他们坐在角落里摆弄着几件简陋的玩具，嬉笑玩耍，像一群雏鸟般叽叽喳喳地相互逗乐。恩斯特正洗刷着茶具，他母亲则在照看小婴儿——这温馨一幕猛地勾起丹尼斯心头一阵温柔的回忆，让他想起了自己的母亲和少年时干过的家务活。布鲁德先生依旧坐在昏暗的角落里。这一整天对他而言着实难熬。眼下无所事事，他只能一遍又一遍地咀嚼着悲惨的过往。有好几回他几乎支撑不住，全靠妻子柔声宽慰：“耐心点儿！你的朋友弗利特先生很快就要来了。”

===Original===
From a few hints of what had passed, Dennis saw the trouble at once. Mr. Bruder must have occupation. After a few kindly generalities, they two got together, as congenial spirits, before the rescued picture; and soon both were absorbed in the mysteries of the divine art.

As the wife looked at the kindling, interested face of her husband, she murmured to herself over and over again, like the sweet refrain of a song, “His artist-soul haf come back; it truly haf.”

The lesson that night could be no more than a talk on general principles and rules. But Mr. Bruder soon found that he had an apt scholar, and Dennis’s enthusiasm kindled his own flagging zeal, and the artist-soul awakening within him, as his wife believed, longed to express itself as of old in glowing colors.

Moreover, his ambition was renewed in this promising pupil. Naturally generous, and understanding his noble profession, he felt his poor benumbed heart stir and glow at the thought of aiding this eager aspirant to become what he had hoped to be. He might live again in the richer and better-guided genius of his scholar.

===Chinese===
从两人只言片语的暗示中，丹尼斯立刻看穿了症结所在。布鲁德先生眼下最要紧的是得有事可做。寒暄了几句和煦的贴心话后，这对志趣相投的知音便凑到那幅失而复得的画作前；很快，两人都沉浸在神圣艺术的奥秘之中。

妻子望着丈夫重新焕发光彩、兴味盎然的脸庞，禁不住一遍又一遍地喃喃低语，宛如吟唱一曲甜美歌谣的叠句：“他那颗艺术家的魂灵回来啦；真真正正回来啦。”

当晚这堂课，其实不过是就绘画的普遍原则与法度闲谈一番罢了。可布鲁德先生很快便发现，自己收了一位悟性极高的弟子；丹尼斯满腔的热忱，也点燃了他自己早已懈怠消沉的志趣，而正如他妻子所坚信的，他体内正在苏醒的艺术家灵魂，再次渴望像从前那样，借绚丽明亮的色彩来抒发心志。

更何况，在这位前途无量的学生身上，他的雄心也重新燃起。他本性宽厚慷慨，又深谙自己这门高尚行当的甘苦，一想到能提携这位热切上进的年轻人去成就自己当年曾期许的事业，他那颗麻木已久的心便不由得微微悸动、发热起来。或许他能在学生更丰沛、更得明师指点的天赋里，重新活出自己的生命。

===Original===
“I will send you by Ernst in the morning some sketching paper, materials, and canvas, and you can prepare some studies for me. I will let him bring some drawings and colorings that I have made of late in odd moments, and you can see about how advanced I am, and what faults I have fallen into while groping my own way. And I am going to send you some canvas, also, for I am quite sure that if you paint a picture Mr. Ludolph will buy it.”

The man’s face brightened visibly at this.

“Will you let your friend make a suggestion?” continued Dennis.

“You can command me,” said Mr. Bruder, with emphasis.

“No; friends never do that; but I would like to suggest that at first you take some simple subject, that you can soon finish, and leave efforts that require more time for the future. That picture there shows what you can do, and you need to work now more from the commercial standpoint than the artist’s.”

After a moment’s thought, the man said, “You are right. As I look around dis room, and see our needs, I see dat you are right. Do’ I meant to attempt someding difficult, to show Mr. Ludolph vat I could do.”

===Chinese===
“明早我让恩斯特给您捎些素描纸、画材和画布来，您可以先替我起几幅习作底稿。我也让他把近来我抽空涂画的一些素描和敷彩画稿带过来，您瞧瞧我如今大概到了什么火候，自己摸索门道时又染上了哪些毛病。另外我还要给您捎些画布来，因为我十分笃定，您若是画出画儿来，卢多尔夫先生一定会收下的。”

听到这话，那汉子的脸色明显亮堂了起来。

“不知您愿不愿意听朋友提个建议？”丹尼斯接着说道。

“您尽管吩咐就是，”布鲁德先生郑重其事地说道。

“不敢；朋友之间从不兴吩咐那一套。我只是想建议您，起初先挑些简单些的题材，好快些完工，至于那些更费工夫的大手笔，不妨留待日后。摆在那儿的那幅画已经足以证明您的功底了；眼下您动笔，与其一味照着艺术家的心意来，不如先多从生计销路的角度着眼。”

汉子沉吟片刻，说道：“您说得对。我环顾这间屋子，瞧瞧一家老小的需用，就知道您说得在理。虽说我原先盘算着挑件难些的活计露一手，好叫卢多尔夫先生见识见识我的本事。”

===Original===
“That will all come in good time; and now, my friend, good night.”

The next day was far more tolerable for poor Bruder, because he was occupied, and he found it much easier to resist the clamors of appetite.

Dennis’s sketches interested him greatly, for, though they showed the natural defects of one who had received little instruction, both power and originality were manifest in their execution.

“He, too, can be an artist, if he vill,” was his emphatic comment, after looking them over.

He prepared one study, to be continued under his own eye, and another for Dennis to work at alone. Afterward he sat down to something for himself. He thought a few moments, and then outlined rapidly as his subject the figure of a man dashing a wineglass to the ground.

As he worked, his wife smiled encouragement to him as of old, and often looked upward in thankfulness to Heaven.

===Chinese===
“那些日后都会水到渠成的；好了，我的朋友，晚安。”

次日，对于可怜的布鲁德而言，日子便好过得多了——只因手里有了正经事做，他发现酒瘾的煎熬也远比先前容易抵挡了。

丹尼斯的画稿令他兴致勃勃；虽然画里难免带着自学成才、少经指点之人常有的生涩毛病，但笔下显露出的魄力与独创性却一目了然。

“只要他肯立志，他也一样能成为画家，”他把画稿从头到尾翻看一遍后，语气笃定地评断道。

他拟好了两份习作：一份由丹尼斯在自己眼皮底下接着画，另一份则留给丹尼斯独自揣摩练习。随后，他便坐下来给自己铺纸起稿。他凝神思索了片刻，随即便飞快勾勒出画面的主题——一个男子正将手中的酒杯狠狠摔向地面。

他埋头作画时，妻子像从前那样朝他露出鼓励的微笑，还不时抬头望向苍穹，满怀感恩之情。

## XXIV Night Thoughts / 第二十四章 夜思

===Original===
Dennis passed out of the heavy, massive entrance to the wealthy brewer’s mansion with a sense of relief as if escaping from prison. The duskiness and solitude of the street seemed a grateful refuge, and the night wind was to his flushed face like a cool hand laid on a feverish brow. He was indeed glad to be alone, for his was one of those deep, earnest natures that cannot rush to the world in garrulous confidence when disturbed and perplexed. There are many sincere but shallow people who must tell of and talk away every passing emotion. Not of the abundance of their hearts, for abundance there is not, but of the uppermost thing in their hearts their mouths must speak, even though the subjects be of the delicate nature that would naturally be hidden. Such mental constitutions are at least healthful. Concealed trouble never preys upon them like the canker in the bud. Everything comes to the surface and is thrown off.

But at first Dennis scarcely dared to recognize the truth himself, and the thought of telling even his mother was repugnant. For half an hour he walked the streets in a sort of stupor. He was conscious only of a heavy, aching heart and a wearied, confused brain. All the time, however, he knew an event had occurred that must for good or evil affect his entire existence; but he shrank with nervous dread from grappling with the problem. As the cold air refreshed and revived him, his strong, practical mind took up the question almost without volition, and by reason of his morbid, wearied state, only the dark and discouraging side was presented. The awakening to his love was a very different thing to Dennis, and to the majority in this troubled world, from the blissful consciousness of Adam when for the first time he saw the fair being whom he might woo at his leisure, amid embowering roses, without fear or thought of a rival.

To Dennis the fact of his love, so far from promising to be the source of delightful romance and enchantment, clearly showed itself to be the hardest and most practical question of a life full of such questions. In his strong and growing excitement he spoke to himself as to a second person: “Oh, I see it all now. Poor, blind fool that I was, to think that by coveting and securing every possible moment in her presence I was only learning to love art! As I saw her tonight, so radiant and beautiful, and yet in the embrace of another man, and that man evidently an ardent admirer, what was art to me? As well might a starving man seek to satisfy himself by wandering through an old Greek temple as for me to turn to art alone. One crumb of warm, manifested love from her would be worth more than all the cold, abstract beauty in the universe. And yet what chance have I? What can I hope for more than a passing thought and a little kindly, condescending interest? Clerk and man-of-all-work in a store, poor and heavily burdened, the idea of my loving one of the most wealthy, admired, and aristocratic ladies in Chicago! It is all very well in storybooks for peasants to fall in love with princesses, but in practical Chicago the fact of my attachment to Miss Ludolph would be regarded as one of the richest jokes of the season, and by Mr. Ludolph as such a proof of rusticity and folly as would at once secure my return to pastoral life.”

Then hope whispered, “But you can achieve position and wealth as others have done, and then can speak your mind from the standpoint of equality.”

===Chinese===
丹尼斯走出那位富有的啤酒商公馆厚重气派的大门，顿觉如释重负，宛如逃出牢笼一般。街道上的暮色沉沉与寂寥无人，倒成了一处令人心安的避风港；夜风吹拂着他涨红发烫的脸庞，恰似一只清凉的手抚上灼热的额头。能独自一人，他实在感到庆幸——他生就一副深沉笃厚的性情，一旦心烦意乱、困惑不解，便绝做不到逢人便絮絮叨叨地倾诉衷肠。世上确有许多心肠真诚却浅薄之人，哪怕是转瞬即逝的情绪，也非要一吐为快、说散了才罢休。他们并非“心里所充满的，口里就说出来”——因为他们心里原本并无多少积蓄——而是眼下心头浮着什么，嘴上便非说出来不可，纵使所谈之事本该幽微隐秘、秘而不宣亦然。这样的心性至少有益于身心健康，郁结的忧烦绝不会像蛀蚀花蕾的蟊虫般暗自啮咬他们的肺腑。一切都在嘴上摊开，也便随之烟消云散了。

然而起初，丹尼斯连自己几乎都不敢直面这个真相，一想到哪怕要向母亲吐露只言片语，心中便觉得抵触难耐。有半个钟头的光景，他恍恍惚惚地在街上走着。他只觉一颗心沉重疼痛，脑海疲惫而混乱。尽管如此，他心里始终明白，方才已发生了一件足以影响他此后一生祸福的大事；只是他心怀惶遽，实在不敢直面这桩难题。待冷风将他吹醒，令他精神略微振作起来，他那强健而务实的头脑几乎是不由自主地抓住了这个问题；只是由于此刻心神病态、疲惫不堪，呈现在他眼前的便只有阴暗沮丧的一面。爱情的觉醒于丹尼斯而言——也如于这纷扰尘世中的大多数人而言——与亚当（Adam）初见那位绰约佳人时的欣喜心境截然不同：亚当大可在玫瑰环绕的花荫间从容倾诉衷情，既无忧惧，也全无情敌之虞。

对丹尼斯来说，爱上她这个事实非但无望成为甜蜜浪漫、令人沉醉的源泉，反而清楚地显露出：这将是他本就棘手不断的人生里最艰难、最现实的考题。他心潮翻涌，愈发激动，仿佛对着另一个人般自言自语起来：“噢，如今我全明白了。我真是个可怜又瞎眼的蠢货，竟以为自己贪恋并死死抓住能在她身旁多待的每一刻，不过是在学着热爱艺术！今晚我亲眼看见她那样光彩照人、明艳动人，却偏偏偎依在另一个男人的臂弯里，而那男人显然又是个热烈的追求者——那时，艺术于我又算得了什么呢？倘若要我单靠艺术来慰藉自己，那无异于叫一个饥肠辘辘的饿汉去古老的希腊神庙里徘徊果腹。哪怕她肯赐予我一星半点真切流露的温情，也胜过宇宙间一切冰冷抽象的美。可我又有什么指望呢？除了偶尔被她记起一瞬、施舍一点和善而居高临下的关切之外，我还能奢望什么？一个店铺里的店员兼杂役，一贫如洗、重担压肩，竟妄想爱上芝加哥最富有、最受倾慕、也最具贵族气派的小姐之一！故事书里写乡下小子爱上公主固然动听，可在讲究实际的芝加哥，我倾心卢多尔夫小姐这档子事，只会被当作本季最叫人捧腹的笑谈；在卢多尔夫先生眼里，这更会成为我粗鄙愚妄的铁证，足以让他立刻把我打发回乡间过那田园生活去。”

这时，希望却在耳畔低语：“可你也能像旁人那样挣得地位与财富，到那时，你便能以平等的姿态倾吐心声了。”

===Original===
But Dennis was in a mood to see only the hopeless side that night, and exclaimed almost aloud: “Nonsense! Can it be even imagined that she, besieged by the most gifted and rich of the city, will wait for a poor unknown admirer? Mr. Mellen, I understand, approaches her from every vantage-ground save that of a noble character; but in the fashionable world how little thought is given to this draw back!” and in his perturbation he strode rapidly and aimlessly on, finding some relief in mere physical activity.

Suddenly his hasty steps ceased, and even in the dusk of the street his face gleamed out distinctly, so great was its pallor. Like a ray of light, a passage from the Word of God revealed to him his situation in a new aspect. It seemed to him almost that someone had whispered the words in his ear, so distinctly did they present themselves﻿—“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers.”

Slowly and painfully he said to himself, as if recognizing the most hopeless barrier that had yet been dwelt upon, “Christine Ludolph is an infidel.”

Not only the voice of reason, and of the practical world, but also the voice of God seemed to forbid his love; and the conviction that he must give it all up became a clear as it was painful. The poor fellow leaned his head against the shaggy bark of an elm in a shadowy square which the streetlamps could but faintly penetrate. The night wind swayed the budding branches of the great tree, and they sighed over him as if in sympathy.

The struggle within his soul was indeed bitter, for, though thus far he had spoken hopelessly, he had not been altogether hopeless; but now that conscience raised its impassable wall high as heaven, which he must not break through, his pain was so great as to almost unman him, and such tears as only men can weep fell from his eyes. In anguish he exclaimed, “That which might have been the chief blessing of life has become my greatest misfortune.”

===Chinese===
然而今夜的丹尼斯满心只看得见绝望的一面，几乎脱口大声嚷道：“胡说！全城最有才干、最富有的男子都围着她打转，难道还指望她去等一个一文不名、穷困潦倒的仰慕者不成？梅伦先生——据我所知——除了品格高尚这一条之外，他追求她可谓占尽了所有优势；可在上流风尚界里，又有谁会在意这点缺憾呢！”心乱如麻之中，他大步流星地漫无目的地向前疾走，姑且借着单纯的奔走劳顿来排遣几分烦闷。

猛地，他急促的脚步顿住了。哪怕是在昏暗幽微的街灯影里，他那张骤然失血的脸也显得格外惨白清晰。宛如一道光芒骤然照彻，一段《圣经》经文从另一个崭新的角度向他揭示了眼前的处境。那句话清晰无比地浮现出来，简直就像有人贴在他耳边亲口低语一般——“你们和不信的原不相配，不要同负一轭。”

他缓缓地、痛苦地喃喃自语，仿佛终于认清了一道比此前思及的任何阻碍都更加绝望的屏障：“克里斯蒂娜·卢多尔夫是个不信神的人。”

不只是理智的声音、现实世俗的声音，就连上帝的声音似乎也在严厉禁止他的这份爱；他必须彻底割舍这一切的信念，霎时变得既痛彻心扉，又无比清晰。这可怜的小伙子将头抵在一棵老榆树粗糙斑驳的树皮上——那树立在一个幽暗的广场边，街灯微弱的光晕几乎透不进来。夜风拂动大树方才抽芽的枝条，枝叶在他头顶发出轻轻的叹息，仿佛在同情他的苦楚。

他灵魂深处的煎熬实在是撕心裂肺；只因他方才嘴上虽尽说些绝望的话，心底却原未彻底断绝指望；而今良知却筑起了一道高耸入云、绝不可逾越的高墙，令他万万不可冒犯穿行，那痛苦竟剧烈得几乎令他丧失男儿的克制，唯有男子才会落下的热泪从他眼眶中滚落下来。他在悲痛中呼号道：“那本可成为我一生最大福分的念想，如今却成了我最大的祸殃。”

===Original===
Above him the gale caused two fraying limbs to appear to moan in echo of the suffering beneath.

“This then must be the end of my prayers in her behalf﻿—my ardent hope and purpose to lead her to the truth﻿—she to walk through honored, sunny paths to everlasting shame and night, and I through dark and painful ways to light and peace, if in this bitter test I remain faithful. Surely there *is* much to try one’s faith. And yet it must be so as far as human foresight can judge.”

Then a great pity for her swelled his heart, for he felt that her case was the saddest after all, and his tears flowed faster than ever.

Human voices now startled him﻿—some late revellers passing homeward. The tears and emotion, of which we never think of being ashamed when alone with Nature and its Author, he dreaded to have seen by his fellows, and hastily wiping his eyes, he slunk into the deeper shadow of the tree, and they passed on. Then, an old trait asserting itself, he condemned his own weakness. Stepping from the sheltering trunk against which he was leaning, he stood strong and erect.

The winds were hushed as if expectant in the branches above.

===Chinese===
在他头顶上方，狂风刮得两条相互摩擦的树杈仿佛在呜咽哀鸣，恰与树下的苦痛遥相呼应。

“那么，我为她所做的一切祈祷，我曾怀抱的引导她归向真理的热切盼望与志向，竟只能落得如此结局了么——她将踏着鲜花荣宠、阳光普照的大道，走向永恒的羞辱与黑夜；而我若能在这场苦涩的试炼中坚守忠贞，便将穿过幽暗坎坷的小径，走向光明与平安。人的信心，*果真*要经受这许多严峻的考验啊。然而仅就凡人的远见所能判断的而言，事情又非如此不可。”

念及于此，一股深沉的怜悯顿时涨满了他的胸膛，因为他觉得归根结底，她的处境才是最可悲的，于是他的泪水淌得愈发汹涌了。

这时，几声人语惊动了他——是几个夜深狂欢过后正往家走的醉客。人在独自面对大自然及其造物主时，从不会因落泪动情而感到羞惭，可他却生怕被世俗旁人瞧见自己的这副模样，急忙一把抹干眼泪，缩进树干后更深浓的阴影里，直到那伙人走远。随后，他骨子里向来硬朗的性情重新占了上风，他暗暗唾弃自己方才的软弱，迈步离开方才倚靠栖身的树干，挺直身躯，刚毅而坚定地站定。

头顶枝桠间的风声霎时平息下来，仿佛正屏息拭目以待。

===Original===
“Dennis Fleet,” he said, “you must put your foot on this folly here and now.”

He bared his head and looked upward.

“O God,” he said, solemnly, “if this is contrary to Thy will﻿—Thy will be done.”

He paused a moment reverently, and then turned on his heel and strode resolutely homeward.

A gust of wind crashed the branches overhead together like the clash of cymbals in victory.

===Chinese===
“丹尼斯·弗利特，”他开口说道，“你必须此时此地就把这桩蠢念头一脚踩灭。”

他摘下帽子，仰首望向夜空。

“上帝啊，”他庄严地祷告道，“倘若此事违逆祢的旨意——愿祢的旨意成就。”

他虔敬地默立片刻，随即脚跟一转，迈着果决的步子大步朝家的方向走去。

一阵疾风掠过，头顶的树枝轰然相击，宛如凯旋时铿锵交鸣的铜钹。

===Original===
The early spring dawn was tingeing the eastern horizon before the gay revel ceased and the mansion of the rich brewer was darkened. All the long night, light, airy music had caused late passersby to pause a moment to listen, and to pity or envy the throng within, as disposition dictated. Mr. Brown was a man who prided himself on lavish and rather coarse hospitality. A table groaning under costly dishes and every variety of liquor was the crowning feature, the blissful climax of all his entertainments; and society from its highest circles furnished an abundance of anxious candidates for his suppers, who ate and criticised, drank to and disparaged, their plebeian host.

Mrs. Brown was heavy in every sense of the word, and with her huge person draped with acres of silk, and festooned with miles of point-lace, she waddled about and smiled and nodded good-naturedly at everybody and everything.

It was just the place for a fashionable revel, where the gross, repulsive features of coarse excess are veiled and masked somewhat by the glamour of outward courtesy and good-breeding.

At first Christine entered into the dance with great zest and a decided sense of relief. She was disappointed and out of sorts with herself. Again she had failed in the object of her intense ambition, and though conscious that, through the excitement of the occasion, she had sung better than ever before, yet she plainly saw in the different results of her singing and that of Dennis Fleet that there was a depth in the human heart which she could not reach. She could secure only admiration, superficial applause. The sphere of the true artist who can touch and sway the popular heart seemed beyond her ability. By voice or pencil she had never yet attained it. She had too much mind to mistake the character of the admiration she excited, and was far too ambitious to be satisfied with the mere praise bestowed on a highly accomplished girl. She aspired, determined, to be among the first, and to be a second-rate imitator in the world of art was to her the agony of a disappointed life. And yet to imitate with accuracy and skill, not with sympathy, was the only power she had as yet developed. She saw the limitations of her success more clearly than did anyone else, and chafed bitterly at the invisible bounds she could not pass.

The excitement of the dance enabled her to banish thoughts that were both painful and humiliating. Moreover, to a nature so active and full of physical vigor, the swift, grace motion was a source of keen enjoyment.

===Chinese===
直到早春的曙光已将东方的天际线染上一抹微明，这场热闹的欢宴方才散场，那座富有啤酒商的豪宅也归于沉寂幽暗。整整一个漫漫长夜，屋里传出的轻快悠扬的乐声，屡屡引得深夜行人驻足倾听一会儿，各自性情不同，对屋内的宾客或生怜悯、或起艳羡。布朗先生平素最引以为傲的，便是自己待客阔绰豪奢、却颇有些粗俗的排场。一张摆满珍馐美馔与各色佳酿、重得仿佛要压弯桌腿的大餐桌，永远是他所有宴饮中最压轴的亮点，也是宾主尽欢的最高潮；而城中最高雅的社交圈里，也从不缺少迫切盼着来蹭他一顿夜宵的食客——他们一面大快朵颐、品头论足，一面举杯向主人祝酒，暗地里却百般贬损他们这位平民出身的东道主。

布朗太太（Mrs. Brown）无论从哪个意义上讲都分量十足。她那庞硕的身躯上披挂着好几英亩似的绸缎，又悬垂着仿佛绵延数里的挑花蕾丝，就这么摇摇摆摆地四处踱步，对上上下下所有人和一切事都露出和善的微笑，频频点头致意。

这恰是最适合办一场时髦狂欢宴的所在——在这里，粗鄙放纵那股惹人反感的俗陋之气，多少被表面上的彬彬有礼与教养风度所笼罩、所掩饰住了。

起初，克里斯蒂娜兴致勃勃地投入了舞会，心里着实感到一阵解脱。此前她既觉失望，又对自己恼火万分。她热切追逐的志向再度落了空；尽管她清楚，凭着当时那股激昂的氛围，她唱得比以往任何一次都要出色，可从她与丹尼斯·弗利特两人演唱后截然不同的反响里，她分明看出了人心深处存在着一片她无力触及的幽微境界。她所能博取的不过是赞叹与浮面的喝彩罢了。真正的大艺术家能够扣动并左右芸芸众生的心弦，那片天地似乎远非她力所能及。无论是凭歌喉还是凭画笔，她至今都未能臻此境界。她天资聪颖，绝不会错认自己所激起的那份赞赏究竟成色几何；她又雄心勃勃，决不肯满足于旁人夸奖一个才艺出众的姑娘时随口奉上的那些赞誉。她立志、而且笃定要跻身一流之列，在艺术界做一个二流模仿者，于她而言无异于一场抱负落空的终生惨痛。然而迄今为止，她唯一修成的本领，却恰恰只是精准而娴熟地模仿——而非以真情去感通。她比世上任何人都更清楚自己成功背后的局限，对着那道怎么也跨不过去的无形藩篱，暗自焦灼苦恼不已。

舞池里的热络兴奋，正好使她得以暂时抛开这些既痛苦又屈辱的思绪。况且，对于像她这样一个精力充沛、体魄强健的性情中人来说，飞旋轻快、优雅舒展的舞步本身就是一种酣畅淋漓的享受。

===Original===
But when after supper many of the ladies were silly, and the gentlemen were either stupid or excited, according to the action of the “invisible spirit of wine” upon their several constitutions﻿—when after many glasses of champagne Mr. Mellen began to effervesce in frothy sentimentality and a style of lovemaking simply nauseating to one of Christine’s nature﻿—she looked around for her father in order to escape from the scenes that were becoming revolting.

Though of earth only in all the sources of her life and hopes, she was not earthy. If her spirit could not soar and sing in the sky, it also could not grovel in the mire of gross materiality. Some little time, therefore, before the company broke up, on the plea of not feeling well she lured her father away from his wine and cigars and a knot of gentlemen who were beginning to talk a little incoherently. Making their adieux amid many protestations against their early departure, they drove homeward.

“How did you enjoy yourself?” asked her father.

“Very much in the early part of the evening, not at all in the latter part. To sum up, I am disgusted with Mr. Mellen and these Browns in general, and myself in particular.”

“What is the matter with Mr. Mellen? I understand that the intriguing mammas consider him the largest game in the city.”

“When hunting degenerates into the chase and capture of insects, you may style him game. Between his champagne and silly lovemaking, he was as bad as a dose of ipecac.”

===Chinese===
然而夜宵过后，依着那“无形的酒灵”在各人体质上施展的不同魔力，许多女士开始变得傻气胡言，绅士们则非呆滞木然即亢奋失态——尤其是梅伦先生喝下几杯香槟后，竟像酒沫子似的冒出一串串虚浮矫情的酸腐情话，那副追求女子的做派，在克里斯蒂娜这等性情的人看来简直令人作呕——于是她环顾四周寻找父亲，一心想逃离这越发不堪入目的场面。

尽管克里斯蒂娜生命与希望的一切源泉都只系于尘世，她却绝不流于庸俗泥淖。她的灵魂纵然还不能展翅高飞、在云霄间放歌，却也断不肯在粗鄙物欲的泥涂里俯首打滚。因此，在宾客尚未散尽之前的好一阵子，她便推说身体不适，把父亲从美酒、雪茄以及一群已开始语无伦次的绅士堆里拉了出来。在一片挽留与埋怨他们早退的声浪中，父女俩向主人辞别，乘车朝家里驶去。

“今晚玩得可还尽兴？”父亲问道。

“前半夜极尽兴，后半夜则半点乐趣也无。总而言之，我对梅伦先生和这帮布朗家的人深感厌恶，而尤以对自己为甚。”

“梅伦先生怎么惹着你了？据我所知，城里那些工于心计的阔太太们都把他视作最大的一块猎物呢。”

“要是打猎堕落到追捕虫豸的地步，您倒也不妨管他叫猎物。又是灌香槟，又是说些蠢不可耐的甜言蜜语，他简直比喝下一剂吐根催吐药还叫人作呕。”

===Original===
Christine spoke freely to her father of her admirers, usually making them the themes of satire and jest.

“And what is the trouble with our entertainers?”

“I am sorry to speak so of anyone whose hospitality I have accepted, but unless it is your wish I hope never to accept it again. They all smell of their beer. Everything is so coarse, lavish, and ostentatious. They tell you as through a brazen trumpet on every side, ‘We are rich.’ ”

“They give magnificent suppers,” said Mr. Ludolph, in apology.

“More correctly, the French cook they employ gives them. I do not object to the nicest of suppers, but prefer that the Browns be not on the *carte de menu*. From the moment our artistic programme ended, and the entertainment fell into their hands, it began to degenerate into an orgy. Nothing but the instinctive restraints of good-breeding prevents such occasions from ending in a drunken revel.”

“You are severe. Mr. Brown’s social effort is not a bad type of the entertainments that prevail in fashionable life.”

===Chinese===
克里斯蒂娜向来对父亲无话不谈，提起自己的追求者们，往往拿他们当作讽刺戏谑的话柄。

“那今天款待咱们的主人家又有什么不妥？”

“既然领了人家的盛情款待，本不该在背后如此议论，实在过意不去；但除非您执意要去，否则我真盼望往后再也别赴他们的约了。他们浑身上下都透着一股啤酒味儿。屋里屋外的一切都显得那么粗鄙、铺张、卖弄。四面八方都仿佛在吹着黄铜号角向你宣示：‘我们有钱。’”

“可他们置办的夜宵的确丰盛气派啊。”卢多尔夫先生代为辩解了一句。

“说得更准确些，是他们雇来的那位法国大厨置办得好。精美可口的夜宵我倒并不反对，只是宁愿菜单上别列着布朗夫妇的名字罢了。打从咱们的文艺节目一落幕、整场宴会交回到他们手里那一刻起，气氛便立刻滑向纵酒狂欢。若不是还剩点上流教养带来的本能克制，这种聚会只怕非得闹成一场酒鬼撒疯的闹剧不可。”

“你未免太苛刻了。布朗先生这一番社交排场，在眼下时髦圈子里盛行的宴会当中，已算得上是很像样的代表了。”

===Original===
“Well, it may be true, but they never seemed to me so lacking in good taste and refinement before. Wait till we dispense choice viands and wines to choicer spirits in our own land, and I will guarantee a marvellously wide difference. Then the eye, the ear, the mind, shall be feasted, as well as the lower sense.”

“Well, I do not see why you should be disgusted with yourself. I am sure that you covered yourself with glory, and were the belle of the occasion.”

“That is no great honor, considering the occasion. Father, strange as it may seem to you, I envied your man-of-all-work tonight. Did you not mark the effect of his singing?”

“Yes, and felt it in a way that I cannot explain to myself. His tones seemed to thrill, and stir my very heart. I have not been so affected by music for years. At first I thought it was surprise at hearing him sing at all, but I soon found that it was something in the music itself.”

“And that something I fear I can never grasp﻿—never attain.”

===Chinese===
“嗯，也许您说得对，只是从前我倒从未觉得他们竟如此缺乏品味与雅致。等日后回到咱们自己的故土，由我们亲自以佳肴美酒款待更出众雅致的宾客时，我敢担保那场面会大不相同，判若云泥。到那时，不只口腹感官得以饱餐，就连耳目与心灵也必能共享盛宴。”

“好吧，可我还是不明白你为何要厌恶自己。我可以肯定，今晚你光彩夺目、大出风头，分明是全场最耀眼的佳人。”

“就今晚那种场合而论，这实在算不得什么体面的荣耀。父亲，这话听在您耳里或许有些荒唐，可今晚我着实嫉妒起您那位打杂的伙计了。您难道没有留意他歌声产生的反响吗？”

“留意到了，而且我自己也深受震动，那种滋味连我自己都说不清道不明。他的嗓音仿佛有种穿透力，直震得人心弦发颤。我已经许多年不曾被音乐这样打动过了。起初我还当自己是惊讶于他居然会唱歌，可很快便察觉，真正教人动容的，原是音乐本身里蕴含的某种东西。”

“而那种东西，我只怕自己永远也领悟不到——永远也企及不到。”

===Original===
“Why, my dear, they applauded you to the echo.”

“I would rather see one moist eye as the tribute to my singing than to be deafened by noisy applause. I fear I shall never reach high art. Men’s hearts sleep when I do my best.”

“I think you are slightly mistaken there, judging from your train of admirers,” said Mr. Ludolph, turning off a disagreeable subject with a jest. The shrewd man of the world guessed the secret of her failure. She herself must feel, before she could touch feeling. But he had systematically sought to chill and benumb her nature, meaning it to awake at just the time, and under just the circumstances, that should accord with his controlling ambition. Then reverting to Dennis, he continued: “It won’t answer for Fleet to sweep the store any longer after the part he played tonight. Indeed, I doubt if he would be willing to. Not only he, but the world will know that he is capable of better things. What has occurred will awaken inquiry, and may soon secure him good business offers. I do not intend to part readily with so capable a young fellow. He does well whatever is required, and therefore I shall promote him as fast as is prudent. I think I can make him of great use to me.”

“That is another thing that provokes me,” said Christine. “Only yesterday morning he seemed such a useful, humble creature, and last evening through my own folly he developed into a fine gentleman; and I shall have to say, ‘By your leave, sir’; ‘Will you please do this’?﻿—If I dare ask anything at all.”

“I am not so sure of that,” said her father. “My impression is that Fleet has too much good sense to put on airs in the store. But I will give him more congenial work; and as one of the young gentleman clerks, we can ask him up now and then to sing with us. I should much enjoy trying some of our German music with him.”

===Chinese===
“咦，我亲爱的女儿，刚才众人给你鼓掌，掌声简直震天响呢。”

“我宁可看见一双因我歌声而湿润的眼眸作为赞赏，也不愿被震耳欲聋的喧闹掌声吵得耳鸣。我只怕自己永远也登不上高雅艺术的殿堂。哪怕我竭尽全力去唱，旁人的心却依然沉睡不醒。”

“要从你身后那一长串追求者来看，你这话怕是略有些偏颇了吧。”卢多尔夫先生笑着打趣，把一个令人不快的话题轻巧地岔了开去。这位老练世故的商人心里早猜透了她失败的秘诀：自己必得先有真情实感，方能触动旁人的情感。然而多年来，他一直有意识地将女儿的性情冰封麻木，蓄意要让它只在恰当的时机、恰当的境遇下苏醒，好顺应他自己那根深蒂固的野心。接着他又把话题转回丹尼斯身上，继续说道：“经过今晚这番表现，再让弗利特在店里扫地可就说不过去了。事实上，只怕他自己也未必肯再干了。不光是他自己，外头的人也都会知道他原是个能担大事的人才。今晚发生的事必定会引来各方打听，说不定很快就会有人出高价挖他去商行任职。这么个精明能干的年轻人，我可不打算轻易放手。交代给他的差事，他桩桩件件都办得妥帖漂亮，因此只要时机稳妥，我会尽快提拔他。我看得出，他将来能替我帮上大忙。”

“这正是另一件叫我恼火的事呢！”克里斯蒂娜说道，“明明就在昨天早上，他还是个既顺手又卑微的小角色，谁知昨晚竟因我自己的糊涂举动，摇身一变成了位风度翩翩的绅士；往后我还得对他说‘承蒙恩准，先生’、‘劳驾您办一下这事好吗’——倘若我还敢开口使唤他什么的话。”

“那倒未必，”她父亲说道，“依我看，弗利特是个很懂分寸的年轻人，不至于在店里摆起架子来。不过我确实要派给他些更合他性情的活计；况且等他成了店里的年轻体面职员，咱们倒可以隔三差五请他到楼上与我们一道合唱几曲。我倒真很想同他试着排练几首咱们的德国乐曲呢。”

## XLIV On the Beach / 第四十四章 海滩之上

===Original===
In the situation of supreme peril described in the last chapter, Dennis stood a second helpless and hopeless. Christine rested a heavy burden in his arms, happily unconscious. Breathing an agonized prayer to heaven, he looked around for any possibility of escape. Just then an express-wagon was driven furiously toward them, its driver seeking his way out by the same path that Dennis had chosen. As he reached them the man saw the hopeless obstruction, and wheeled his horses. As he did so, quick as thought, Dennis threw Christine into the bottom of the wagon, and, clinging to it, climbed into it himself. He turned her face downward from the fire, and, covering his own, he crouched beside her, trusting all now to God.

The driver urged his horses toward the lake, believing that his only chance. They tore away through the blazing streets. The poor man was soon swept from his seat and perished, but his horses rushed madly on till they plunged into the lake.

At the sound of water Dennis lifted his head and gave a cry of joy. It seemed that the hand of God had snatched them from death. Gently he lifted Christine out upon the sands and commenced bathing her face from the water that broke in spray at his feet. She soon revived and looked around. In a voice full of awe and wonder she whispered, “Ah! there is another world and another life, after all.”

“Indeed there is, Miss Ludolph,” said Dennis, supporting her on his arm and bending over her, “but, thanks to a merciful Providence, you are still in this one.”

“How is it?” she said, with a bewildered air. “I do not understand. The last I remember, we were surrounded by fire, you were despairing, and it seemed that I died.”

===Chinese===
面对上一章所述的那般绝境险厄，丹尼斯茫然伫立了一瞬，感到束手无策、绝望至极。克里斯蒂娜沉甸甸地瘫软在他怀里，幸而已经人事不省。他怀着撕心裂肺的悲痛向上天默祷一声，随即环顾四周，搜寻任何一线生机。就在此时，一辆快运货车朝他们疯狂疾驰而来——那车夫竟也选了丹尼斯同一条路企图突围。赶到他们近前时，那人瞧见前方已彻底堵死，急忙勒马调头。就在他调转车头的那一刹那，丹尼斯电光石火般将克里斯蒂娜扔进车厢底部，自己也一把抓住车帮翻爬了上去。他把她的脸朝下按住以避开烈焰，自己也遮住面庞蜷伏在她身旁，此刻唯有将一切全数托付给上帝。

车夫认定这是唯一的活路，便拼命鞭策马匹朝湖边狂奔。骏马沿着熊熊燃烧的街道飞驰而去。那可怜的汉子很快便被烈焰狂风从车座上掀落丧命，可那几匹马却依旧发狂般往前猛冲，直到一头扎进湖水之中。

听见水声，丹尼斯猛地抬起头，失声欢呼起来。这仿佛真是上帝之手将他们从鬼门关硬生生夺了回来。他轻手轻脚地将克里斯蒂娜抱下车，放到沙滩上，掬起脚边激溅起水花的湖水轻轻拍打她的脸庞。她很快苏醒过来，茫然环视四周，随后用一种满含敬畏与惊奇的嗓音低语道：“啊！果然还有另一个世界，还有来生。”

“确实有的，卢多尔夫小姐，”丹尼斯一边用手臂托住她、俯身望着她，一边说道，“但承蒙仁慈的上苍垂怜，您眼下还活在今生这世上呢。”

“这是怎么回事？”她神色迷惘地问，“我不明白。我最后记得的，是我们被大火围困，您一脸绝望，我只觉得自己已经死了。”

===Original===
“You fainted, Miss Ludolph. But God as by a miracle brought us out of the furnace, and for the present we are safe.” After she had sufficiently rallied from her excessive exhaustion and terror, he told her how they escaped.

“I see no God in it all,” she said; “only a most fortunate opportunity, of which you, with great nerve and presence of mind, availed yourself. To you alone, again and again this dreadful night, I owe my life.”

“God uses us as His instruments to do His will. The light will come to you by and by, and you will learn a better wisdom.”

“In this awful conflagration the light has come. On every side I see as in letters of fire, ‘There is no God.’ If it were otherwise these scenes would be impossible. And any being permitting or causing the evils and crimes this dreadful night has witnessed, I shall fear and hate beyond the power of language to express.”

She uttered these words sitting on the sands with multitudes of others, her face (from which Dennis had washed the dust and smoke) looking in the glare so wan and white that he feared, with a sickening dread, that through exposure, terror, or some of the many dangers by which they were surrounded, she might pass into the future world with all her unbelief and spiritual darkness. He yearned over her with a solicitude and pity that he could not express. She seemed so near﻿—indeed he could feel her form tremble, as she kneeled beside her, and supported her by his arm﻿—and yet, in view of her faithless state, how widely were they separated! Should anyone of the many perils about them quench the little candle of her life, which even now flickered faintly, where in the wide universe could he hope to meet her again? God can no doubt console His children and make up to them every loss, but the passionate heart, with its intense human love, clings to its idol none the less. Dennis saw that the fire would probably hem them in on the beach for the remainder of the night and the following day. He determined therefore in every way possible to beguile the weary, perilous hours, and, if she would permit it, to lead her thoughts heavenward. Hence arose from time to time conversations, to which, with joy, he found Christine no longer averse. Indeed, she often introduced them.

===Chinese===
“您只是昏过去了，卢多尔夫小姐。但上帝宛若行了神迹一般，将我们从那座烈焰熔炉中带了出来，眼下我们暂时安全了。”等她从极度的疲惫与惊恐中稍稍缓过神来，丹尼斯便向她讲述了二人脱险的经过。

“这整件事里，我半点儿也看不出有什么上帝，”她说道，“不过是个天大的巧合，而您凭着过人的胆识与镇定抓住了它。在这个骇人的夜晚，我一次又一次得以保全性命，全都是托您一人的福。”

“上帝不过是借我们作祂的器皿，行祂的旨意罢了。真光迟早会照进您心里，到那时您自会领悟更深一层的智慧。”

“在这场可怖的大火里，光倒是已经照进我心里了。四面八方，我都看见仿佛用火焰写就的大字：‘世上并无上帝。’倘若真有上帝，这等惨象绝无可能发生。而任何纵容或降下今晚这般罪恶与祸殃的存在，我都将对祂满怀畏惧与憎恨，非言语所能道尽。”

她坐在沙滩上，置身于成千上万逃难者之中说出这番话；丹尼斯已替她洗去了脸上的灰尘与烟垢，此刻在火光映照下，那张面庞显得如此苍白憔悴，令他心头一阵揪紧，惶恐地担心她会因受寒受惊、或遭逢四周重重险厄中的任何一桩，便带着满腔的不信与灵性黑暗离开人世，步入来生。他对她怀着难以言喻的关切与怜惜。她仿佛近在咫尺——事实上，当他跪在她身旁、用手臂支撑着她时，甚至真切地感受到她身躯的阵阵战栗——然而一想到她毫无信仰的心境，两人之间又仿佛相隔万里！倘若四周无数险境中的任何一桩吹灭了她那此刻已摇曳欲熄的生命微烛，放眼浩瀚宇宙，他又该去何处期盼与她重逢呢？上帝固然能慰藉祂的儿女，弥补他们的一切失落，可那颗炽热的心连同人世间深沉的爱恋，却依然死死依恋着自己的偶像不放。丹尼斯料定今夜余下的时光乃至明天一整天，大火多半都会将他们困在这片海滩上。于是他决意想尽办法排遣这漫长而又危机四伏的时辰，并趁此——只要她不排斥——将她的思绪引向天国。由此，两人便时不时攀谈起来；令他欣喜的是，克里斯蒂娜非但不再抵触这样的话题，甚至往往由她主动挑起。

===Original===
Chafing her hands, he said in accents of the deepest sympathy, “How I pity you, Miss Ludolph! It must indeed be terrible to possess your thoughtful mind, to realize these scenes so keenly, and yet have no faith in a Divine Friend. I cannot explain to you the mystery of evil﻿—why it came, or why it exists. Who can? I am but one of God’s little children, and only know with certainty that my Heavenly Father loves and will take care of me.”

“How do you know it?” she asked, eagerly.

“In several ways. Mainly because I feel it.”

“It all seems so vague and unreal,” she sighed, dreamily. “There is nothing certain, assured. There is no test by which I can at once know the truth.”

“That does not prevent the truth from existing. That some are blind is no proof that color does not exist.”

===Chinese===
他轻轻搓揉着她的双手，语气里满是深切的同情：“卢多尔夫小姐，我真替您感到痛惜！像您这样心思敏锐之人，将眼前这般惨景感受得如此真切，却偏偏不信世上有位神圣的挚友可以依靠，那该是何等煎熬。恶的奥秘——它缘何而来，又为何存在——我无法向您解释清楚。世上又有谁能说清呢？我不过是上帝膝下的一个小小孩童，我唯一笃定知晓的，便是我的天父爱我，且必将看顾我。”

“您怎么知道的？”她急切地追问。

“从好些方面都能知道。最主要的，是因为我真切地感受到了。”

“这一切听起来都那么缥缈，那么虚幻，”她神思恍惚地叹了口气，“没有半点儿确凿无疑的凭据，也没有一种试金石，能让我立时分辨真伪。”

“可这并不妨碍真理本身的存在。世上有人双目失明，并不能证明色彩就不存在。”

===Original===
“But how can you be sure there is a God? You never saw Him.”

“I do not see the heat that scorches us, but I feel it, and know it exists.”

“But I feel the heat the same as yourself, and I have no consciousness of a Divine Being.”

“That does not take away my consciousness that He is my Saviour and Friend. As yet you are spiritually dead. If you were physically dead, you would not feel the heat of this fire.”

“Oh, it is all mystery﻿—darkness,” she cried, piteously.

===Chinese===
“可您怎么能笃定世上真有上帝？您又从未见过祂。”

“此刻炙烤着我们的热浪，我也同样看不见，可我感受得到，也就知道它确然存在。”

“但那热浪我跟您感受得一模一样，可对于什么神圣的存在，我却毫无感知。”

“可这并不能抹去我心中的感知——我深知祂就是我的救主与挚友。只是您的灵性至今仍处在死寂之中。倘若您肉身已死，同样也感受不到这火焰的热度了。”

“唉，全都是谜团——一片漆黑，”她凄然哀呼道。

===Original===
The sun had now risen quite above the waters of the lake, but seen through the lurid smoke which swept over its face, it seemed like one of the great red cinders that were continually sailing over their heads. In the frightful glare, the transition from night to day had scarcely been noted. The long, narrow beach was occupied by thousands of fugitives, who were hemmed in on every side. On the south was the river, skirted with fire, while opposite, on the west, the heat was almost intolerable; on the east were the cold waves of the lake, and on the north a burning pier that they could not cross. Their only hope was to cling to that narrow line where fire and water mingled, and with one element to fight the other. Here again was seen the mingling of all classes which the streets and every place of refuge witnessed. Judges, physicians, statesmen, clergymen, bankers, were jostled by roughs and thieves. The laborer sat on the sand with his family, side by side with the millionaire and his household. The poor debauched woman of the town moaned and shivered in her scant clothing, at a slight remove from the most refined Christian lady. In the unparalleled disaster, all social distinctions were lost, levelled like the beach on which the fugitives cowered. From some groups was heard the voice of prayer; from others, bitter wailings and passionate cries for lost members of the family; others had saved quantities of vile whiskey, if nothing else, and made the scene more ghastly by orgies that seemed not of earth. Added to the liquor were the mad excitement and recklessness which often seize the depraved classes on such occasions. They committed excesses that cannot be mentioned﻿—these drunken, howling, fighting wretches. Obscene epithets and words fell around like blows. And yet all were so occupied with their own misfortunes, sufferings, and danger, as scarcely to heed their neighbors, unless these became very violent.

Upon this heterogeneous mass of humanity the fire rained down almost as we imagine it to have fallen upon the doomed cities of the plain, and the hot breath of the flames scorched the exposed cheek and crisped even eyebrows and hair. Sparks, flakes, cinders, pieces of roof, and fiery pebbles seemed to fill the air, and often cries and shrieks announced that furniture and bedding which had been dragged thither, and even the clothing of women and children, were burning. Added to all the other terrors of the scene was the presence of large numbers of horses and cattle, snorting and plunging in their fright and pain.

But the sound that smote Dennis’s heart with the deepest commiseration was the continuous wail of helpless little children, many of them utterly separated from parents and friends, and in the very agony of fear.

He greatly dreaded the effect of these upon Christine, knowing how, in the luxurious past, she had been shielded from every rough experience. But she at length rallied into something like composure. Her constitution was elastic and full of vitality, and after escaping from immediate danger she again began to hope. Moreover, to a degree that even she could not understand, his presence was a source of strength and courage, and her heart clung to him with desperate earnestness, believing him the sole barrier against immediate death, and (what she dreaded scarcely less) a lonely, wretched existence, should her life be spared.

===Chinese===
此时朝阳早已升出湖面，然而透过横扫太阳表面的惨红浓烟望去，它却活像是一块不断从人们头顶飘飞而过的巨大红炭。在那一片骇人的火光之中，黑夜向白昼的交替几乎无人察觉。狭长的海滩上挤满了数以千计的逃难者，他们四面受困：南面是沿岸烈焰腾腾的河道；正对的西面热浪滚滚，几乎令人窒息；东面是冰冷刺骨的湖浪；北面则是一座燃烧着的栈桥，根本无法通行。他们唯一的指望，便是死死守住那条水火交汇的窄窄岸线，借水克火、勉力求生。在街头与各处避难所屡见不鲜的那一幕众生混杂之景，此刻又在这里重现：法官、名医、政要、牧师与银行家，正被地痞与窃贼推搡挤撞；劳工带着一家老小坐在沙地上，身旁紧挨着的便是百万富翁与其家眷；城中可怜的堕落女子衣衫单薄，在不远处蜷缩呻吟、瑟瑟发抖，身旁相隔不过几步，便是端庄至极的基督徒贵妇。在这场空前浩劫面前，一切门第贵贱荡然无存，被夷平得如同难民们畏缩栖身的这片沙滩一般。人群中，这一簇传出祈祷之声，那一堆响起痛彻心扉的哀号与声声凄厉的呼唤，只为寻找失散的亲人；还有些人别无长物，却偏偏抢出了大批劣质威士忌，在这片炼狱般的天地间纵酒狂欢，把场面搅得愈发阴森可怖。酒力助长了每逢此类乱象便常在堕落之徒身上发作的癫狂兴奋与肆无忌惮。这帮醉醺醺、嗷嗷乱叫、扭打作一团的恶棍，干出了种种不堪言表的暴行。污言秽语与下流骂声如同拳脚般四下乱飞。然而，每个人全都自顾不暇，沉溺于自身的厄运、苦痛与险境之中，只要旁人不是闹得太过凶暴，几乎都无暇顾及。

烈焰如雨般倾泻在这群五方杂处的人潮头上，简直如同我们想象中天火降临那遭天罚的平原诸城一般；火焰喷出的炽热气息炙烤着人们裸露的面颊，甚至把眉毛与头发都烤卷了。火星、飞灰、余烬、碎裂的屋顶木片以及滚烫的石砾仿佛塞满了整片天空；时不时便有惊呼与尖叫骤起，宣告好不容易拖到这儿来的家具被褥，乃至妇孺身上的衣裳，又被火星引燃了。更添几分惨厉的是，大群马匹与牛羊也混杂其间，因惊恐与灼痛而嘶鸣打着响鼻，四下狂奔乱窜。

然而，最令丹尼斯揪心刺痛、油然而生无穷怜悯的，却是那些孤立无援的小儿们连绵不断的哭号——其中许多孩子与父母亲友彻底失散，正陷入极度的惊恐煎熬之中。

他极为担心这番惨状会给克里斯蒂娜带来太大刺激，深知她在往昔养尊处优的日子里，向来受尽呵护，从未见识过半点人间粗粝。但她终于还是振作起来，恢复了几分镇定。她体魄强健、颇具韧性，又充满了生命力，既已逃脱了迫在眉睫的死劫，心中便又重燃起求生的希望。何况，连她自己也说不清为何竟会如此——丹尼斯就在身旁，本身便成了她力量与勇气的源泉；她的心怀着近乎绝望的虔诚紧紧依附着他，认定他是横亘在自己与眼下死神之间的唯一屏障，也是倘若大难不死、日后免于孤苦凄凉度日的唯一依托——后者在她心目中的可怕程度，几乎丝毫不亚于死亡本身。

===Original===
Though he never lost sight of her for a moment, and kept continually wetting her hair and person, he found time to render assistance to others, and, by carrying his hat full of water here and there, extinguished many a dangerous spark. He also, again and again, snatched up little children from under the trampling hoofs of frightened horses.

As she watched him, so self-forgetful and fearless, she realized more and more vividly that he was sustained and animated by some mighty principle that she knew nothing of, and could not understand. The impression grew upon her that he was right and she wrong. Though it all remained in mystery and doubt, she could not resist the logic of true Christian action.

But as the day advanced the flames grew hotter, and their breath more withering. About noon Dennis noticed that some shanties on the sand near them were in danger of catching fire and perilling all in that vicinity. Therefore he said, “Miss Ludolph, stay here where I leave you for a little time, so that I may know just where to find you.”

“Oh, do not leave me!” she pleaded: “I have no one in the wide world to help me except you.”

“I shall not be beyond call. You see those shanties there; if possible we must keep them from burning, or the fire will come too near for safety.” Then, starting forward, he cried, “Who will volunteer to keep the fire back? All must see that if those buildings burn we shall be in danger.”

===Chinese===
他虽一刻也未曾让视线离开过她，还不断替她淋湿头发与衣衫，却仍抽空去搭救旁人——拿帽子盛满湖水四处奔走，扑灭了不知多少险象环生的火星。他还一次次冲上前去，从受惊马匹的乱蹄之下抢救出一个个幼童。

望着他如此忘我无畏的身影，她愈发真切地体会到，支撑并鼓舞着他的，定然是某种她一无所知、亦无法参透的强大信念。她心头渐渐生出一种念头：或许他是对的，而自己错了。尽管一切依旧笼罩在迷雾与疑云之中，可真正基督徒所展现出的行动逻辑，却让她无论如何也无法抗拒。

可随着白昼渐深，火势愈发猛烈，炽热的气浪也更加烤人。将近正午时，丹尼斯发觉近旁沙滩上的几间棚屋随时可能着火，危及这一带的所有人。于是他说道：“卢多尔夫小姐，请您暂且待在这儿我安顿您的地方，好叫我待会儿一找便能找着您。”

“啊，别撇下我！”她哀求道，“放眼这广阔天地，除了您之外，我再没有半个可以指望的人了。”

“我不会走远，一唤就能听见的。您瞧见那几间棚屋了吗？只要还来得及，咱们就得保住它们别烧起来，不然火势逼得太近，大伙儿可就危险了。”说完，他大步往前奔去，高声呼喊：“有谁自告奋勇来挡住火势？大伙儿都瞧得见，那几间屋子一着火，咱们全都要遭殃！”

===Original===
Several men stepped forward, and with hats and anything that would hold water they began to wet the old rookeries. But the fiery storm swooped steadily down on them, and their efforts were as futile as if they had tried to beat back the wind. Suddenly a mass of flame leaped upon the buildings, and in a moment they were all ablaze.

“Into the lake, quick!” cried Dennis, and all rushed for the cool waters.

Lifting Christine from the sand, and passing his arm around her trembling, shivering form, he plunged through the breakers, and the crowd pressed after him. Indeed they pushed him so far out in the cold waves that he nearly lost his footing, and for a few moments Christine lost hers altogether, and added her cries to those of the terror-stricken multitude. But pushing in a little nearer the shore, he held her firmly and said with the confidence that again inspired hope: “Courage, Miss Ludolph. With God’s help I will save you yet.”

Even as she clung to him in the water, she looked into his face. He was regarding her so kindly, so pitifully, that a great and generous impulse, the richest, ripest fruit of her human love, throbbed at her heart, and faltered from her lips﻿—“Mr. Fleet, I am not worthy of this risk on your part. If you will leave me you can save your own life, and your life is worth so much more than mine!”

True and deep must have been the affection that could lead Christine Ludolph to say such words to any human being. There was a time when, in her creed, all the world existed but to minister to her. But she was not sorry to see the look of pained surprise which came into Dennis’s face and to hear him say, very sadly: “Miss Ludolph, I did not imagine that you could think me capable of that. I had the good fortune to rescue Miss Brown last night, at greater peril than this, and do you think I would leave you?”

===Chinese===
几名男子站了出来，抄起帽子和手头一切能盛水的家伙，开始往那些破旧木屋上泼水。然而烈焰风暴铺天盖地直扑而来，他们的挣扎徒劳得宛如举手去拍打狂风。刹那间，一团烈火猛扑上屋顶，转眼工夫几间棚屋便全烧成了一片火海。

“快下湖去！”丹尼斯大喝一声，众人纷纷朝冰凉的湖水狂奔。

他从沙地上抱起克里斯蒂娜，一臂揽紧她战栗发抖的身躯，涉过拍岸的浪花冲入湖中，身后人群一拥而上。人潮推搡得太猛，竟将他一路挤进冰冷的深水里，险些站立不稳；克里斯蒂娜更是有片刻双脚完全悬空，禁不住随惊惶失措的人群一同惊呼起来。好在丹尼斯奋力往岸边又挪回了些许，稳稳托住她，用那足以重新点燃希望的笃定嗓音说道：“振作起来，卢多尔夫小姐。蒙上帝佑助，我定能把您救出去。”

就这样在水中紧紧依偎着他时，她仰起脸凝望着他。他正用那般温柔、那般怜惜的眼神看着她，霎时间，一股崇高而无私的冲动——那是她人间真爱所结出的最丰盈、最醇熟的硕果——在她心头剧烈搏动起来，化作颤抖的话语脱口而出：“弗利特先生，我不值得您为我冒这般险。您若是撇下我，自个儿本可以逃出生天的，况且您的性命比我金贵不知多少倍！”

得是何等真挚深沉的爱意，才能让克里斯蒂娜·卢多尔夫对世上任何一个人说出这样一番话啊。曾几何时，在她的信条里，普天之下万物存在唯一的意义便是侍奉于她。可此刻，瞧见丹尼斯脸上浮现出既痛心又惊愕的神色，听见他万分伤感地开口，她心中却并未感到懊悔——他说道：“卢多尔夫小姐，我万没想到，在您眼中我竟是会干出这种事的人。昨夜在比这还要凶险百倍的境地里，我都幸而救出了布朗小姐，难道您以为我会抛下您不管吗？”

===Original===
“You are a true knight, Mr. Fleet,” she said, humbly, “and the need or danger of every defenceless woman is alike a sacred claim upon you.”

Dennis was about to intimate that, though this was true in knightly creed, still among all the women in the world there might be a preference, when a score of horses, driven before the fire, and goaded by the burning cinders, rushed down the beach, into the water, right among the human fugitives.

Again went up the cry of agony and terror. Some were no doubt stricken down not to rise again. In the melee Dennis pushed out into deeper water, where the frantic animals could not plunge upon him. A child floated near, and he snatched it up. As soon as the poor brutes became quiet, clasping Christine with his right arm and holding up the child with the other, he waded into shallow water.

The peril was now perhaps at its height, and all were obliged to wet their heads, to keep even their hair from singeing. Those on the beach threw water on each other without cessation. Many a choice bit of property﻿—it might be a piano, or an express-wagon loaded with the richest furs and driven to the beach as a place of fancied security﻿—now caught fire, and added to the heat and consternation.

===Chinese===
“您真是一位名副其实的骑士，弗利特先生，”她谦卑地说道，“世上每一位弱女子一旦身处危难、急需援手，对您而言都同样是一份神圣的托付。”

丹尼斯正要委婉表明，骑士的信条固然如此，然而在普天下的女子之中，总有一位是教人另眼相看、偏爱有加的——话未出口，忽有二十来匹马被烈焰驱赶、又被飞溅的灼热余烬刺痛，发狂般冲下沙滩，直扑进湖水里，一头撞进逃难的人群当中。

惨痛与惊骇的呼号再度四起。毫无疑问，定有人被踏翻在地，再也没能爬起来。混乱之中，丹尼斯护着她退往更深的水域，免得那些发疯的牲口扑撞到身上。恰巧一个孩童漂到近旁，他顺手一把捞了起来。待那群可怜的畜生总算安静下来，他右臂紧搂着克里斯蒂娜，另一只手高举起那个孩子，涉水走回浅滩。

此刻的险情恐怕已臻顶点，所有人都不得不频频打湿头顶，才不致连头发都被烤焦。留在沙滩上的人你泼我、我泼你，一刻也不敢停歇。好些贵重家当——兴许是一架钢琴，又或是一辆装满最上等毛皮、原以为拉到海滩上便万无一失的快运货车——如今也都燃起熊熊大火，平添了几分灼热与惊惶。

===Original===
When this hour of extreme danger had passed, standing with the cold billows of the lake breaking round him, and the billows of fire still rolling overhead, Dennis began to sing in his loud, clear voice:

> “Jesus, lover of my soul,
 

 Let me to thy bosom fly,
 

 While the billows near me roll,
 

 While the tempest still is high.”

Voice after voice joined in, some loud and strong, but others weak and trembling﻿—the pitiful cry of poor terror-stricken women to the only One who it seemed could help them in their bitter extremity. Never before were those beautiful words sung in such accents of clinging, touching faith. Its sweet cadence was heard above the roar of the flames and the breakers.

Christine could only cling weeping to Dennis.

===Chinese===
当这最凶险的时刻终于熬过去后，丹尼斯站在身畔湖水冷浪拍打之中，头顶依旧火浪翻涌，竟放开洪亮清越的嗓音高唱起来：

> “耶稣，我灵魂的爱主，
>
> 求容我飞入你怀中，
>
> 任惊涛在我身旁翻卷，
>
> 任狂飙依旧正汹涌。”

一个接一个的声音汇了进来，有的高亢浑厚，有的却微弱战栗——那是吓破了胆的可怜女人们，在绝境苦痛之中向那似乎唯一能施以援手的神明发出的凄切呼求。这般优美的词句，从未曾以如此死心塌地、动人心魄的虔信唱响过。那甜美柔婉的旋律压过了烈焰的咆哮与巨浪的轰鸣，在天地间久久回荡。

克里斯蒂娜唯有一面流泪，一面紧紧依偎着丹尼斯。

===Original===
When the hymn ceased, in harshest discord the voice of a half-drunken man grated on their ears.

“An’ what in bloody blazes does yer Jasus burn us all up for, I’d like to know. Sure an’ he’s no right to send us to hell before our time.”

“Oh, hush! hush!” cried a dozen voices, shocked and pained.

“Divil a bit will I hush, sure; an’ haven’t I as good a right to have me say as that singin’ parson!”

“You are an Irishman, are you not?” said Dennis, now venturing out of the water.

===Chinese===
圣诗刚一停歇，一个半醉男子的刺耳嗓音便如同最难听的杂音般直钻进众人耳膜。

“见鬼了，老子倒想知道，你们那位耶稣干嘛要把咱们全烧成灰！真没天理，他凭什么不等咱们阳寿尽了就把人打进地狱！”

“哎呀，住嘴！快住嘴！”十来个人又惊又痛，齐声喝止。

“要我闭嘴没门儿！我就跟那个唱圣诗的牧师一样，照样有资格开口说两句！”

“您是位爱尔兰老兄，没错吧？”丹尼斯这时壮起胆子从水里走了出来，问道。

===Original===
“Yis! what have ye got to say agin it?” asked the man, belligerent at once.

“Did you ever know an Irishman refuse to do what a lady asked of him?”

“Faith no, and I niver will.”

“Then this lady, who is sick and suffering, asks you to please keep still, and I will be still also; so that’s fair.”

The Irishman scratched his head a moment, and said in a quieter tone, “Since ye spake so civil and dacent, I’ll do as ye sez; and here’s to the leddy’s health;” and he finished a bottle of whiskey, which he soon laid him out on the beach.

===Chinese===
“是啊！你有啥不服气的？”那汉子立时摆出一副挑衅架势反问道。

“您可曾听说过哪个爱尔兰汉子会回绝一位淑女的请求？”

“凭良心说，没听说过，我也绝不会干那种事。”

“那么这位小姐此刻身子不适、正受着苦，她恳请您行个好、保持安静，我也一道闭嘴；这样一来，咱们可就两平了。”

那爱尔兰汉子挠了挠头，放低声音说道：“既然你话说得这么客气厚道，那我就依你；来，祝这位小姐安康！”说完便一口气喝干了那瓶威士忌，没过多久酒劲发作，他便直挺挺地醉倒在了沙滩上。

===Original===
“Thank you! Thank you!” said grateful voices on every side.

Dennis found the mother of the child and gave it to her; and then causing Christine to sit down near the water, where he could easily throw it on her, he stood at her side, vigilant and almost tender in his solicitude. Her tears were falling very fast, and he presently stooped down and said, gently, “Miss Ludolph, I think the worst of the danger is over.”

“Oh, Mr. Fleet!” she whispered, “dreadful as it may seem to you, the words of that drunken brute there are nearer the language of my heart than those of your sweet hymn. How can a good God permit such creatures and evils to exist?”

“Again I must say to you,” said Dennis, “that I cannot explain the mystery of evil. But I know this, God is superior to it; He will at last triumph over it. The Bible reveals Him to us as able and as seeking to deliver all who will trust Him and work with Him, and those who venture out upon His promises find them true. Miss Ludolph, this is not merely a matter of theory, argument, and belief. It is more truly a matter of experience. The Bible invites, ‘Oh, taste and see that the Lord is good.’ I have tasted and know He is. I have trusted Him for years, and He never failed me.”

“You certainly have been sustained throughout this dreadful scene by a principle that I cannot understand, but I would give all the world to possess it.”

===Chinese===
“多谢您！多谢您了！”四周一片感激之声响起。

丹尼斯寻到那孩子的母亲，把孩子交还给她；随后扶着克里斯蒂娜在水边坐下——这样他随时都能掬水泼在她身上——自己则守立在她身旁，既警觉万分，又满怀近乎温柔的怜惜。她的泪水簌簌滑落，过了一会儿，他弯下腰，轻声说道：“卢多尔夫小姐，我看最凶险的关头已经过去了。”

“啊，弗利特先生！”她低声说道，“尽管在您听来或许无比骇人，可刚才那醉醺醺的粗汉所说的话，倒比您那曲温柔甜美的圣诗更贴近我的心声。一位良善的上帝，怎能容忍这等恶徒与祸患存在于世上呢？”

“我还是得对您说，”丹尼斯答道，“恶的奥秘我无法解释。但我深知一点：上帝凌驾于恶之上，祂终究必将战胜恶。《圣经》向我们启示，祂大有能力，也切望拯救一切肯信靠祂、并与祂同工之人；凡敢于凭信踏上祂应许之道的人，都会印证祂的应许句句真实。卢多尔夫小姐，这并不单单是理论、辩论与教义的问题，更真切地说，这是切身体验的问题。《圣经》发出邀约：‘你们要尝尝，便知道主是美善的。’我已经尝过，也深知祂确实美善。这么多年来我一直信靠祂，祂从未令我失望。”

“在这番骇人听闻的劫难中，支撑着您的确然是一种我无法理解的信念；但为了能拥有它，我甘愿舍弃整个世界。”

===Original===
“You may possess it, Miss Ludolph.”

“How? how?” she asked, eagerly.

“Do you wish to believe as I do?”

“Yes, indeed; and yet my heart rebels against a God who permits, even if He does not cause, all this evil.”

“Does it rebel against a Being who from first to last tries to save men from evil?”

“Tries! tries! what an expression to apply to a God! Why does He not do it in every case?”

===Chinese===
“您可以拥有它的，卢多尔夫小姐。”

“怎么才能拥有？怎么才能？”她急切地追问。

“您愿意像我一样去信吗？”

“我当然愿意；可是，一想到上帝纵然不曾降下这一切灾祸，却容许它们发生，我的心便不由自主地抗拒起来。”

“那它还会抗拒一位自始至终都在竭力救世人脱离罪恶与灾祸的主吗？”

“‘竭力’！‘竭力’！这种字眼怎能用在一位上帝身上！祂为何不把每一桩祸患都彻底制止呢？”

===Original===
“Because multitudes will not let Him.”

“Oh, that is worse still! Surely, Mr. Fleet, you let your reason have nothing to do with your faith. How can a poor and weak being like myself prevent an Almighty one from doing what He pleases?”

“I am stronger than you, Miss Ludolph, and yet I could not have saved you tonight unless you had first trusted me, and then done everything in your power to further my efforts.”

“But your power is human and limited, and you say God is all-powerful.”

“Yes, but it is His plan and purpose never to save us against our will. He has made us in His own image and endowed us with reason, conscience, and a will to choose between good and evil. He appeals to these noble faculties from first to last. He has given us hearts, and seeks to win them by revealing His love to us. More than all, His Spirit, present in the world, uses every form of truth in persuading and making us willing to become His true children. So you see that neither on the one hand does God gather us up like driftwood nor does He on the other drag us at His chariot wheels, unwilling captives, as did those who, at various times, have sought to overrun the world by force. God seeks to conquer the world by the might of the truth, by the might of love.”

===Chinese===
“因为世上无数人根本不肯容祂那样做。”

“哦，这话就更离奇了！弗利特先生，您定然是把理性全抛到信仰外头去了。像我这般渺小脆弱的凡人，怎可能阻拦一位全能者行祂所愿之事？”

“卢多尔夫小姐，我的力气比您大得多，然而今晚若非您先信得过我，继而竭尽全力配合我的营救，我也照样救不了您。”

“可您的力量只是凡人有限之力，而您口中的上帝却是无所不能的呀。”

“正是如此，然而上帝的旨意与安排，便是不违逆我们的自由意志来拯救我们。祂按着自己的形象造了我们，赋予我们理性、良知，以及在善恶之间自行抉择的意志。自始至终，祂都在向人身上的这些崇高秉赋发出呼召。祂赐予我们一颗心，又借着向我们显明祂的慈爱来赢取这颗心。不仅如此，祂运行在世间的圣灵，更以千般真理形式不断劝勉感化，使我们甘心乐意成为祂真正的儿女。所以您看，上帝既不会像打捞浮木那样把我们一把抓起，也不会像历史上那些妄图凭武力征服世界的暴君一般，把不甘屈服的俘虏绑在战车轮后强行拖走。上帝所要凭藉征服世界的，乃是真理的大能，乃是爱的大能。”

===Original===
Christine was hanging with the most eager interest on his words. Suddenly his eyes, which had expressed such a kindly and almost tender interest in her, blazed with indignation, and he darted up the beach. Turning around she saw, at some little distance, a young woman most scantily clad, clinging desperately to a bundle which a large, coarse man was trying to wrench from her. The wretch, finding that he could not loosen her hold, struck her in the face with such force that she fell stunned upon the ground, and the bundle flew out of her hand. He eagerly snatched it up, believing it to contain jewelry. Before he could escape he was confronted by an unexpected enemy. But Dennis was in a passion, and withal weak and exhausted, while his adversary was cool, and an adept in the pugilistic art. The two men fought savagely, and Christine, forgetting herself in her instinctive desire to help Dennis, was rushing to his side, crying, “If there is a man here worthy of the name, let him strike for the right!” but before she and others could reach the combatants the thief had planted his fist on Dennis’s temple. Though the latter partially parried the blow, it fell with such force as to extend him senseless on the earth. The villain, with a shout of derision, snatched up the bundle and dashed off apparently toward the fire. There was but a feeble attempt made to follow him. Few understood the case, and indeed scenes of violence and terror had become so common that the majority had grown apathetic, save in respect to their personal well-being.

Christine lifted the pale face, down which the blood was trickling, into her lap, and cried, in a tone of indescribable anguish, “Oh, he is dead! he is dead!”

“Oh, no, miss; he is not dead, I guess,” said a good-natured voice near. “Let me bring a hatful of water from the lake, and that’ll bring him to.”

And so it did. Dennis opened his eyes, put his hand to his head, and then looked around. But when he saw Christine bending over him with tearful eyes, and realized how tenderly she had pillowed his aching head, he started up with a deep flush of pleasure, and said: “Do not be alarmed, Miss Ludolph; I was only stunned for a moment. Where is the thief?”

“Oh, they let him escape,” said Christine, indignantly.

===Chinese===
克里斯蒂娜正怀着最热切的兴致倾听他一字一句。忽然之间，他那双先前还流露着温厚怜惜之情的眼睛里猛地迸出怒火，整个人如箭般沿沙滩上方疾冲而去。她回过头，只见不远处有个衣不蔽体的年轻女子正死死抱住一个包袱，而一个高大粗壮的汉子正试图从她手中硬抢。那恶徒发觉掰不开她的手，竟狠狠一拳照着她的脸砸了过去，力道之大将她打得昏死倒地，包袱也脱手飞了出去。那恶棍以为里头藏着金银首饰，急忙一把抓起。可还没等他逃走，面前便骤然拦下一名不速之敌。然而丹尼斯本就在盛怒之下，加之早已精疲力竭，而那对手却冷静沉着，且深谙拳斗路数。两人凶狠地扭打在一起；克里斯蒂娜本能地只想帮丹尼斯，顿时顾不得自身安危，朝他那边飞奔过去，一路高喊：“这儿要是有个配称作男子汉的人，就替公道出把力吧！”可还没等她和其他几人赶到搏斗处，那贼人一记重拳已正中丹尼斯的太阳穴。尽管丹尼斯勉强格挡了一下，那一拳力道依然极重，直将他打得不省人事，扑倒在地。那恶棍发出一声讥笑，抄起包袱拔腿逃窜，看去竟是朝火场方向奔去了。旁人只敷衍追了几步便作罢。没几个人弄得清来龙去脉；说到底，这般暴力与惨剧早已司空见惯，大多数人除了自己的生死安危之外，对旁的事早已麻木不仁了。

克里斯蒂娜将他那张淌着鲜血的苍白脸庞扶枕在自己膝头，用一种难以名状的悲恸嗓音哭喊道：“啊，他死了！他死了！”

“噢，不会的，小姐，依我看他没死，”近旁一个热心肠的声音说道，“容我从湖里舀一帽子水来，准能把他浇醒。”

果然如此。丹尼斯睁开眼睛，抬手摸了摸头，随即环顾四周。可当他望见克里斯蒂娜正含泪俯身看着自己，又发觉她方才竟那般温柔地让自己的痛首枕在她膝上，顿时心头一喜，双颊泛起深深的红晕，猛地坐起身说道：“别害怕，卢多尔夫小姐，我不过是一时被打晕罢了。那贼人呢？”

“唉，他们叫他给逃了，”克里斯蒂娜愤愤不平地说道。

===Original===
“Shame!” cried Dennis, regaining his feet rather unsteadily.

“Wal, stranger, a good many wrongs tonight must go unrighted.”

The poor girl who had been robbed sat on the sands swaying backing and forth, wringing her hands, and crying that she had lost everything.

“Well, my poor friend, that is about the case with the most of us. We may be thankful that we have our lives. Here is my coat,” for her shoulders and neck were bare; “and if you will come down to the lake this lady,” pointing to Christine, “will bathe the place where the brute struck you.”

“Shall I not give up my shawl to some of these poor creatures?” asked Christine.

===Chinese===
“真叫人汗颜！”丹尼斯喊了一声，摇摇晃晃地撑着站起身来。

“唉，这位老兄，今晚多得是不平事儿，怕是没处桩桩讨公道喽。”

那遭了抢劫的可怜姑娘坐在沙地上，身子前仰后合地晃着，一个劲儿绞着双手哭号，说自己什么全丢光了。

“唉，我可怜的朋友，咱们大伙儿十有八九也都是这般光景。能保住一条命，就该谢天谢地了。这件外套给您披上，”——因为她肩颈正光裸着——“您要是愿意到湖边来，这位小姐，”他指了指克里斯蒂娜，“会替您洗洗那畜生打伤的地方。”

“我要不要把披肩也让给这些可怜人穿呢？”克里斯蒂娜问道。

===Original===
“No, Miss Ludolph, I do not know how long we may be kept here; but I fear we shall suffer as much from cold as from heat, and your life might depend upon keeping warm.”

“I will do whatever you bid me,” she said, looking gratefully at him.

“That is the way to feel and act toward God,” he said, gently.

But with sudden impetuosity she answered: “I cannot see what He has just permitted to happen before my eyes. Right has not triumphed, but the foulest wrong.”

“You do not see the end, Miss Ludolph.”

===Chinese===
“使不得，卢多尔夫小姐，我还不知咱们得在这儿困上多久；只怕咱们挨冻的苦头决不亚于受热，您的性命兴许正全指望着御寒保暖呢。”

“您吩咐什么，我就照做便是，”她感激地望着他说道。

“人对待上帝，正该怀着这样的心意去行事啊，”他轻声说道。

可她骤然急切地答道：“方才祂竟容许在眼皮底下发生这等事，我实在想不通。得胜的不是公义，而是最卑劣的邪恶。”

“卢多尔夫小姐，您还没有看到结局呢。”

===Original===
“But I must judge from what I see.”

After she had bathed the poor girl’s face, comforted and reassured her, Dennis took up the conversation again and found Christine eager to listen. Pausing every few moments to throw water over his companion, he said: “Faith is beyond reason, beyond knowledge, though not contrary to them. You are judging as we do not judge about the commonest affairs﻿—from a few isolated, mysterious facts, instead of carefully looking the subject all over. You pass by what is plain and well understood to what is obscure, and from that point seek to understand Christianity. Every science has its obscure points and mysteries, but who begins with those to learn the science? Can you ignore the fact that millions of highly intelligent people, with every motive to know the truth, have satisfied themselves as to the reality of our faith? Our Bible system of truth may contain much that is obscure, even as the starry vault has distances that no eye or telescope can penetrate, and as this little earth has mysteries that science cannot solve, but there is enough known and understood to satisfy us perfectly. Let me assure you, Miss Ludolph, that Christianity rests on broad truths, and is sustained by arguments that no candid mind can resist after patiently considering them.”

She shook her head, silenced perhaps, but not satisfied.

===Chinese===
“可我只能凭自己亲眼所见的来评断。”

等她替那可怜姑娘清洗过脸庞，又好言抚慰、宽解了她一番之后，丹尼斯重又接上先前的话题，见克里斯蒂娜正急切地等着聆听。他隔一会儿便停下来往同伴身上泼些湖水，接着说道：“信仰超越了理性，也超越了知识，却并不与它们相悖。您眼下评断这件事的方式，就连日常最寻常的事务咱们也不会那样去断——您只凭几桩孤立而又玄奥难解的事实就下结论，却没有审慎地通盘审视全局。您绕过了那些平白浅显、早已为人熟知的道理，径直钻进晦暗难明之处，想从那里着手去理解基督教。世上每一门学问都有其晦涩疑难与奥秘所在，可又有谁学一门学问是从那些疑难奥秘入手的呢？难道您能视而不见吗——千百万极具才智、且怀着种种求真动机的人，经过求索之后，都已对我们信仰的真实性深信不疑。我们《圣经》的真理体系固然难免有好些深奥难解之处，正如浩瀚星穹有着肉眼与望远镜皆难以穿透的遥远深空，正如这小小地球也有着科学尚无法破解的奥秘；然而，其中业已为人所知、所明悟的部分，已足以令我们心悦诚服。卢多尔夫小姐，请容我向您保证，基督教根植于宽广宏阔的真理之上，其立论之坚实，凡是坦诚之心只要肯耐心推究，便绝无可能抗拒。”

她摇了摇头，或许是无言以对，却仍未信服。

## XLV “Prayer Is Mighty”﻿—Christine a Christian / 第四十五章 “祈祷大有能力”——克里斯蒂娜成了基督徒

===Original===
The day was now declining, and the fire in that part of the city opposite them had so spent itself that they were beginning to have a little respite from immediate danger. The fiery storm of sparks and cinders was falling mostly to the northward.

Dennis now ventured to sit down almost for the first time, for he was wearied beyond endurance. The tremendous danger and excitements, and the consciousness of peril to the one most dear to him, had kept him alert long after he ought to have had rest, but overtaxed nature now asserted its rights, and the moment the sharp spur of danger was removed he was overpowered by sleep.

Christine spoke to him as he sat near, but even to her (a thing he could not have imagined possible) he returned an incoherent reply.

“My poor friend, you do indeed need rest,” said she, in kindest accents.

He heard her voice like a sweet and distant harmony in a dream, swayed a moment, and would have fallen over in utter unconsciousness on the sands, had she not glided to his side and caught his head upon her lap.

===Chinese===
此时白昼已近黄昏，他们对面那片城区的火势已渐渐烧尽，紧迫的危险总算稍稍缓和下来。那场火星与灰烬交织的烈焰风暴，此刻大多落在了北面。

丹尼斯这才头一回敢安心坐下——他早已精疲力竭，苦撑到了极限。此前那惊心动魄的险境与亢奋，加上心头牵挂着最挚爱之人的安危，让他在早该歇息的时候依然强打精神；如今透支过度的身体终于讨回了自己的权利，危险的尖刺刚一撤去，睡意便排山倒海般将他彻底吞没。

克里斯蒂娜见他坐在身旁，便开口同他说话，可就连面对她——这本是他做梦也想不到的事——他含糊回应的话也已语无伦次。

“我可怜的朋友，你确实太需要歇一歇了。”她用无比温柔关切的语调说道。

他听见她的声音，仿佛梦中传来的遥远而甜美的乐音；身子晃了一晃，眼看就要彻底失去知觉栽倒在沙地上，亏得她轻盈地滑到他身旁，将他的头稳稳接在了自己膝上。

===Original===
In the heavy stupor that follows the utmost exhaustion, Dennis slept hour after hour. The rest of the day was a perfect blank to him. But Christine, partially covering and shading his face with the edge of her shawl, bent over him as patient in watching as he had been brave in her deliverance. It was beautiful to see the features once so cold and haughty, now sweet with more than womanly tenderness. There upon that desolate beach, cold, hungry, homeless, shelterless, she was happier than she had been for months. But she trembled as she thought of the future; everything was so uncertain. She seemed involved in a labyrinth of dangers and difficulties from which she could see no escape. She knew that both store and home had gone, and probably most, if not all, of her father’s fortune. She felt that these losses might greatly modify his plans, and really hoped that they would lead him to remain in this country. She felt almost sure that he would not go back to Germany a poor man, and to remain in America was to give her a chance of happiness, and happiness now meant life with him over whom she bent. For a long time she had felt that she could give up all the world for him, but now existence would scarcely be endurable without him. In proportion to the slowness with which her love had been kindled was its intensity﻿—the steady, concentrated passion of a strong, resolute nature, for the first time fully aroused. All indecision passed from her mind, and she was ready to respond whenever he should speak; but woman’s silence sealed her lips, and more than maiden delicacy masked her heart. While she bent over him with an expression that, had he opened his eyes, might have caused him to imagine for a moment that his sleep had been death, and he had wakened in heaven, yet he must needs awake to find that the look and manner of earth had returned. Her sensitive pride made her guarded even in expressing her gratitude, and she purposed to slip his head off upon her shawl whenever he showed signs of awakening, so that he might believe that the earth only had been his resting-place.

But now in his unconsciousness, and unnoted by all around, indeed more completely isolated by the universal misery and apathy about her than she could have been in her own home, with a delicious sense of security, she bent her eyes upon him, and toyed daintily with the curling locks on his brow. Whatever the future might be, nothing should rob her of the strange, unexpected happiness of this opportunity to be near him, purchased at such cost.

As she sat there and saw the fire rush and roar away to the northward, and the sun decline over the ruins of her earthly fortune, she thought more deeply and earnestly of life than ever before.
