Moreover, I confess that I hope to derive great advantages from this labor.”
“In what way?” she asked, with a slight frown, imagining that he thought of extra pay.
“Because unconsciously you will give me instruction, and I hope that you are not unwilling that I should gain such hints and suggestions as I can from the display of your taste that I must witness.”
“Not at all,” said she, laughing. “I see that you are ambitious to learn your business and rise in the store.”
“I am ambitious to gain a knowledge of one of the noblest callings.”
“What is that?”
“Art.”
“What!” said she, with a half-scornful smile; “are you a disciple of art?”
“Yes; why not?”
“Well, I do not wish to hurt your feelings, but, to tell you the honest truth, it seems but the other day that you were Pat Murphy.”
“But am I a Pat Murphy?” he asked, with gentle dignity.
“No, Mr. Fleet; I will do you the justice to say that I think you very much above your station.”
“I am sufficiently a democrat, Miss Ludolph, to believe that a man can be a man in any honest work.”
“And I, Mr. Fleet, am not in the least degree a democrat.”
Which fact she proceeded to prove by ordering him about for the next hour like the most absolute little despot that ever queened it over a servile province in the dark ages. Bat it was rather difficult to keep up this style of dictatorship with Dennis. He seemed so intelligent and polite that she often had it to her tongue to ask his opinion on certain points. Toward the last she did so, and the opinion he gave, she admitted to herself, was judicious; but for a purpose of her own she disregarded it, and took a different way.
Dennis at once saw through her plan of arrangement. In the centre of that side of the room which he had cleared, she caused him to hang one of the largest and finest pictures, which, under Mr. Schwartz’s management, had been placed in a corner. Around the central painting all the others were to be grouped, according to color, subject, and merit. At the same time each wall was to have a character of its own. Such a task as this would require no little thought, study, and comparison; and Miss Ludolph was one to see delicate points of difference which most observers would not notice. It was her purpose to make the room bloom out naturally like a great flower.

话音刚落，她便用实际行动印证了这句宣言——在接下来的整整一个钟头里，她像极了中世纪黑暗时代里统治某个顺从行省的专横小女皇，居高临下地对他指手画脚、发号施令。不过面对丹尼斯时，这副暴君架子倒也不大容易一直端得下去。他显得如此机敏干练、彬彬有礼，好几次她话都到了嘴边，差点要开口征询他在某些细节上的意见。临近收尾时，她果真问了一句；而他给出的见解，连她自己心里也不得不暗暗承认颇为精当；只是为了某种自个儿的心思，她偏偏故意不予采纳，另挑了别一种摆法。

This careful selection of pictures was necessarily slow, and Dennis rejoiced that their united work would not soon be over.
To her surprise she often saw his eyes instinctively turning to the same picture that she was about to select, and perceived that he had divined her plan without a word of explanation, and that his taste was constantly according with hers in producing the desired effects. Though all this filled her with astonishment, she revealed no sign of it to him. At eight she said: “That will do for today. We have made a good beginning﻿—better indeed than I had hoped. But how is it, Mr. Fleet, since you are such an uncompromising democrat, that you permit a young lady to order you about in this style?”
Dennis smiled and said: “It seems perfectly natural for you to speak in this way, and it does not appear offensive as it might in another. Moreover, I have voluntarily taken this position and am in honor bound to accept all it involves.”
“But which was the controlling motive of your mind?”
“Well, a few seem born to command, and it is a pleasure to obey,” said Dennis, paying a strong but honest compliment to the natural little autocrat.
“Indeed, Mr. Fleet, do church members flatter?” said she, secretly much pleased.
“I did not mean to flatter,” said he, flushing. “They who have power should use it like the All-powerful﻿—gently, considerately.”
It was her turn to flush now, and she said, “Oh, I perceive, the compliment was the sugarcoating of the little homily to follow.”
“I have no such diplomacy as you credit me with,” said Dennis, looking straight into her eyes with honest frankness. “I merely spoke my passing thought.”
“But he has fine eyes,” said she to herself, and then she said to him: “Very well, I certainly will give you credit for being superior to your position. Be ready again tomorrow at the same hour;” and with a smile somewhat kindly she vanished.
Somehow she seemed to take the light out of the room with her. The pictures suddenly looked tame and ordinary, and everything commonplace. Here was an effect not exactly artistic, which he could not understand. He sighed, he scarcely knew why.
But the day’s duties came with a rush, and soon he was utterly absorbed in them.
That evening Dennis was much cheered by Mr. Bruder’s comments on his sketches.

令克里斯蒂娜颇感惊异的是，她常常留意到，自己正准备选中哪一幅画，丹尼斯的目光竟已本能地率先落在了同一幅画上；她这才发觉，自己根本无需多费半句唇舌解释，他便已心有灵犀地领会了她的全盘构思，而且他的审美眼光总能与她严丝合缝地契合，恰如其分地烘托出她想要的意境效果。尽管这一切令她心里暗暗惊奇，她面上却丝毫不露声色。到了八点钟，她停手说道：“今天就先到这儿吧。咱们开了个好头——比我原先指望的还要顺利得多。不过话说回来，弗利特先生，既然你是个如此绝不妥协的民主派，怎么偏偏肯容许一位年轻小姐这样对你颐指气使、呼来喝去呢？”

“我绝无意阿谀奉承，”他脸颊微红地辩解道，“手握权柄之人，理当效法全能的上帝来行使权柄——温和，且体恤人心。”

这回轮到她双颊飞红了，她接口道：“哦，我明白了，原来前面那句恭维，不过是给后面紧跟着的这番小小布道裹上的一层糖衣罢了。”

“我可没有您夸赞我的那等外交手腕，”丹尼斯坦率真诚地直视着她的双眼说道，“我不过是把心头闪过的一个念头照直说出来罢了。”

不知怎的，她一走，仿佛连整间屋子里的光亮也一并被她带走了。墙上的画作霎时间显得平庸乏味，四周的一切也变得索然无奇。这可不是什么艺术美学上的效果，教他自己也琢磨不透。他不由轻轻叹了口气，却连自己为何叹息也说不上来。

然而白日里繁杂的店务很快排山倒海般涌了上来，没多久他便一头扎进忙碌之中，再无暇旁顾。

那天晚上，布鲁德先生对他的素描习作大加赞赏，令丹尼斯精神大振。

“论起你从前得到的条件，再加上眼下能挤出来这么点儿工夫，这些画已经相当不赖啦。

===Original===

You haf fallen into de natural faults of dose who work alone, but we can soon cure dese. Now here is some vork dat I vant you to do under my eye, and dat study on outlining you can take home. Moreover, I can give you some lessons in outlining from my own picture;” and Mr. Bruder showed him what he had done.
Dennis saw in the clear, vigorous profile the artist’s thought, and congratulated himself that his teacher was a master in his profession.
For two hours they worked and talked, and Dennis felt that every such lesson would be a long step forward.
Poor Bruder looked more and more like himself every day, but God only knew how he had to struggle.
“I don’t know how him vill end,” he said. “I pray nearly every minute, but sometimes I feel dat I must drink even do’ I die dat moment.”
It was disease as well as appetite that he was fighting, for appetite indulged beyond a certain point becomes disease.
His wife’s face was different also﻿—the sharp look of misery fading out of it. Dennis noticed the changes, and thought to himself, while walking home: “After all, the highest art is to bring out on the living face all we can of God’s lost image. How beautiful the changes in these two poor people’s faces! and the best part of it is, that they are the reflex of changes going on in the soul, the imperishable part.”
Then, in quick and natural transition, his mind reverted to Christine Ludolph; and the thought of her face, which God had fashioned so fair, but which was already sadly marred by sin, becoming fixed and rigid in pride and selfishness, was as painful as if, according to an old legend, her lithe, active form should gradually turn to stone. But if the reverse could ever be true﻿—if the beautifying Christian graces could dwell within her soul and light up her face﻿—as lamps illumining some rare and quaint transparency, the resulting loveliness would realize the artist’s fondest ideal.
Musing thus, what wonder that he vowed then and there, under the starlight, to pray and work for her till the new life should illumine her heart. Little dreamed Christine, as she slept that night, that the first link of a chain which might bind her to heaven had been forged.
The dawn was late and lowering on the following morning. Great masses of clouds swept across the sky, and soon the rain was falling in gusty torrents.

师徒俩一边切磋画艺一边畅谈，转眼便是两个钟头，丹尼斯只觉每一回这样的指点，都让自己向前迈出了一大步。

可怜的布鲁德一天天恢复了往日那副坦荡正直的本色，然而只有上帝才知道他暗地里经受着何等艰难的煎熬与搏斗。

“我真不晓得自己最后会落得个啥下场，”他苦笑着说，“我几乎每一分钟都在暗自祈祷，可有时候心里那股馋虫翻涌上来，觉着哪怕一口喝下去立时毙命，我也非灌上一杯不可！”

他所对抗的早已不只是口腹之欲，更是一场沉疴痼疾——因为欲望一旦纵容过了某条界线，便会沦为噬人的病症。

他妻子的面容也悄然变了样——往日那副愁苦凄厉、尖刻消瘦的神色正一点点从她脸上褪去。丹尼斯敏锐地察觉到了这些变化，走回家的路上不禁暗自思忖：“说到底，世间最高明的艺术，莫过于在一张张活生生的面孔上，尽可能地重现上帝失落已久的荣光与形象。这两个可怜人脸上绽放出的变化该有多美啊！而最妙的莫过于，那正是他们灵魂深处——那永不朽坏的部分——正在悄然蜕变的外在映照。”

紧接着，他的思绪极其自然地一转，又落回到了克里斯蒂娜·卢多尔夫身上；一想到她那张本由上帝雕琢得如此绝美、如今却已被罪孽可悲地玷污损毁的脸庞，倘若日后在傲慢与自私中彻底僵化定型，那该是何等令人痛心——简直不亚于古老传说里那般，教她那柔韧鲜活的躯体一点点化作冰冷顽石。可倘若恰恰相反呢？倘若基督徒那些美化灵魂的恩典美德能够进驻她的心房，点亮她的面容——宛如明灯照透一盏稀世奇巧的透光画灯——那么由此绽放出的绝美风华，必将圆满实现艺术家梦寐以求的最高理想。

想到此处，也难怪他在漫天星斗之下当即立下宏愿：定要为她祈祷、为她尽心尽力，直到那崭新的生命之光照亮她的心扉。那一夜，克里斯蒂娜在沉沉梦乡之中做梦也想不到，一根或许有朝一日会将她系往天国的链条，已经悄然锻造出了第一环。

次日黎明来得迟缓而阴沉。大团大团乌云席卷过天际，很快，狂风便裹挟着瓢泼大雨倾盆而下。

===Original===

Dennis rose and hastened through his duties as before, and was ready at the hour appointed, but had little hope of seeing Miss Ludolph. Still he opened the door and looked up the street. To his surprise he saw her coming, attended by her father’s valet. Only part of her glowing face was visible, for she was encased from head to foot in a light and delicate suit of rubber.
Dennis opened the door, and she stepped quickly in, scattering spray on every side like a sea-nymph. The young man looked at her with open-eyed admiration and surprise, which both amused and pleased her.
“True enough,” she thought, “his face is like a signboard.”
She seemed to him, as she threw off her wet coverings, like an exquisite flower, that, lifted by the breeze after a storm, scatters the burdensome raindrops on every side and stands up more beautiful and blooming than ever.
“You were not expecting me, I imagine,” she said.
“Well, I must admit I scarcely did, and yet I could not help looking for you.”
“Isn’t that a distinction without a difference?” she asked, with a pleasant smile, for she was gratified at not finding the store closed and dark.
“I am very glad you have come,” he replied, flushing slightly with pleasure, “for it would have been a long, dreary morning if you had not.”
Dennis thought he referred to the lack of occupation. He did not know, nor did she notice, that he meant the lack of herself.
“Well,” said she, “I am glad you like the work, for you destined to have enough of it.”

===Chinese===

丹尼斯照旧早早起身，麻利地赶在约定时刻前料理完了所有店务；虽说心里几乎不敢指望卢多尔夫小姐会冒雨前来，他还是推开店门，朝长街那头张望了一眼。令他喜出望外的是，他竟然看见她正在父亲贴身男仆的护送下款款走来。她那张容光焕发的脸庞只露出了半张，因为她从头到脚严严实实地裹在一套轻盈精致的橡胶雨衣里。

丹尼斯连忙拉开门扉，她轻快地跨步而入，周身抖落四溅的水花，活像一位凌波踏浪而来的海神仙女。年轻人睁大双眼，带着毫不掩饰的惊艳与诧异望着她，那副神情既教她觉得好笑，又令她芳心窃喜。

“果真不错，”她暗想，“他那张脸简直就像一块写满心思的招牌。”

在她抖落身上湿漉漉雨具的那一刹那，在他眼里她恰似一朵经过暴风雨洗礼后被微风轻轻托起的绝世名花，抖落了花瓣上沉甸甸的雨珠，比往日更加亭亭玉立、娇艳盛放。

“我猜你原本没指望我会来吧？”她开口问道。

“唔，我得老实承认，确实几乎不敢指望，可我还是忍不住一直盼着您来。”

“这岂不是换汤不换药、毫无分别的废话吗？”她带着一抹愉快的微笑反问道，因为进门时看见画店并没有因为下雨而黑灯闭户，她心里着实颇为受用。

“我太高兴您来了，”他微微涨红了脸，掩不住喜悦地答道，“要是您不来，这整个上午怕是又漫长又沉闷了。”

丹尼斯原以为自己是在感叹若不来便无活可干；他自己浑然不觉，而她也没有留神，他心里真正说的其实是——少了她便索然无味。

“嗯，”她说道，“我很高兴你这么喜欢这份差事，因为你注定少不了有得干呢。”

## VIII Yahcob Bunk / 第八章 亚科布·邦克
===Original===

Before retiring, Dennis as usual took his Bible from his trunk to read a chapter. He was now in a very different mood from that of a few hours ago. The suggestion of his barroom acquaintance was a light upon his way. And with one of Dennis’s age and temperament, even a small hope is potent. He was eager for the coming day, in order to try the experiment of wringing bread and opportunity for further search out of the wintry snows.
But that which had done him the most good﻿—more than he realized﻿—was the kindness he had received, rough though it was﻿—the sympathy and companionship of another human being; for if he had been cast away on a desert island he could not have been more isolated than in the great city, with its indifferent multitudes.
Moreover the generous supper was not without its decided influence; and with it he had drunk a cup of good coffee, that nectar of the gods, whose subtle, delicate influence is felt in body and brain, in every fibre of the nature not deadened and blunted by stronger and coarser stimulants. He who leaves out physical causes in accounting for mental and moral states, will usually come wide of the mark. But while giving the influences above referred to their due force, so far from ignoring, we would acknowledge with emphasis, the chief cause of man’s ability to receive and appreciate all the highest phases of truth and good, namely, God’s help asked for and given. Prayer was a habit with Dennis. He asked God with childlike faith for the bestowment of every Christian grace, and those who knew him best saw that he had no reason to complain that his prayers were unanswered.
But now, at a time when he would most appreciate it, God was about to reveal to him a truth that would be a rich source of help and comfort through life, and a sudden burst of sunshine upon his dark way at the present hour. He was to be shown how he might look to heaven for help and guidance in respect to his present and earthly interests, as truly as in his spiritual life.
As he opened his Bible his eyes caught the words of our Lord﻿—“Launch out into the deep and let down your nets for a draught.”
Then Peter’s answer﻿—“Master, we have toiled all the night and have taken nothing: nevertheless, at Thy word I will let down the net.”
The result﻿—“They enclosed a great multitude of fishes.”
With these words light broke in upon his mind.

===Chinese===

睡前，丹尼斯照例从行李箱里取出《圣经》，准备读上一章。此刻他的心境，已与短短几个钟头前判若云泥。酒馆里那位萍水相逢的熟人随口出的主意，恰似黑夜旅途上骤然亮起的一盏明灯。对于丹尼斯这般年纪与性情的人来说，哪怕微弱的一点盼头，也蕴含着无穷的力量。他满心迫切地盼着天亮，好去试试这个法子——从严冬积雪里硬生生铲出口粮来，也铲出继续四处求职的生机。

然而，真正让他受益最深、甚至连他自己都未曾完全意识到的，其实是他所领受的那份情义——虽说粗糙率直，却真切地流露出另一个活生生的人给予他的同情与陪伴；毕竟，在这座人潮熙攘却冷漠无情的大都市里，他若真是流落荒岛，孤立无援的凄凉也不过如此。

此外，那顿丰盛热乎的晚饭也绝非毫无功劳；伴着饭菜，他还喝下了一大杯香浓的好咖啡——那堪比众神琼浆玉液的饮品，其微妙醇和的效力缓缓渗入四肢百骸、头脑神经，滋润着天性中每一根尚未被更烈、更粗鄙的刺激物麻痹钝化的纤敏神经。凡是在剖析人的精神与道德状态时把肉体生理缘由撇开不谈的人，往往难免失之毫厘、谬以千里。然而在如实承认上述外在助缘的应有之力时，我们非但不敢忽略，反倒更要着重申明人类之所以能够领受并体悟一切最高境界真理与良善的根本动因——那便是向神祈求、并蒙神垂允而赐下的助佑。祈祷原是丹尼斯自幼养成的习惯。他怀着赤子般的单纯信心，向上帝祈求赐予每一种基督徒的美德恩典；而凡是最了解他的人，都看得出他毫无理由抱怨自己的祷告落了空。

然而此刻，恰恰在他最能体味其宝贵之处的时候，上帝正要向他揭示一条真理——一条将成为他毕生助力与慰藉的丰沛源泉、并在眼下这至暗时刻骤然洒满他前路的灿烂阳光。他即将领悟到：人在眼下尘世的生计利益上，也同样可以如同在属灵生命上一样，仰望上苍的帮助与指引。

翻开《圣经》，他的目光恰巧落在主耶稣的那句圣言上——“把船开到水深之处，下网打鱼。”

紧接着便是彼得的回答——“夫子，我们整夜劳力，并没有打着什么；但依从你的话，我就下网。”

而结局则是——“他们就圈住许多鱼。”

读到这几句经文，一道豁然开朗的亮光骤然照进了他的心田。

“If our Lord,” he mused, “helped His first disciples catch fish, why should He not help me find a good place?” Then unbelief suggested, “It was not for the sake of the fish; they were only means to a higher end.”
But Dennis, who had plenty of good commonsense, at once answered this objection: “Neither do I want position and money for low, selfish purposes. My ends are the best and purest, for I am seeking my own honest living and the support of my mother and sisters﻿—the very imperative duties that God is now imposing on me. Would God reveal a duty and no way of performing it?”
Then came the thought: “Have I asked Him to help me? Have I not been seeking in my own wisdom, and trusting in my own strength? and this too when my ignorance of business, the dull season of the year, and everything was against me, when I specially needed help. Little wonder that I have fared as I have.”
Turning the leaves of his Bible rapidly, he began searching for instances of God’s interference in behalf of the temporal interests of His servants﻿—for passages where earthly prosperity was promised or given. After an hour he closed the Bible with a long breath of wonder, and said to himself “Why, God seems to care as much for the well-being and happiness of his children here as He will when He has us all about Him in the home above. I’ve been blind for twenty-one years to one of the grandest truths of this Book.”
Then, as the thought grew upon him, he exclaimed, joyously, “Take heart, Dennis Fleet: God is on your side in the struggle for an honest success in this life as truly as in your fight against sin and the devil.”
It was long before he slept that night, but a truth had been revealed that rested and strengthened him more than the heavy slumbers after the weary days that had preceded.
The dawn of the winter morning was cold and faint when Dennis appeared in the barroom the next day. The jolly-faced Teuton was making the fire, stopping often to blow his cold fingers, and wasting enough good breath to have kindled a furnace. His rubicund visage, surrounded by shaggy hair and beard of yellow, here appeared in the dust and smoke he was making like the sun rising in a fog.
“Hillo!” he said, on seeing Dennis; “vat you oop dis early for? Don’t vant anoder dinner yet, I hope?”

“既然我们的主，”他沉思着，“当年曾帮他的第一批门徒打鱼，又为何不能帮我寻到一份好差事呢？”随即，心头那股不信的念头又冒出来狡辩：“那回打鱼并不是为了鱼本身；鱼群不过是通往更高属灵目的的手段罢了。”

然而极富常理常识的丹尼斯立刻驳倒了这个疑虑：“我求取职位与钱财，难道是为了卑鄙自私的享乐吗？我的目的至纯至正——我要靠双手挣一碗清白干净的饭吃，还要赡养母亲和妹妹们，这正是上帝眼下摆在我肩头、刻不容缓的本分职责。难道上帝会向人指明一项本分，却偏偏不给人一条履行本分的出路吗？”

紧接着，另一个念头跃上心头：“可我曾开口求过他帮我吗？这些天来，我岂不一直都在凭着自己的小聪明四处瞎闯、只仗着自己的气力硬扛吗？偏巧我对商界门道一窍不通，又赶上一年里生意最冷清的淡季，样样境况都在同我作对，分明是我最亟需帮手的时候。怪不得我一路碰壁，落得这般狼狈下场！”

他飞快地翻动着《圣经》书页，开始细细搜寻上帝为他仆人尘世间的生计利益亲自出手相助的先例——寻找那些应许或赐下今生兴旺蒙福的经文。整整一个钟头之后，他长舒一口惊叹的气，合上《圣经》，喃喃自语道：“天哪，看来上帝关切他儿女在今世尘寰的安康与幸福，竟丝毫不亚于将来在天上家园把我们聚拢在他身旁之时！我活了二十一年，竟对这部宝书里最宏伟的真理之一盲目至此！”

随着这个念头在心底愈发清晰炽热，他忍不住欢欣鼓舞地轻呼出来：“振作起来，丹尼斯·弗利特！在今生为挣一份清白前程而拼搏的征途上，上帝同样站在你这一边，正如他在你同罪恶与魔鬼搏斗时站在你身旁一样！”

那一夜，他久久未能入眠，然而一条崭新的真理既已向他敞开，它带给他的安歇与力量，远胜过连日精疲力竭之后那种沉重的昏睡。

次日冬晨，天色微明，寒气袭人，丹尼斯一早便出现在了小酒馆的酒吧间里。那位圆脸快活的德国汉子正蹲在炉子前生火，隔三岔五便停下来对着冻僵的手指头哈气，白白吹费出去的热气足能把一座大熔炉都点着了。他那张红扑扑的大圆脸被一圈蓬乱的黄色须发簇拥着，在自己捅出来的烟雾灰尘里若隐若现，活像一轮正从浓雾里升起的红日。

“哟！”他一看见丹尼斯便咧嘴招呼道，“这么大清早的，你起这么早干啥呀？但愿你可不是这么快又来讨一顿正餐吃吧？”

“I will take that in good time,” said Dennis; “and shall want a bigger one than that which so astonished you at first.”
“Oh, my eyes!” said the German; “den I go and tell de cook to pegin to get him right avay.”
Laughing good-naturedly, Dennis went to the door and looked out. On sidewalk and street the snow lay six or eight inches deep, untrodden, white and spotless, even in the heart of the great city. “How different this snow will look by night,” thought he; “how soiled and black! Perhaps very many come to this city in the morning of life like this snow, pure and unstained; but after being here awhile they become like this snow when it has been tossed about and trodden under every careless foot. God grant that, however poor and unsuccessful I may remain, such pollution may never be my fate.”
But feeling that he had no time for moralizing if he would secure bread for the coming day of rest, he turned and said to the factotum of the barroom, “How much will you give to have the snow cleared off the sidewalk in front of your house?”
“Zwei shillen.”
“Then I will earn my breakfast before I eat it, if you will lend me a shovel.”
“I dought you vas a shentlemans,” said the German, staring at him.
“So I am; just the shentlemans that will clean off your sidewalk for zwei shillen, if you will let him.”
“You vant to do him for exercise?”
“No; for zwei shillings.”
“I dought you vas a shentlemans,” said the man, still staring in stolid wonder at Dennis.
“Didn’t you ever know of a gentleman who came from Germany to this country and was glad to do anything for an honest living?”
“Often and often I haf. You see von here,” said the man, with a grin. “Well, I am just that kind of a gentleman. Now if you will lend me a shovel I will clean off your sidewalk for two shillings, and be a great deal more thankful than if you had given me the money for nothing.”
“Little fear of dot,” said the man, with another grin. “Vel, you are der queerest Yankee in Chicago, you are; I dink you are ’bout haf Sherman. 丹尼斯爽朗地笑了几声，走到门口往外探望。门外人行道与大街上积雪足有六七八寸厚，尚未有人踩踏，哪怕置身于这座大都会的心腹闹市之中，依然洁白无瑕、一尘不染。“等到了晚上，这片白雪该变成什么模样呢，”他暗自思忖，“该变得多么肮脏乌黑啊！兴许许许多多初来乍到这座城市的人，在人生的清晨也像这新雪一般纯洁无瑕；可在这里混久了，便也变得如同这雪一般，被千万人漫不经心地踩在脚底、践踏得面目全非。求上帝垂怜，无论我日后怎么穷困潦倒、一事无成，千万别叫我落得那样浑身污浊的下场。”

“难道你从前没听说过，有些从德国漂洋过海到这儿来的绅士，为了靠本事挣口清白饭吃，什么活儿都乐意干吗？”

“听过，听过太多次啦！你眼前不就站着一个嘛，”那汉子咧开大嘴笑道，“好吧，我这人就是那一号绅士。这会儿你只要借我一把铁锹，我就替你把人行道上的雪铲干净，赚那两先令，而且比你白送我钱还要感激十分。”

“那倒不怕你不乐意，”汉子又咧嘴一笑，“咳，你小子可真是芝加哥城里头一号古怪的美国佬！依我看，你骨子里倒有一半像咱们德国人。我跟你说吧——喂，你叫啥名字来着？——只要你把那段人行道铲得干干净净，今儿个早饭和午饭随你放开肚皮吃个够，一分钱也不用付！哪怕把厨子累得一整天守在灶台边做饭我也不在乎！我就喜欢你这股——你们美国人咋叫来着？——那股子硬气劲儿！”

“一言为定！”丹尼斯应声道，“今天我要是能多谈成几桩这样的买卖，可就发财喽！”

“这话你倒真说对了。

===Original===

I vill go into der market and see if dere’s enough for me to keep my bart of der bargain goot.”
For half an hour Dennis worked away lustily, and then called his taskmaster and said, “Will you accept the job?”
Surveying with surprise the large space cleared, and looking in vain for reason to find fault, he said: “I say nothin’ agin him. I hope you vill eat your dinner as quick. Now come in to your preakfast.”
He pretended to be perfectly aghast at Dennis’s onslaught on the buckwheat cakes, and rolled up his eyes despairingly as each new plate was emptied.
Having finished, Dennis gave him a nod, and said, “Wait till dinnertime.”
“Ah! dere vill be von famine,” said the German, in a tone of anguish, wringing his hands.
Having procured the needful implement, Dennis started out, and, though there was considerable competition, found plenty to do, and shovelled away with little cessation till one o’clock. Then, counting his gains, he found that he had paid for his shovel, secured breakfast and dinner, and had a balance on hand of two dollars and fifty cents, and he had nearly half a day yet before him. He felt rich﻿—nay, more than that, he felt like a man who, sinking in a shoreless ocean, suddenly catches a plank that bears him up until land appears in the distance.
“This is what comes of asking God to help a fellow,” said he to himself. “Strange, too, that He should answer my prayer in part before I asked, by causing that queer jumble of good and evil, Bill Cronk, to suggest to me this way of turning an honest penny. I wish Bill was as good a friend to himself as he is to others. I fear that he will go to the dogs. Bless me! the gnawings of hunger are bad enough, but what must be those of conscience? I think I can astonish my German friend today as never before;” and, shouldering his shovel, he walked back to dinner, feeling like a prince bearing aloft the insignia of his power.
When he entered the bar and lunch room, he saw that something was wrong. The landlord met him, instead of his jolly, satirical friend.
Now the owner of the place was a wizen-faced, dried-up old anatomy, who seemed utterly exhaling away in tobacco smoke, while his assistant was becoming spherical under the expansive power of lager. It was his custom to sit up and smoke most of the night, and therefore he was down late in the morning.

===Chinese===

我这就赶紧上菜市场采买去，瞧瞧买不买得齐够我兑现这半边买卖的吃食！”

丹尼斯铆足气力呼呼地干了半个钟头，随后唤来他的雇主，问道：“这活儿您还满意吗？”

汉子惊讶地打量着门前铲得干干净净的一大片空地，左右找不出一丁点儿可挑剔的毛病，只得连声道：“没半句话可挑的！但愿你等会儿吃午饭也能有这么麻利。行了，快进来吃你的早饭吧。”

看着丹尼斯风卷残云般扫荡那一摞荞麦煎饼的架势，汉子故意做出一副惊骇欲绝的滑稽模样，每空掉一只盘子，他便绝望地把眼珠子往上一翻。

吃完早饭，丹尼斯冲他点点头，抛下一句：“等着晌午的午饭吧。”

“哎呀！咱们这儿怕是要闹饥荒喽！”德国汉子双手拧在一起，装出一副惨痛哀嚎的腔调叫苦道。

买好趁手的铁锹后，丹尼斯便上街揽活去了；虽说街上抢着扫雪的竞争者着实不少，可活计依然多得干不完，他一口气几乎没歇脚地一直铲到下午一点钟。随后坐下来清点进项，除去买铁锹的本钱，不仅挣出了早饭和午饭，手头竟还净余出两美元五十美分，更何况面前还有将近半天工夫呢！他只觉得自己富得流油——不，比那还要振奋得多：他觉得自己就像一个在无边大洋里快要沉没的落水者，突然摸到了一块木板，稳稳托着他一路浮向远方渐渐显露的陆地。

“这便是开口求上帝帮忙的福报啊，”他心里暗自感叹，“也真是奇妙，我还没来得及开口求告呢，他便早已先替我应允了一半——竟借着比尔·克朗克那个善恶混杂的怪人，点拨了我这条挣清白钱的门路。真盼望比尔待自己也能像待旁人那样厚道才好，只怕他早晚要毁在自己手里。老天保佑！饿肚子的滋味固然难熬，可良心受到啃噬的煎熬又该是何等痛苦？今天晌午，我倒要让那位德国朋友见识见识什么叫前所未有的大吃大喝！”说着，他肩扛铁锹大步往回走去吃午饭，神气活现得宛如一位高举权杖凯旋而归的王子。

谁知一踏进酒吧兼餐馆的大门，他便觉出气氛有些不对劲。迎面走出来的不是他那位快活爱打趣的德国朋友，而是店东本人。

原来这间小店的老板是个干瘪枯瘦、满脸皱纹的小老头，整个人仿佛都快化作一缕烟丝随手里的烟斗飘散了；而他的伙计却在淡啤酒的滋润下日渐发福、圆滚如球。老头向来习惯彻夜不睡地抽大烟斗，因此上午总是很晚才下楼来。

===Original===

When he appeared his assistant told him of the bargain he had made with Dennis as a good joke. But old Hans hadn’t any faculty for jokes. Dollars and cents and his big meerschaum made up the two elements of his life. The thought of losing *zwei* shillings or *zwei* cents by Dennis, or anyone else, caused him anguish, and instead of laughing, his fun-loving assistant was aghast at seeing him fall into a passion.
“You be von big fule. Vat for we keep mens here who haf no money? You should gleared him off, instead of making pargains for him to eat us out of der house.”
“We haf his trunk,” said Jacob, for that was his name.
“Nothin’ in it,” growled Hans, yet somewhat mollified by this fact. When Dennis appeared, he put the case without any circumlocution: “I makes my livin’ by keepin’ dis house. I can no make my livin’ unless efrypodies bays me. I haf reason to dink dot you haf no moneys. Vat ish de druf? ’Gause if you haf none, you can no longer stay here.”
“Have I not paid for everything I have had so far?” said Dennis.
“Dot is not der question. Haf you got any moneys?”
“What is your bill in advance up to Monday morning?”
“Zwei dollar and a quarter, if you dake preakfast.”
“Deduct breakfast and dinner today for clearing off the sidewalk.”
“Dot ish too much; you did it in half-hour.”
“Well, it would have taken you three. But a bargain is a bargain, the world over. Did not you promise it?”﻿—to Jacob.
“Yah! und you shall haf him, too, if I be der loser. Yahcob Bunk ish not der man to go pack on his vort.”
“Vel, den,” said old Hans, “von dollar sheventy-five to Monday morning.”
“There’s the money; now let me have my dinner, for I am in a hurry.”
At the sight of money Hans at once became the most obsequious of hosts, and so would remain while it lasted. But Dennis saw that the moment it was gone his purchased courtesy would change, and he trembled at his narrow escape from being thrust out into the wintry streets, friendless, penniless, to beg or starve﻿—equally hard alternatives to his mind.
“Come, Yahcob, thou snail, give der shentlemans his dinner,” said Hans.
Jacob, who had been looking on with heavy, stolid face, now brightened up on seeing that all was right, and gave Dennis a double portion of the steaming potpie, and a huge mug of coffee.

===Chinese===

老板刚一下楼露面，伙计便把同丹尼斯做的那笔扫雪换饭的买卖当成一桩趣闻笑话讲给他听。谁料老汉斯（Hans）压根儿半点幽默感也没有。美元美分连同他那只海泡石大烟斗，便是他毕生仅有的两大命根子。一想到因为丹尼斯或者无论什么阿猫阿狗平白赔掉两先令甚至两美分，简直要了他的老命；非但没笑，他那位爱凑趣的伙计反倒目瞪口呆地看着老板当场暴跳如雷。

“你个蠢透顶的大傻瓜！咱们店里凭啥收留半文钱没有的穷光蛋？你早该把他轰出门去，倒好，反倒跟他定下什么劳什子契约，教他把咱们一家子吃穷吃垮不成！”

“咱们屋里还扣着他的大行李箱呢。”雅各布（Jacob）辩解道——原来这便是那德国伙计的名字。

“里头准是空空如也！”汉斯咆哮着，不过听到这话火气倒也稍微平息了些。等丹尼斯一进门，老头二话不说，直截了当地摊牌：“我开这座店是靠这个糊口的。人人都付钱，我才能糊得了口。我有充分的理由怀疑你根本没钱。说实话吧，到底有没有？因为要是没钱，你就别想再在这儿住下去了！”

“到目前为止，我吃住的每一笔账难道不是当场付清的吗？”丹尼斯反问道。

“眼下问的不是那个。你兜里到底还有没有钱？”

“预付到星期一早上的食宿费总共是多少？”

“要是算上明早的早饭，两美元两毛五。”

“扣除今天扫人行道顶掉的早饭和午饭钱。”

“那算得太高了；你拢共只干了半个钟头！”

“可换作您自己扫，三个钟头也未必扫得完。再者说，普天之下，买卖一言既出、驷马难追。难道不是你亲口答应的吗？”——丹尼斯转向雅各布问道。

“没错！就算我自己倒贴赔本，这笔账也算你的！亚科布·邦克（Yahcob Bunk）可不是那种说话不算数、朝令夕改的小人！”

“那好吧，”老汉斯算计了一下，改口道，“预付到星期一早上，一美元七毛五。”

“钱在这里；现在快把我的午饭端来，我赶时间呢。”

一见着白花花的银钱，老汉斯立时变作了全天下最卑躬屈膝、殷勤备至的店主——只要客人口袋里还有钱，他便永远是这副嘴脸。可丹尼斯心里雪亮，一旦兜里最后一枚铜板花光，这买来的客气便会瞬间翻脸；一想到方才差一点就要身无分文、举目无亲地被撵到冰天雪地的大街上，要么沿街乞讨、要么活活饿死——在他看来，这两条路同样教人生不如死——他至今仍心有余悸、浑身微颤。

“快着点儿，亚科布，你这只大蜗牛，赶紧给这位体面绅士端午饭去！”汉斯吆喝道。

雅各布方才一直绷着那张沉闷木然的大圆脸在一旁观望，这会儿见一切稳妥过关，眉开眼笑地立刻端来了一大份双人份量的热腾腾炖肉派，外加一只海碗般巨大的热咖啡。

===Original===

When Dennis had finished these and crowned his repast with a big dumpling, Jacob came to him with a face as long and serious as his harvest moon of a visage could be made, and said: “Dere ish nodding more in Chicago; you haf gleaned it out. Ve must vait dill der evenin’ drain gomes pefore ve haf supper.”
“That will be time enough for me,” said Dennis, laughing﻿—for he could laugh today at little things﻿—and started off again with his shovel.

===Chinese===

丹尼斯风卷残云般吃完这些，最后又塞下一只硕大的面团子收尾；这时雅各布迈着沉重的步子走过来，把他那张圆得像中秋满月似的大脸尽力拉得又长又严肃，一本正经地说道：“全芝加哥城里已经没啥吃的剩下来啦；全叫你一个人扫荡精光啦。咱们只能干等着傍晚那趟火车把粮食运来，才有晚饭吃喽！”

“那对我来说也尽够准时的了，”丹尼斯大笑着答道——因为今天这点小玩笑已足够令他开怀大笑——说完，他又扛起铁锹，意气风发地出门干活去了。
